/-!
# The closed geodesics of de Sitter space (Secs. II and IV.D)

Sec. IV.D finds the radius of the largest ring from the geometry of the solution without a mass.
By the last sentence of Postulate 2 a largest ring is a closed geodesic of space.  Without a mass
the geometry of space is the same at every slot (`Solution.geometry_same`, from the symmetry of
space, `Symmetry.lawAt_same`, the state the same at every crossing, and the thesis applied to the
geometry, `hgeom`), and `Space.lean` derives from it, with the rings, that the solution is de Sitter
space.  This file proves what the paper uses of the geometry of de Sitter space, that its closed
spacelike geodesics have one length and are great circles of its space at an instant.

The spacetimes here are quadrics of a space `T × E` of times `T` and places `E`, with the form
`−⟪t, t'⟫ + ⟪x, x'⟫` (`form`).  De Sitter space of radius `ρ` is `form X X = ρ²` with one time
(`T = ℝ`, `E = ℝ⁴`).  A geodesic of a quadric is a curve on it whose acceleration is normal to it, a
multiple of its position (`IsGeodesic`) [B. O'Neill, *Semi-Riemannian Geometry* (1983), Ch. 4].

* **De Sitter space** (`IsGeodesic.circle`, `IsGeodesic.hasLength`).  A spacelike geodesic keeps
  its speed, and its acceleration is `−ω²` times its position, so it runs on a circle of radius `ρ`
  in the plane of its starting point and its velocity, once in each period `2π/ω`: every closed
  spacelike geodesic has the length `2πρ`.
* **The hyperbola** (`hypCurve`, `hypCurve_geodesic`).  The curve `t ↦ (cosh t · a, sinh t · b)`
  with `‖a‖ = ‖b‖ = ℓ` is a geodesic of the quadric `form X X = −ℓ²`.  With one time the upper
  sheet of that quadric is hyperbolic space, and `Space.hyperbolic_space_no_rings` takes in this
  form the geodesics from its lowest point.
* **The space at an instant** (`InSpace`, `IsGeodesic.greatCircle`, `Crossing.Drawing.ofRings`).
  The section of de Sitter space by the hyperplane of time zero, the space at an instant of an
  observer at rest, is the sphere of radius `ρ` of `E`, a three-sphere.  A closed geodesic lying in
  it is a great circle `u a + v b`, `u² + v² = 1`, with `a ⊥ b` and `‖a‖ = ‖b‖ = ρ`.  So rings that
  are closed geodesics of space are drawn as great circles, which the count of a sphere's strings
  uses (`Bridge.sphere_strings_of_rings`).

`circleCurve` shows that rings exist in de Sitter space.  That a largest ring is a closed geodesic of space, made of its
cells as segments of length `ℓ_c`, is the last sentence of Postulate 2; here it enters as a hypothesis, as a postulate does (the rings of
`Bridge.sphere_strings_of_rings`).  It is also part of the admissible drawings (`Symmetry.admissible`) of the rings of the space at an
instant (`Space.SliceIsQubits`).
-/

open RealInnerProductSpace

namespace Geodesic

section Inner

variable {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
        LemmaGeodesic.hasDerivAt_inner'line 55
        /-- The derivative of the inner product of two curves. -/
lemma hasDerivAt_inner' {f g : ℝ → V} {f' g' : V} {t : ℝ} (hf : HasDerivAt f f' t)
    (hg : HasDerivAt g g' t) :
    HasDerivAt (fun u => ⟪f u, g u⟫) (⟪f t, g'⟫ + ⟪f', g t⟫) t := by
  have h := ((isBoundedBilinearMap_inner (𝕜 := ℝ) (E := V)).hasFDerivAt (f t, g t)).comp t
    (hf.hasFDerivAt.prodMk hg.hasFDerivAt)
  convert h.hasDerivAt using 1
  · rfl
  rw [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.prod_apply,

    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] where

  /-- its velocity -/
  vel : ℝ → T × E
  /-- its acceleration -/
  acc : ℝ → T × E
  hpos1 : ∀ t, HasDerivAt (fun u => (pos u).1) (vel t).1 t
  hpos2 : ∀ t, HasDerivAt (fun u => (pos u).2) (vel t).2 t
  hvel1 : ∀ t, HasDerivAt (fun u => (vel u).1) (acc t).1 t
  hvel2 : ∀ t, HasDerivAt (fun u => (vel u).2) (acc t).2 t

        /-- **A geodesic of the quadric** `form X X = k` of `T × E`, `k ≠ 0`: a curve on the quadric
whose acceleration is a multiple of its position.  The position is the normal of the quadric for
the form, so the acceleration is normal to the quadric: the curve is a geodesic of the quadric with
the metric the form induces [B. O'Neill, *Semi-Riemannian Geometry* (1983), Ch. 4], run at a
constant speed (`IsGeodesic.speed_const`).  For `k = 0` the quadric is the null cone, whose metric
is degenerate.  No theorem derives anything from that case; `Bridge.sphere_strings_deSitter` takes
`k = 3/Λ` for every real `Λ`, so `Λ = 0` gives `k = 0` in Lean, and it excludes that case, as it
excludes `Λ < 0`, since a spacelike ring needs `k > 0`. -/
def IsGeodesic (k : ℝ) (γ : Curve T E) : Prop :=
  (∀ t, form (γ.pos t) (γ.pos t) = k) ∧ ∀ t, ∃ c : ℝ, γ.acc t = c • γ.pos t

        /-- **A spacelike curve**: its velocity has positive square in the form. -/
def IsSpacelike (γ : Curve T E) : Prop := ∀ t, 0 < form (γ.vel t) (γ.vel t)
        DefinitionGeodesic.HasLengthline 145
        /-- **A closed spacelike curve of constant speed and length `len`**, traversed once: its position
is periodic, with a least period `P > 0`, and its speed `√(form vel vel)` covers `len` in that
period at every point.  The theorems use it for spacelike curves only (`IsSpacelike`); for a
timelike or null curve the square root is zero. -/

  ∃ P : ℝ, 0 < P ∧ Function.Periodic γ.pos P ∧
    (∀ P' : ℝ, 0 < P' → Function.Periodic γ.pos P' → P ≤ P') ∧
    ∀ t, Real.sqrt (form (γ.vel t) (γ.vel t)) * P = len

lemma harmonic_zero {ω : ℝ} {y y' y'' : ℝ → V} (hy : ∀ t, HasDerivAt y (y' t) t)

    (h0' : y' 0 = 0) (t : ℝ) : y t = 0 := by

    have d := (hasDerivAt_inner' (hy' u) (hy' u)).add
      ((hasDerivAt_inner' (hy u) (hy u)).const_mul (ω ^ 2))
    convert d using 1
    rw [h u, real_inner_smul_right, real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_comm (y u) (y' u)]
    ring

    have := is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero (fun u => (hE u).differentiableAt)
      (fun u => (hE u).deriv) u 0

    simp

    have h1 := real_inner_self_nonneg (x := y' u)
    have h2 := mul_nonneg (sq_nonneg ω) (real_inner_self_nonneg (x := y u))
    have : ⟪y' u, y' u⟫ = 0 := by linarith [hc u]
    exact inner_self_eq_zero.1 this
  have := is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero (fun u => (hy u).differentiableAt)
    (fun u => by rw [(hy u).deriv, hy'0 u]) t 0
  rw [this, h0]

        /-- **The solutions of `z'' = −ω²z`**: `z t = cos(ωt) z(0) + sin(ωt) z'(0)/ω`. -/
lemma harmonic_eq {ω : ℝ} (hω : ω ≠ 0) {z z' z'' : ℝ → V} (hz : ∀ t, HasDerivAt z (z' t) t)

    simpa using (hasDerivAt_id u).const_mul ω

    ((hl u).cos.smul_const (z 0)).add ((hl u).sin.smul_const (ω⁻¹ • z' 0))
  have hc' : ∀ u, HasDerivAt
      (fun u => (-Real.sin (ω * u) * ω) • z 0 + (Real.cos (ω * u) * ω) • (ω⁻¹ • z' 0))
      ((-(Real.cos (ω * u) * ω) * ω) • z 0 + (-Real.sin (ω * u) * ω * ω) • (ω⁻¹ • z' 0)) u :=
    fun u => by
      have d1 : HasDerivAt (fun u => -Real.sin (ω * u) * ω) (-(Real.cos (ω * u) * ω) * ω) u :=
        (hl u).sin.neg.mul_const ω
      have d2 : HasDerivAt (fun u => Real.cos (ω * u) * ω) (-Real.sin (ω * u) * ω * ω) u :=

    (y := fun u => z u - (Real.cos (ω * u) • z 0 + Real.sin (ω * u) • (ω⁻¹ • z' 0)))

      rw [h u]
      module)

end Harmonic

theorem IsGeodesic.acc_eq (h : IsGeodesic k γ) (hk : k ≠ 0) (t : ℝ) :

        /-- **A spacelike geodesic of a quadric `form X X = k > 0` runs on a circle**:

  have hω2 : Real.sqrt (c / k) ^ 2 = c / k := Real.sq_sqrt (div_pos hc hk).le

    rw [h.acc_eq hk.ne' u, hcdef, hω2, neg_div]

theorem HasLength.unique {l₁ l₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : HasLength γ l₁) (h₂ : HasLength γ l₂) : l₁ = l₂ := by
  obtain ⟨P₁, hP₁, hper₁, hleast₁, hlen₁⟩ := h₁
  obtain ⟨P₂, hP₂, hper₂, hleast₂, hlen₂⟩ := h₂

    HasLength γ (2 * Real.pi * Real.sqrt k) := by

  rw [hcdef] at hc
  have hcirc := h.circle hk (hcdef ▸ hsp 0)

  · -- it returns after `2π/ω`

    rw [e, Real.cos_add_two_pi, Real.sin_add_two_pi]

    have hpv : form (γ.vel 0) (γ.pos 0) = 0 := by rw [form_comm]; exact h.form_pos_vel 0

    have hn1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ n := by

    rw [div_le_iff₀ hω, mul_comm P' ω, ← hn]
    nlinarith [Real.pi_pos]

    rw [h.speed_const t, hcdef, hωc]

        /-- for `u² + v² = 1` there is an angle with cosine `u` and sine `v` -/
lemma exists_angle {u v : ℝ} (h : u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 = 1) :
    ∃ θ : ℝ, Real.cos θ = u ∧ Real.sin θ = v := by
  have hu : |u| ≤ 1 := (sq_le_one_iff_abs_le_one u).1 (by nlinarith [sq_nonneg v])
  obtain ⟨hu1, hu2⟩ := abs_le.1 hu
  have hs : Real.sqrt (1 - u ^ 2) = |v| := by
    rw [show 1 - u ^ 2 = v ^ 2 by linarith, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs]
  rcases le_or_gt 0 v with hv | hv
  · refine ⟨Real.arccos u, Real.cos_arccos hu1 hu2, ?_⟩
    rw [Real.sin_arccos, hs, abs_of_nonneg hv]
  · refine ⟨-Real.arccos u, by rw [Real.cos_neg, Real.cos_arccos hu1 hu2], ?_⟩
    rw [Real.sin_neg, Real.sin_arccos, hs, abs_of_neg hv, neg_neg]

        /-- **A great circle run at the angular speed `ω`** in the space at an instant: the curve
`t ↦ (0, cos(ωt) a + sin(ωt) b)` of `ℝ × E`. -/
noncomputable def circleCurve (a b : E) (ω : ℝ) : Curve ℝ E where
  pos t := (0, Real.cos (ω * t) • a + Real.sin (ω * t) • b)
  vel t := (0, (-Real.sin (ω * t) * ω) • a + (Real.cos (ω * t) * ω) • b)
  acc t := (0, (-(Real.cos (ω * t) * ω) * ω) • a + (-Real.sin (ω * t) * ω * ω) • b)
  hpos1 t := hasDerivAt_const t 0
  hpos2 t := ((hasDerivAt_mul_left' ω t).cos.smul_const a).add
    ((hasDerivAt_mul_left' ω t).sin.smul_const b)
  hvel1 t := hasDerivAt_const t 0
  hvel2 t := by
    have d1 : HasDerivAt (fun u => -Real.sin (ω * u) * ω) (-(Real.cos (ω * t) * ω) * ω) t :=
      (hasDerivAt_mul_left' ω t).sin.neg.mul_const ω
    have d2 : HasDerivAt (fun u => Real.cos (ω * u) * ω) (-Real.sin (ω * t) * ω * ω) t :=
      (hasDerivAt_mul_left' ω t).cos.mul_const ω
    exact (d1.smul_const a).add (d2.smul_const b)

  have h := ((Real.hasDerivAt_exp t).add

  have h := ((Real.hasDerivAt_exp t).sub
    ((Real.hasDerivAt_exp (-t)).comp t (hasDerivAt_neg t))).div_const 2
  convert h using 1

        /-- **A hyperbola** `t ↦ (cosh t · a, sinh t · b)` of `T × E`, a geodesic of the quadric

noncomputable def hypCurve (a : T) (b : E) : Curve T E where
  pos t := (Real.cosh t • a, Real.sinh t • b)

        import RegisterGravity.Geodesics

/-!
# One geodesic through two points, as one ring through two cells (Sec. II)

By the last sentence of Postulate 2 every largest ring is a closed geodesic of space, made of its
cells as segments of length `ℓ_c`; the files take it as a hypothesis, as a postulate.  It matches the register on pairs of cells (Sec. II): two
cells that are not opposite lie on exactly one largest ring (Postulate 2, `Horizon.unique_loop`),
and two points of space that are not antipodal lie on exactly one geodesic
(`geodesic_through_two`).  This file proves that fact of geometry in the space at an instant of
de Sitter space of radius `ρ`, the sphere of radius `ρ` of a real inner product space `E`: the
geodesics of that space run on its great circles (`Geodesic.IsGeodesic.greatCircle`), each closed,
of length `2πρ`, and two of its points that are neither equal nor antipodal lie on exactly one
great circle (`greatCircle_through`, `greatCircle_unique`).  That the space at an instant is the
three-sphere itself, and no quotient of it, the rings give (`Space.sphere_rings`).
-/

open RealInnerProductSpace Set

namespace TwoCells

/-! ### Great circles -/

section Circles

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] {a b : E} {ρ : ℝ}

lemma mem_greatCircle_of_eq (hab : ⟪a, b⟫ = 0) (ha : ‖a‖ = ρ) (hb : ‖b‖ = ρ) (hρ : 0 < ρ)

        /-- **Two unit pairs with a vanishing determinant are equal or opposite**: if

lemma det_ne_zero {u₁ v₁ u₂ v₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : u₁ ^ 2 + v₁ ^ 2 = 1) (h₂ : u₂ ^ 2 + v₂ ^ 2 = 1)
    (hne : ¬ (u₂ = u₁ ∧ v₂ = v₁)) (hne' : ¬ (u₂ = -u₁ ∧ v₂ = -v₁)) : u₁ * v₂ - u₂ * v₁ ≠ 0 := by
  intro hD
  have hu : u₂ = (u₁ * u₂ + v₁ * v₂) * u₁ := by linear_combination (-u₂) * h₁ - v₁ * hD
  have hv : v₂ = (u₁ * u₂ + v₁ * v₂) * v₁ := by linear_combination u₁ * hD - v₂ * h₁
  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ : ∃ l, l = u₁ * u₂ + v₁ * v₂ := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hl] at hu hv

    rw [h₂, h₁, mul_one] at e

  have hfac : (l - 1) * (l + 1) = 0 := by linear_combination hl2
  rcases mul_eq_zero.1 hfac with h | h
  · have h1 : l = 1 := by linarith
    exact hne ⟨by rw [hu, h1, one_mul], by rw [hv, h1, one_mul]⟩
  · have h1 : l = -1 := by linarith

        /-- Two points of a great circle that are neither equal nor antipodal, `p = u₁ a + v₁ b` and

        TheoremTwoCells.greatCircle_throughline 75
        /-- **A great circle through two points**: two points of the sphere of radius `ρ` that are neither
equal nor antipodal lie on a great circle, the one through `p` and `ρ w/‖w‖`, with `w` the part of
`q` orthogonal to `p`. -/
theorem greatCircle_through (hρ : 0 < ρ) {p q : E} (hp : ‖p‖ = ρ) (hq : ‖q‖ = ρ) (hqp : q ≠ p)
    (hqp' : q ≠ -p) : ∃ a b : E, ⟪a, b⟫ = 0 ∧ ‖a‖ = ρ ∧ ‖b‖ = ρ ∧
      p ∈ Crossing.greatCircle a b ∧ q ∈ Crossing.greatCircle a b := by
  have hρ2 : ρ ^ 2 ≠ 0 := by positivity
  have hpp : ⟪p, p⟫ = ρ ^ 2 := by rw [real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hp]
  have hqq : ⟪q, q⟫ = ρ ^ 2 := by rw [real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hq]
  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ : ∃ s, s = ⟪p, q⟫ / ρ ^ 2 := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ : ∃ w, w = q - s • p := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have hpw : ⟪p, w⟫ = 0 := by
    rw [hw, inner_sub_right, real_inner_smul_right, hpp, hs, div_mul_cancel₀ _ hρ2, sub_self]
  have hqe : q = s • p + w := by
    rw [hw]
    abel
  have hww : ‖w‖ ^ 2 = ρ ^ 2 - s ^ 2 * ρ ^ 2 := by
    have e := hqq
    rw [hqe, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, norm_add_sq_real, real_inner_smul_left, hpw, norm_smul,
      Real.norm_eq_abs, mul_pow, sq_abs, hp] at e
    linarith
  have hw0 : ‖w‖ ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0
    have hs2 : (s - 1) * (s + 1) = 0 := by
      have e : s ^ 2 * ρ ^ 2 = 1 * ρ ^ 2 := by rw [h0] at hww; linarith
      have := mul_right_cancel₀ hρ2 e
      linear_combination this
    have hwz : w = 0 := norm_eq_zero.1 h0
    rw [hwz, add_zero] at hqe
    rcases mul_eq_zero.1 hs2 with h | h
    · exact hqp (by rw [hqe, show s = 1 by linarith, one_smul])
    · exact hqp' (by rw [hqe, show s = -1 by linarith, neg_one_smul])
  have hwpos : 0 < ‖w‖ := lt_of_le_of_ne (norm_nonneg _) (Ne.symm hw0)
  refine ⟨p, (ρ / ‖w‖) • w, ?_, hp, ?_, ⟨1, 0, by norm_num, by simp⟩, ⟨s, ‖w‖ / ρ, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · rw [real_inner_smul_right, hpw, mul_zero]
  · rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (div_pos hρ hwpos)]
    field_simp
  · rw [div_pow, hww]
    field_simp
    ring
  · rw [smul_smul, show ‖w‖ / ρ * (ρ / ‖w‖) = 1 by field_simp, one_smul, hqe]
        TheoremTwoCells.greatCircle_subsetline 117
        /-- **A great circle through two points that are neither equal nor antipodal lies on any other

of the other.  With the converse, the two great circles are the same (`greatCircle_unique`). -/
theorem greatCircle_subset {a' b' : E} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hab : ⟪a, b⟫ = 0) (ha : ‖a‖ = ρ)
    (hb : ‖b‖ = ρ) (hab' : ⟪a', b'⟫ = 0) (ha' : ‖a'‖ = ρ) (hb' : ‖b'‖ = ρ) {p q : E}
    (hp : p ∈ Crossing.greatCircle a b) (hq : q ∈ Crossing.greatCircle a b)
    (hp' : p ∈ Crossing.greatCircle a' b') (hq' : q ∈ Crossing.greatCircle a' b')
    (hqp : q ≠ p) (hqp' : q ≠ -p) : Crossing.greatCircle a' b' ⊆ Crossing.greatCircle a b := by

  have hxn := norm_of_mem_greatCircle hab' ha' hb' hρ hx
  obtain ⟨u, v, -, rfl⟩ := hx
  obtain ⟨u₁, v₁, h₁, hp1⟩ := hp'
  obtain ⟨u₂, v₂, h₂, hq1⟩ := hq'

  obtain ⟨s₂, t₂, -, hq2⟩ := hq

      (u * v₂ - v * u₂) • p + (v * u₁ - u * v₁) • q := by
    rw [hp1, hq1]

    rw [← e, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ hD, one_smul]

    (s := (u₁ * v₂ - u₂ * v₁)⁻¹ * ((u * v₂ - v * u₂) * s₁ + (v * u₁ - u * v₁) * s₂))
    (t := (u₁ * v₂ - u₂ * v₁)⁻¹ * ((u * v₂ - v * u₂) * t₁ + (v * u₁ - u * v₁) * t₂)) ?_ hxn
  rw [e', hp2, hq2]
  module
        TheoremTwoCells.greatCircle_uniqueline 146
        /-- **Only one great circle passes through two points that are neither equal nor antipodal.** -/
theorem greatCircle_unique {a' b' : E} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hab : ⟪a, b⟫ = 0) (ha : ‖a‖ = ρ)
    (hb : ‖b‖ = ρ) (hab' : ⟪a', b'⟫ = 0) (ha' : ‖a'‖ = ρ) (hb' : ‖b'‖ = ρ) {p q : E}
    (hp : p ∈ Crossing.greatCircle a b) (hq : q ∈ Crossing.greatCircle a b)
    (hp' : p ∈ Crossing.greatCircle a' b') (hq' : q ∈ Crossing.greatCircle a' b')
    (hqp : q ≠ p) (hqp' : q ≠ -p) : Crossing.greatCircle a' b' = Crossing.greatCircle a b :=
  Subset.antisymm (greatCircle_subset hρ hab ha hb hab' ha' hb' hp hq hp' hq' hqp hqp')
    (greatCircle_subset hρ hab' ha' hb' hab ha hb hp' hq' hp hq hqp hqp')
        LemmaTwoCells.circleCurve_rangeline 155
        /-- The path in space of the great circle through `a` and `b` run at unit angular speed:
`θ ↦ cos θ · a + sin θ · b` runs through every point `u a + v b` with `u² + v² = 1` and no other. -/
lemma circleCurve_range :
    range (fun t => ((Geodesic.circleCurve a b 1).pos t).2) = Crossing.greatCircle a b := by
  ext x
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨θ, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨Real.cos (1 * θ), Real.sin (1 * θ), Real.cos_sq_add_sin_sq _, rfl⟩
  · rintro ⟨u, v, huv, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨θ, hcos, hsin⟩ := Geodesic.exists_angle huv
    exact ⟨θ, by show Real.cos (1 * θ) • a + Real.sin (1 * θ) • b = _; rw [one_mul, hcos, hsin]⟩
        TheoremTwoCells.geodesic_through_twoline 167
        /-- **Exactly one geodesic of space passes through two points that are neither equal nor
antipodal** (Sec. II).  In the space at an instant of de Sitter space of radius `ρ`, the sphere of
radius `ρ` of `E`, a geodesic runs on a great circle (`Geodesic.IsGeodesic.greatCircle`), and
exactly one great circle passes through the two points (`greatCircle_through`,
`greatCircle_unique`).  So there is such a geodesic, closed, of length `2πρ`
(`Geodesic.IsGeodesic.hasLength`), and any two have the same path. -/
theorem geodesic_through_two (hρ : 0 < ρ) {p q : E} (hp : ‖p‖ = ρ) (hq : ‖q‖ = ρ) (hqp : q ≠ p)
    (hqp' : q ≠ -p) :
    (∃ γ : Geodesic.Curve ℝ E, Geodesic.IsGeodesic (ρ ^ 2) γ ∧ Geodesic.IsSpacelike γ ∧
      Geodesic.InSpace γ ∧ Geodesic.HasLength γ (2 * Real.pi * ρ) ∧
      p ∈ range (fun t => (γ.pos t).2) ∧ q ∈ range (fun t => (γ.pos t).2)) ∧
    ∀ γ₁ γ₂ : Geodesic.Curve ℝ E,
      Geodesic.IsGeodesic (ρ ^ 2) γ₁ → Geodesic.IsSpacelike γ₁ → Geodesic.InSpace γ₁ →
      p ∈ range (fun t => (γ₁.pos t).2) → q ∈ range (fun t => (γ₁.pos t).2) →
      Geodesic.IsGeodesic (ρ ^ 2) γ₂ → Geodesic.IsSpacelike γ₂ → Geodesic.InSpace γ₂ →
      p ∈ range (fun t => (γ₂.pos t).2) → q ∈ range (fun t => (γ₂.pos t).2) →
      range (fun t => (γ₁.pos t).2) = range (fun t => (γ₂.pos t).2) := by
  constructor
  · obtain ⟨a, b, hab, ha, hb, hpm, hqm⟩ := greatCircle_through hρ hp hq hqp hqp'
    have hg := Geodesic.circleCurve_geodesic (ω := 1) hab ha hb
    have hs := Geodesic.circleCurve_spacelike (ω := 1) hab ha hb hρ one_ne_zero
    have hl := hg.hasLength (by positivity) hs
    rw [Real.sqrt_sq hρ.le] at hl
    refine ⟨Geodesic.circleCurve a b 1, hg, hs, Geodesic.circleCurve_inSpace, hl, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [circleCurve_range]
      exact hpm
    · rw [circleCurve_range]
      exact hqm
  · intro γ₁ γ₂ g₁ s₁ i₁ p₁ q₁ g₂ s₂ i₂ p₂ q₂
    obtain ⟨o₁, n₁, m₁, r₁⟩ := g₁.greatCircle hρ s₁ i₁
    obtain ⟨o₂, n₂, m₂, r₂⟩ := g₂.greatCircle hρ s₂ i₂
    rw [r₁] at p₁ q₁ ⊢
    rw [r₂] at p₂ q₂ ⊢
    exact (greatCircle_unique hρ o₂ n₂ m₂ o₁ n₁ m₁ p₂ q₂ p₁ q₁ hqp hqp')

        
end Circles

end TwoCells

/-!
# The rotations of the three-sphere (Sec. IV.D), and rings in a quotient

The solution without a mass is found in `Space.lean` from its space at an instant, a quotient of
the three-sphere by a finite group `Γ` of rotations, which the rings make trivial
(`Space.sphere_rings`); this file proves what that step needs of such a group, the plane it turns
(`exists_rotation_plane`) and a plane that finitely many such maps leave (`exists_plane_not_turned`).

It also states what a ring in a quotient is, in the terms that `Space.lean` and `Solution.lean`
use.  A curve closes in the quotient by `Γ` after the time `P` when some map of `Γ` carries its
point at every `t` to its point at `t + P` (`Returns`).  A ring of length `len` closes so after a
least time `P > 0`, and its speed covers `len` in that time (`ClosesIn`); in the trivial quotient
it is a closed curve of length `len` (`closesIn_bot`).  A group acts properly discontinuously when
only finitely many of its maps carry a point of a compact set into that set (`ProperOn`), which is
what `Space.flat_space_no_rings` and `Space.hyperbolic_space_no_rings` use of the group.  The great
circles `t ↦ cos t · a + sin t · b` of de Sitter space (`planeCurve`) are geodesics of the quadric
`form X X = k` when `a` and `b` are orthogonal with `form a a = form b b = k`
(`planeCurve_isGeodesic`); `Space.sphere_rings` and the model rings of `Solution.lean` are such
circles.

One fact of geometry is taken as known: a closed geodesic of a quotient is a geodesic `c` of the
space with `c (t + P) = g (c t)` for one map `g` of `Γ` and every `t`, of length its speed times
the least such `P > 0`.
-/

open RealInnerProductSpace Set Geodesic

namespace Quotients

section Form

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
        LemmaQuotients.form_eqline 36
        /-- The form of `ℝ × E`, one time: `−st + ⟪x, y⟫`. -/
lemma form_eq (p q : ℝ × E) : form p q = -(p.1 * q.1) + ⟪p.2, q.2⟫ := by
  unfold form
  simp [RCLike.inner_apply, mul_comm]
        LemmaQuotients.exists_orthonormal_pairline 41
        /-- Two orthonormal vectors in a space of at least two dimensions. -/
lemma exists_orthonormal_pair [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (hE : 2 ≤ Module.finrank ℝ E) :
    ∃ f₁ f₂ : E, ‖f₁‖ = 1 ∧ ‖f₂‖ = 1 ∧ ⟪f₁, f₂⟫ = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨B⟩ : Nonempty (OrthonormalBasis (Fin (Module.finrank ℝ E)) ℝ E) :=
    ⟨stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ E⟩
  exact ⟨B ⟨0, by omega⟩, B ⟨1, by omega⟩, B.orthonormal.1 _, B.orthonormal.1 _,
    B.orthonormal.2 (by simp)⟩

lemma exists_unit_perp [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (hE : 2 ≤ Module.finrank ℝ E) {u : E} (hu : u ≠ 0) :
    ∃ w : E, ‖w‖ = 1 ∧ ⟪u, w⟫ = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨w', hw', hw0⟩ : ∃ w' ∈ (ℝ ∙ u)ᗮ, w' ≠ 0 := by
    apply Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot
    intro h

  refine ⟨‖w'‖⁻¹ • w', ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm, inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hw0)]
  · rw [real_inner_smul_right, Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right.1 hw', mul_zero]

/-! ### Rings in a quotient -/

section Rings

variable {F X : Type*} [FunLike F X X]
        DefinitionQuotients.Returnsline 74
        /-- **The curve `c` closes in the quotient by `Γ` after the time `P`**: some map of `Γ` carries its
point at every `t` to its point at `t + P`, so that in the quotient the curve is back where it was. -/
def Returns (Γ : Set F) (c : ℝ → X) (P : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ g ∈ Γ, ∀ t, c (t + P) = g (c t)
        DefinitionQuotients.ClosesInline 79
        /-- **A ring of length `len` in the quotient by `Γ`**: the curve `c` closes in the quotient after a
least time `P > 0`, and its speed `v` covers `len` in that time at every point.  For the trivial
group this is a closed curve of length `len` (`closesIn_bot`), and for a group acting on de Sitter
space it is a closed geodesic of the quotient when `c` is a geodesic. -/
def ClosesIn (Γ : Set F) (c : ℝ → X) (v : ℝ → ℝ) (len : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : ℝ, 0 < P ∧ Returns Γ c P ∧ (∀ P' : ℝ, 0 < P' → Returns Γ c P' → P ≤ P') ∧
    ∀ t, v t * P = len

        
end Rings
        DefinitionQuotients.speedline 89
        /-- the speed of a curve, `√(form vel vel)` -/
noncomputable def speed {T E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup T] [InnerProductSpace ℝ T]
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] (γ : Curve T E) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt (form (γ.vel t) (γ.vel t))
        DefinitionQuotients.ProperOnline 94
        /-- **A group of maps of `X` acting properly discontinuously**: only finitely many of its maps
carry a point of a compact set `K` into `K`.  The quotient of a manifold by a group of
homeomorphisms that acts so, and whose maps other than the identity fix no point, is a Hausdorff
manifold. -/
def ProperOn {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] (Γ : Set (Equiv.Perm X)) : Prop :=
  ∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → {g | g ∈ Γ ∧ ((⇑g) '' K ∩ K).Nonempty}.Finite

        
/-! ### The trivial quotient of de Sitter space -/

section DeSitter

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
        LemmaQuotients.closesIn_botline 107
        /-- **In the trivial quotient a ring is a closed curve**: a curve closes in the quotient by the
trivial group, with the length `len`, exactly when it is a closed curve of length `len`. -/
lemma closesIn_bot {γ : Curve ℝ E} {len : ℝ} :
    ClosesIn ((⊥ : Subgroup ((ℝ × E) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × E))) : Set ((ℝ × E) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × E))) γ.pos
      (speed γ) len ↔ HasLength γ len := by
  have hret : ∀ P, Returns ((⊥ : Subgroup ((ℝ × E) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × E))) :
      Set ((ℝ × E) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × E))) γ.pos P ↔ Function.Periodic γ.pos P := by
    intro P
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨g, hg, hgP⟩ t
      rw [SetLike.mem_coe, Subgroup.mem_bot] at hg
      rw [hgP t, hg]
      rfl
    · intro hP
      exact ⟨1, Subgroup.one_mem _, fun t => hP t⟩
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨P, hP, hr, hleast, hlen⟩
    exact ⟨P, hP, (hret P).1 hr, fun P' hP' h' => hleast P' hP' ((hret P').2 h'), hlen⟩
  · rintro ⟨P, hP, hper, hleast, hlen⟩
    exact ⟨P, hP, (hret P).2 hper, fun P' hP' h' => hleast P' hP' ((hret P').1 h'), hlen⟩

        
end DeSitter

lemma exists_angle_pos {c s : ℝ} (h : c ^ 2 + s ^ 2 = 1) (hc : c < 1) :

  have hc' : -1 ≤ c := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg s]

    rw [Real.sin_arccos, hsq, abs_of_nonneg hs]

vector at which `⟪y, A y⟫` is largest on the unit sphere, with the value `m`.  Along the sphere the
value does not change to first order at `u`, so `A u + A⁻¹ u = 2m u`, and the plane of `u` and
`A u` is carried onto itself.  As `A` fixes no vector, `m < 1`.  If `m = −1`, `A = −1`, which turns

lemma exists_rotation_plane [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (hE : 2 ≤ Module.finrank ℝ E)

    ∃ u w : E, ‖u‖ = 1 ∧ ‖w‖ = 1 ∧ ⟪u, w⟫ = 0 ∧ ∃ c s : ℝ, c ^ 2 + s ^ 2 = 1 ∧ c < 1 ∧

  have hnorm : ∀ y, ‖A y‖ = ‖y‖ := fun y => by
    rw [norm_eq_sqrt_real_inner, norm_eq_sqrt_real_inner, hA]

  rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm] at hu
  have hu2 : ⟪u, u⟫ = 1 := by rw [real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hu]; norm_num
  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ : ∃ m, m = ⟪u, A u⟫ := ⟨_, rfl⟩

    intro y

    · simp

        rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm, inv_mul_cancel₀ hn.ne']

      simp only [map_smul, real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_right] at h
      rw [← hm] at h

        field_simp
      rw [e]
      have := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h (sq_nonneg ‖y‖)

  have hstat : ∀ w, ⟪u, w⟫ = 0 → ⟪u, A w⟫ + ⟪w, A u⟫ = 0 := by
    intro w hw
    obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ : ∃ b, b = ⟪u, A w⟫ + ⟪w, A u⟫ := ⟨_, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ : ∃ D, D = m * ‖w‖ ^ 2 - ⟪w, A w⟫ := ⟨_, rfl⟩
    have key : ∀ t : ℝ, t * b ≤ t ^ 2 * D := by
      intro t
      have h := hle (u + t • w)
      have hn : ‖u + t • w‖ ^ 2 = 1 + t ^ 2 * ‖w‖ ^ 2 := by
        rw [← real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, inner_add_left, inner_add_right, inner_add_right,
          real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_right, real_inner_smul_left,
          real_inner_smul_right, hu2, real_inner_comm u w, hw, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
        ring
      rw [hn, map_add, map_smul, inner_add_left, inner_add_right, inner_add_right,
        real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_right, real_inner_smul_left,
        real_inner_smul_right, ← hm] at h
      rw [hb, hD]
      nlinarith [h]
    obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ : ∃ M, M = |D| + 1 := ⟨_, rfl⟩
    have hM0 : 0 < M := by rw [hM]; positivity
    have hDM : D ≤ M - 1 := by rw [hM]; linarith [le_abs_self D]
    have h1 := key (b / (2 * M))
    have h2 : b ^ 2 * (2 * M ^ 2 + 2 * M) ≤ 0 := by
      have e1 : b / (2 * M) * b = b ^ 2 / (2 * M) := by ring
      have e2 : (b / (2 * M)) ^ 2 * D = b ^ 2 * D / (4 * M ^ 2) := by ring
      rw [e1, e2, div_le_div_iff₀ (by positivity) (by positivity)] at h1

lemma eq_of_sin_sub_eq_zero {ψ ψ' : ℝ} (hψ : ψ ∈ Set.Ico 0 Real.pi) (hψ' : ψ' ∈ Set.Ico 0 Real.pi)

        /-- **A plane that none of finitely many turns of `E` carries onto itself.**  Let finitely many
linear maps of `E`, of dimension four, keep the inner product, fix no vector but zero and differ
from `−1`.  Then some orthonormal pair `u, v` spans a plane that none of them carries onto itself:
for no map `A` among them and no `c, s` is `A u = c u + s v` and `A v = −s u + c v`.  With
`e₀, …, e₃` an orthonormal basis, the planes of `u(ψ) = cos ψ e₀ + sin ψ e₁` and `v = e₂`,
`0 ≤ ψ < π`, are infinitely many, and each map carries at most one of them onto itself.  For if `A`
carried two, `ψ ≠ ψ'`, then `A e₂ = −s u(ψ) + c e₂ = −s' u(ψ') + c' e₂` gives `c = c'` and
`s u(ψ) = s' u(ψ')`.  With `s ≠ 0` the unit vectors `u(ψ)` and `u(ψ')` are parallel, so `ψ = ψ'`.
With `s = 0`, `A e₂ = c e₂` with `c = −1`, as `c = 1` would fix `e₂`, and `A u(ψ) = −u(ψ)`,
`A u(ψ') = −u(ψ')`, so `cos ψ a + sin ψ d = 0 = cos ψ' a + sin ψ' d` with `a = A e₀ + e₀` and
`d = A e₁ + e₁`; as `ψ ≠ ψ'` this makes `a = d = 0`, so `A = −1` on `e₀, e₁, e₂`, and then on `e₃`
too, since `A e₃` is orthogonal to `A e₀, A e₁, A e₂` and `A e₃ = e₃` would fix `e₃`: `A = −1`. -/

    ∃ u v : E, ‖u‖ = 1 ∧ ‖v‖ = 1 ∧ ⟪u, v⟫ = 0 ∧
      ∀ A ∈ S, ∀ c s : ℝ, A u = c • u + s • v → A v = (-s) • u + c • v → False := by
  have hb : ∀ i j, ⟪b i, b j⟫ = if i = j then 1 else 0 := orthonormal_iff_ite.1 b.orthonormal
  have hbn : ∀ i, ‖b i‖ = 1 := b.orthonormal.1
  have hb1 : ∀ i, ⟪b i, b i⟫ = 1 := fun i => by rw [hb]; simp
  have hb0 : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → ⟪b i, b j⟫ = 0 := fun i j h => by rw [hb]; simp [h]

        RegisterGravity/Homogeneous.lean48 lines

        import RegisterGravity.RouteB

/-!
# No cell differs from another (Postulate 2)

After its four clauses on cells and rings, Postulate 2 says: "No cell differs from another: some map
of the cells that keeps the largest rings carries any cell to any other and leaves every law
unchanged.  No law depends on the direction in which a ring passes through a cell.  Every largest
ring is a closed geodesic of space, made of its cells as segments of length `ℓ_c`."  This file
concerns the first of these clauses.  A
**symmetry** of a register is a map of the cells onto themselves, with a map of the largest rings,
that keeps which cells lie on which ring (`Symmetry`).

The clause has two parts.  The first, that some symmetry carries any cell to any other, is a
property of the register, `Horizon.Homogeneous`; `Models.lean`, `DiffSet.lean` and `Singer.lean`
build registers that have it, for every prime-power order.  The second, that the symmetry leaves
every law unchanged, concerns the laws.  `Symmetry.lean` states the laws as functions of the
register, of the crossing of a ring with a cell, and takes the whole clause as its hypothesis
`hsym`; with the clause on directions it derives the symmetry of space (Sec. II): every law is the
same at every place and in every direction of the space the rings describe, whatever the drawing
(`Symmetry.laws_same`, `Symmetry.lawAt_same`).

Until v18-40 the clause also asked that the map keep the positions of the cells along the rings up
to one common shift, and the structure carried that as a field; no theorem used it, and the paper
(-6-38-27) drops the words.
-/

open Finset

namespace Horizon

variable {L : ℕ} (H : Horizon L)
        Input · Postulate 2 (structure)Horizon.Symmetryline 34
        /-- **A symmetry of the register**: a map of the cells onto themselves, with a map of the largest
rings, that keeps which cells lie on which ring. -/
structure Symmetry where
  /-- where each cell goes -/
  cellMap : H.Cell ≃ H.Cell
  /-- where each ring goes -/
  loopMap : H.Loop ≃ H.Loop
  /-- a cell lies on a ring exactly when its image lies on the ring's image -/
  mem_iff : ∀ l x, x ∈ H.cells l ↔ cellMap x ∈ H.cells (loopMap l)
        DefinitionHorizon.Homogeneousline 44
        /-- **The register's part of the clause of Postulate 2 that no cell differs from another**: some
symmetry of the register carries any cell to any other. -/
def Homogeneous : Prop := ∀ x y : H.Cell, ∃ s : H.Symmetry, s.cellMap x = y

        
end Horizon

import RegisterGravity.Projective

/-!
# A register from a perfect difference set (Sec. II, "The count")

A **perfect difference set** mod `n` is a set `D` of residues such that every nonzero residue is
the difference `d − d'` of exactly one ordered pair of its elements.  With `|D| = k`, it is the
Singer form of a projective plane of order `k − 1`: the points are the residues mod `n`, and the
lines are the translates `D + l`.  Doubling each point into a cell and its opposite gives a
register of `L = 2k` (`ofDiffSet`): a cell is (point, side), its opposite flips the side, and the
ring `l` holds both sides of the points `d + l`, `d ∈ D`, running through them in the order of `D`
on one side and back through them on the other (`ofDiffSetPositions`), so that the opposite of a
cell lies `k` steps, half the ring, on.  That its cells and rings meet the first four clauses of
Postulate 2 follows from the difference property.

**The register has the maps of the clause of Postulate 2 that no cell differs from another**
(`ofDiffSet_homogeneous`): the translation `p ↦ p + t`, which carries the ring `l` to the ring
`l + t`, and the swap of sides are symmetries (`dsSym`), and together they carry any cell to any
other.  `register_of_diffSet` states
the result, with the register's order as a projective plane (`Projective.lean`), `k − 1`.  `Singer.lean`
supplies a perfect difference set of `q + 1` residues mod `q² + q + 1` for every prime power `q`.
-/

open Finset

namespace Horizon
        DefinitionHorizon.xorEquivline 29
        /-- flipping the side of every cell, or not -/
def xorEquiv (f : Bool) : Bool ≃ Bool where
  toFun b := xor b f
  invFun b := xor b f
  left_inv b := by cases b <;> cases f <;> rfl
  right_inv b := by cases b <;> cases f <;> rfl
        DefinitionHorizon.IsPerfectDifferenceSetline 36
        /-- **A perfect difference set** mod `n`: every nonzero residue is the difference of exactly one
ordered pair of its elements. -/
def IsPerfectDifferenceSet {n : ℕ} (D : Finset (ZMod n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : ZMod n, t ≠ 0 → ((D ×ˢ D).filter (fun pr => pr.1 - pr.2 = t)).card = 1
        LemmaHorizon.IsPerfectDifferenceSet.existsUniqueline 41
        /-- In a perfect difference set, each nonzero residue is the difference of one ordered pair. -/
lemma IsPerfectDifferenceSet.existsUnique {n : ℕ} {D : Finset (ZMod n)}
    (hD : IsPerfectDifferenceSet D) {t : ZMod n} (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    ∃! pr : ZMod n × ZMod n, pr.1 ∈ D ∧ pr.2 ∈ D ∧ pr.1 - pr.2 = t := by
  obtain ⟨pr, hpr⟩ := Finset.card_eq_one.mp (hD t ht)
  have hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ (D ×ˢ D).filter (fun pr => pr.1 - pr.2 = t) ↔ x = pr := by
    intro x
    rw [hpr, Finset.mem_singleton]
  refine ⟨pr, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have := (hmem pr).2 rfl
    simp only [mem_filter, mem_product] at this

        import RegisterGravity.DiffSet
import Mathlib.FieldTheory.Finite.Extension

/-!
# Singer's theorem: a register for every prime-power order (Sec. II, "The count")

**Singer's theorem** [J. Singer, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 43, 377 (1938)]: for a finite field `K` of
`q` elements there is a perfect difference set of `q + 1` residues mod `n = q² + q + 1`
(`exists_pds`).  The proof here is Singer's.  Let `E` be the cubic extension of `K`
(`FiniteField.Extension K p 3`, of `q³` elements, a vector space of dimension 3 over `K`), `ω` a
generator of its units, of order `q³ − 1 = (q − 1)n`, and `W` a plane of `E`, a `K`-subspace of
dimension 2.  Then `ω ^ n` lies in `K` (`pow_n_mem`), the nonzero vectors of `E` are the points
`ω ^ k`, `0 ≤ k < n`, times the nonzero elements of `K`, each in one way (`card_nonzero`), and a
subspace of dimension `d` holds `(q^d − 1)/(q − 1)` points (`card_points`).  Let `D` be the `k` for
which `ω ^ k` lies in `W`: `q + 1` of them.  A pair `(d, d')` of `D` with `d − d' = t` is a point of
`W` that `ω ^ t` carries into `W`, a point of `W ∩ ω^{−t}W`.  Two planes of a space of dimension 3
share at least a line, so every nonzero `t` is a difference at least once; and the differences of
distinct elements of `D` number `|D|(|D| − 1) = q² + q = n − 1`, one for each nonzero `t`.  So each
nonzero `t` is a difference exactly once.

With `DiffSet.lean`, a register of `L = 2(q + 1)` whose cells and rings meet the first four
clauses of Postulate 2, with the maps of the clause that no cell differs from another, exists for
every finite field (`homogeneous_register`), so for every prime power `q`
(`homogeneous_register_of_prime_power`).  It is the only file that imports Mathlib's extensions of
finite fields (`Mathlib.FieldTheory.Finite.Extension`).
-/

namespace Horizon

namespace Singer

        /-- **Every nonzero vector of a subspace is a point of it times a nonzero element of `K`**, in
exactly one way: the nonzero vectors number `(q − 1)` times the points. -/
lemma card_nonzero (V : Submodule K (Ext K p)) :
    (univ.filter (fun x : Ext K p => x ∈ V ∧ x ≠ 0)).card =
      (univ.filter (fun k : ZMod (nPts K) => pt ω k ∈ V)).card * (Fintype.card K - 1) := by
  classical
  set A := (univ.filter (fun k : ZMod (nPts K) => pt ω k ∈ V)) ×ˢ (univ : Finset Kˣ)
  have hA : A.card =
      (univ.filter (fun k : ZMod (nPts K) => pt ω k ∈ V)).card * (Fintype.card K - 1) := by
    rw [card_product, card_univ, Fintype.card_units]
  rw [← hA]
  symm
  apply Finset.card_nbij (fun pr => ((pr.2 : K)) • pt ω pr.1)
  · intro pr hpr
    have h1 : pt ω pr.1 ∈ V := (Finset.mem_filter.mp (Finset.mem_product.mp hpr).1).2
    exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, V.smul_mem _ h1,
      smul_ne_zero pr.2.ne_zero (pt_ne_zero _)⟩
  · intro pr _ pr' _ h
    simp only at h
    have hk : pr.1 = pr'.1 := by
      apply pt_inj hord (b := ((pr.2 : K))⁻¹ * (pr'.2 : K))
      rw [← smul_smul, ← h, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ pr.2.ne_zero, one_smul]
    rw [hk] at h
    have ha : (pr.2 : K) = pr'.2 := smul_left_injective K (pt_ne_zero pr'.1) h
    exact Prod.ext hk (Units.ext ha)
  · intro x hx
    have hx' := Finset.mem_filter.mp (Finset.mem_coe.mp hx)
    obtain ⟨hxV, hx0⟩ := hx'.2
    have hmem : Units.mk0 x hx0 ∈ Submonoid.powers ω :=
      (mem_powers_iff_mem_zpowers).2 (hω _)
    obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := hmem
    have hxm : x = (ω : Ext K p) ^ m := by
      have := congrArg Units.val hm
      simpa using this.symm
    obtain ⟨b, hb0, hb⟩ := pow_split hord m
    refine ⟨((m : ZMod (nPts K)), Units.mk0 b hb0), ?_, ?_⟩
    · refine Finset.mem_coe.mpr (Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_filter.mpr
        ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩, Finset.mem_univ _⟩)
      rw [← pow_mem_iff hord, ← hxm]
      exact hxV
    · simp only [Units.val_mk0]
      rw [hxm, hb]

        /-- **The points of a subspace**: `(q − 1)` times their number is `q^{dim} − 1`. -/
lemma card_points (V : Submodule K (Ext K p)) :
    (univ.filter (fun k : ZMod (nPts K) => pt ω k ∈ V)).card * (Fintype.card K - 1) =
      Fintype.card K ^ Module.finrank K V - 1 := by
  classical
  rw [← card_nonzero hω hord V]
  have hV : (univ.filter (fun x : Ext K p => x ∈ V)).card = Fintype.card K ^ Module.finrank K V := by
    rw [← Module.card_eq_pow_finrank (K := K) (V := V)]
    rw [Fintype.card_subtype]
  have herase : univ.filter (fun x : Ext K p => x ∈ V ∧ x ≠ 0) =
      (univ.filter (fun x : Ext K p => x ∈ V)).erase 0 := by
    ext x
    simp [and_comm]
  rw [herase, card_erase_of_mem (by simp [V.zero_mem]), hV]

        /-- multiplying the point `k` by the point `t` lands in a subspace exactly when the point
`t + k` does -/
lemma mul_pt_mem_iff (V : Submodule K (Ext K p)) (t k : ZMod (nPts K)) :
    pt ω t * pt ω k ∈ V ↔ pt ω (t + k) ∈ V := by
  rw [pt, pt, ← pow_add, pow_mem_iff hord, Nat.cast_add, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val,
    ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]

        /-- **A plane of the cubic extension**: a `K`-subspace of dimension 2, the kernel of a coordinate. -/
lemma exists_plane : ∃ W : Submodule K (Ext K p), Module.finrank K W = 2 := by
  let b : Module.Basis (Fin 3) K (Ext K p) := Module.finBasisOfFinrankEq K _ finrank_ext
  refine ⟨LinearMap.ker (b.coord 2), ?_⟩
  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (b.coord 2) := fun a => ⟨a • b 2, by simp⟩
  have h := LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker (b.coord 2)
  rw [LinearMap.range_eq_top.mpr hsurj, finrank_top, Module.finrank_self, finrank_ext] at h
  omega

      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_offDiag, Finset.mem_product]
      constructor

        exact ⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, h3⟩
      · rintro ⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, h3⟩

        rw [heq, sub_self] at h3

variable (K) in
        TheoremHorizon.Singer.exists_pdsline 403
        /-- **Singer's theorem**: for a finite field `K` of `q` elements there is a perfect difference set
of `q + 1` residues mod `q² + q + 1`. -/
theorem exists_pds :
    ∃ D : Finset (ZMod (nPts K)), IsPerfectDifferenceSet D ∧ D.card = Fintype.card K + 1 := by
  have : Fact (ringChar K).Prime := ⟨CharP.prime_ringChar K⟩
  exact exists_pds_aux (ringChar K)
        TheoremHorizon.Singer.homogeneous_registerline 410
        /-- **A register for every finite field**: with `q = |K|`, a register of `L = 2(q + 1)`, with a
cyclic order on each ring, whose cells and rings meet the first four clauses of Postulate 2, with
the maps of the clause that no cell differs from another; its order as a projective plane is
`q`. -/
theorem homogeneous_register (K : Type) [Field K] [Fintype K] :
    ∃ H : Horizon (2 * (Fintype.card K + 1)), Nonempty H.Positions ∧ H.Homogeneous ∧
      ∀ hL : 6 ≤ 2 * (Fintype.card K + 1), H.order hL = Fintype.card K := by
  obtain ⟨D, hD, hcard⟩ := exists_pds K
  have h3 : 3 ≤ D.card := by
    rw [hcard]
    have := two_le_card (K := K)
    omega
  obtain ⟨H, hP, hhom, hord⟩ := register_of_diffSet hD h3
  rw [← hcard]
  refine ⟨H, hP, hhom, fun hL => ?_⟩
  rw [hord hL, hcard]
  rfl
        TheoremHorizon.Singer.homogeneous_register_of_prime_powerline 428
        /-- **A register for every prime power**: for every prime `p` and `n ≥ 1` there is a register of
`L = 2(pⁿ + 1)`, with a cyclic order on each ring, whose cells and rings meet the first four
clauses of Postulate 2, with the maps of the clause that no cell differs from another; its order as
a projective plane is `pⁿ`. -/
theorem homogeneous_register_of_prime_power (p n : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    ∃ H : Horizon (2 * (p ^ n + 1)), Nonempty H.Positions ∧ H.Homogeneous ∧
      ∀ hL : 6 ≤ 2 * (p ^ n + 1), H.order hL = p ^ n := by
  have : Fintype (GaloisField p n) := Fintype.ofFinite _
  have hq : Fintype.card (GaloisField p n) = p ^ n := by
    rw [← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
    exact GaloisField.card p n hn
  have key := homogeneous_register (GaloisField p n)
  rw [hq] at key
  exact key

        
end Singer

        import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.BigOperators
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Group.Finset
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Field.Basic
import Mathlib.Basic.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.Positivity

/-!
# The qubit ceiling (Sec. IV.A, and the remarks of Sec. V)

Formal counterpart of the paragraph of Sec. IV.A that derives the bound `2^N ≤ L`, and of the
remarks of Sec. V on how soft the bound is and on Palmer's bit count.

The bits are the possible outcomes of one measurement of the qubit (Postulate 1): each cell's bit
is one possible outcome among the `L`, so the outcome is the bit of a cell of a set `A` with the
probability `|A|/L` (`share_read`, from the hypothesis `halike`: each cell's bit is the outcome
with the probability `1/L`), and the probability of an outcome is its share of the bits.  When a
state is measured jointly (Postulate 1), the possible outcomes are the positions, each one among
`L`, the same on every string of the qubits it measures, since the shift is one translation on
every string and keeps them in step; the outcome at a position is the bits there.  So every
position of a later string is paired with one outcome of the earlier qubits, their bits there
(`jointOutcome`); this is Palmer's state of `N` qubits, `N` correlated strings of `L` bits with one
permutation applied to all of them, and it needs no shared cell.  The paper's *block* (Sec. IV.A)
is the set of cells of a later string whose bits are paired with one joint outcome of the earlier
qubits; blocks of different outcomes are disjoint, and the fraction of 1s on a block is the
probability of the outcome 1 given the block's joint outcome, its share of the possible outcomes
that show that joint outcome (`block_fraction_read`).  The general
theorems take the pairing as a function `e` from the cells of the later string to the joint
outcomes, and index the blocks through a map `s` from outcomes to labels: `block e s σ` is the set
of cells whose outcome has the label `σ`.  With `s` the identity, the blocks are the paper's, one
per joint outcome (`ceiling_by_outcome`); with `s` injective, still one per outcome (the general
`ceiling`); with `s` constant, all outcomes would share one block, the whole string, a coarser
grouping than the paper's: the test of Sec. IV.A,
which rests on whether each string has room for the different conditional states of its qubit,
its states given the outcomes of the earlier qubits, counts in this way when it says "In a product
state each string has one conditional state to hold, on all its cells" (a block holds the conditional
state of its joint outcome, and blocks of different outcomes may hold the same one).  The paper's
Sec. IV.A also derives the limit for a linear cluster state followed by one layer of generic
single-qubit rotations, whose last qubit has a different conditional state for each joint outcome of
the earlier ones (`Cluster.chain_card`); for generic rotations every block's fraction lies strictly
between 0 and 1, so that state is a case of `ceiling_by_outcome` as a random state is.  `ceiling_in_step` is the
bound with the pairing the strings supply, `e` the bits of the earlier strings at each position.

* `two_le_card_of_frac`: a block whose fraction lies strictly between 0 and 1 needs at least two
  cells, one reading 1 and one reading −1 (the bit `false` here).
* `frac_pos_lt_one`: conversely, a block with a cell reading 1 and a cell reading −1 has a
  fraction strictly between 0 and 1.  The ceilings of `Main.lean` come to the fractions this way,
  from a joint outcome that occurs being the outcome at a position.
* `outcomes_iff_cells`: what that premise and a condition on `pr` ask together.  Each outcome of
  a set has a cell of either bit exactly when some `pr` meets both the premise and the condition
  that each outcome of the set occurs with either value of the bit.
* `ceiling`: when each of the `2^(N−1)` joint outcomes of the first `N − 1` qubits occurs, with
  the last qubit's bit given it at a probability strictly between 0 and 1, the last string, of
  `L` cells, needs `2^(N−1)` blocks of at least two cells, so `2^N ≤ L`.  A random state is such a
  state, and so is a product state of `N` qubits each in a superposition (Sec. IV.A): the bound
  holds for every state in which all `2^N` joint outcomes occur.  `ceiling_by_outcome` is the
  theorem with the paper's blocks, `s` the identity on outcomes.
* `ceiling_logical`: a string with `2^N` blocks, each with a fraction strictly between 0 and 1,
  needs `2^(N+1) ≤ L`.  Sec. IV.A finds up to that many conditional states on the fullest physical
  string of `N` logical qubits, and that many in the surface code; that no physical string has
  more, with the blocks read in order, is a step of coding theory that `Coding.lean` proves, with
  the same count for blocks by
  conditional state (`Coding.ceiling_line_code`, `Coding.card_condStates_le`);
  `Numerics.logical_ceiling_cos` gives the `203` logical qubits that follow.
* `ceiling_soft`: if each block needs `r` cells, `2^(N−1) r ≤ L`, that is `N ≤ log₂(2L/r)`
  (Sec. V: `202`, `200` and `199` for `r = 10`, `30` and `100` at `L_cos`,
  `Numerics.soft_ceilings`).
* `ceiling_in_step`: the same bound for `N` strings read in step, the pairing being their bits at
  each position (`jointOutcome`).
* `share_read`: with each cell's bit one possible outcome among `L` (Postulate 1), the outcome is
  the bit of a cell of a set `A` with the probability `|A|/L`, the set's share of the cells.
* `condProb`, `block_fraction_read`: the probability that the outcome is `1`, given that it is
  the bit of a cell of a block (`condProb`), is the block's fraction of 1s, so a block's fraction
  is the conditional probability that the ceiling theorems of this file take it to be.
  `Main.block_fraction` states it from Postulate 1's premise for the cells
  (`Sources.P1.ring_bits_alike`).  The ceilings of `Main.lean` do not take those equal weights.
  They take that a joint outcome that occurs is the outcome at a position
  (`Sources.P1.outcomes_at_positions`) and that no ring has more than `L` cells
  (`Sources.P1.ring_cells`).
* `one_cell_block`: a block of one cell has the fraction 0 or 1, as a state of the
  Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger type needs (Secs. IV.A and V).
* `nmax_iff`: when `2^N₀ ≤ L < 2^(N₀+1)`, `2^N ≤ L` exactly when `N ≤ N₀`, so `N_max = N₀`.
* `palmer_threshold`: Palmer's bit count `2^(N+1) − 2 ≤ NL` holds exactly for `N ≤ N₀` once it
  holds at `N₀ ≥ 1` and fails at `N₀ + 1`.
-/

open Finset

namespace Register
namespace Capacity

variable {Cell : Type*}
        DefinitionCapacity.fracline 97
        /-- the fraction of 1s of the bits `b` on a block `B` of cells -/
noncomputable def frac (b : Cell → Bool) (B : Finset Cell) : ℝ :=
  ((B.filter (fun x => b x = true)).card : ℝ) / B.card
        TheoremCapacity.two_le_card_of_fracline 101
        /-- **A block whose fraction lies strictly between 0 and 1 needs at least two cells, one reading 1
and one reading −1** (the bit `false` here). -/
theorem two_le_card_of_frac (b : Cell → Bool) (B : Finset Cell)
    (h0 : 0 < frac b B) (h1 : frac b B < 1) :
    2 ≤ B.card ∧ (∃ x ∈ B, b x = true) ∧ (∃ y ∈ B, b y = false) := by
  unfold frac at h0 h1
  set a := (B.filter (fun x => b x = true)).card with ha
  -- the block is not empty, and it holds a 1
  have hn : (0 : ℝ) < B.card := by
    rcases (div_pos_iff.1 h0) with ⟨-, h⟩ | ⟨h, -⟩
    · exact h
    · exact absurd h (not_lt.2 (Nat.cast_nonneg _))
  have hapos : (0 : ℝ) < a := by
    rcases (div_pos_iff.1 h0) with ⟨h, -⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩
    · exact h
    · exact absurd h (not_lt.2 hn.le)
  have hone : ∃ x ∈ B, b x = true := by
    have : 0 < a := by exact_mod_cast hapos
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := Finset.card_pos.1 this
    rw [mem_filter] at hx
    exact ⟨x, hx.1, hx.2⟩
  -- and it holds a 0: else every cell reads 1 and the fraction is 1
  have hzero : ∃ y ∈ B, b y = false := by
    by_contra hno
    push Not at hno
    have hall : B.filter (fun x => b x = true) = B := by
      apply Finset.filter_true_of_mem
      intro y hy
      have := hno y hy
      simpa using this
    rw [ha, hall, div_self hn.ne'] at h1
    exact lt_irrefl _ h1
  obtain ⟨x, hxB, hx⟩ := hone
  obtain ⟨y, hyB, hy⟩ := hzero
  have hxy : x ≠ y := by
    rintro rfl
    rw [hx] at hy
    exact Bool.noConfusion hy
  exact ⟨Finset.one_lt_card.2 ⟨x, hxB, y, hyB, hxy⟩, ⟨x, hxB, hx⟩, ⟨y, hyB, hy⟩⟩
        LemmaCapacity.frac_pos_lt_oneline 141
        /-- A block with a cell that reads 1 and a cell that reads −1 has a fraction of 1s strictly
between 0 and 1: the converse of `two_le_card_of_frac`. -/
lemma frac_pos_lt_one (b : Cell → Bool) (B : Finset Cell) {x y : Cell} (hx : x ∈ B)
    (hbx : b x = true) (hy : y ∈ B) (hby : b y = false) : 0 < frac b B ∧ frac b B < 1 := by
  have hB : (0 : ℝ) < B.card := by exact_mod_cast Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨x, hx⟩
  have hpos : 0 < (B.filter (fun z => b z = true)).card :=
    Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨x, Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨hx, hbx⟩⟩
  have hlt : (B.filter (fun z => b z = true)).card < B.card :=
    Finset.card_lt_card (Finset.filter_ssubset.2 ⟨y, hy, by simp [hby]⟩)
  unfold frac
  exact ⟨div_pos (by exact_mod_cast hpos) hB, (div_lt_one hB).2 (by exact_mod_cast hlt)⟩
        LemmaCapacity.outcomes_iff_cellsline 153
        /-- **What the premise and a condition on `pr` ask together.**  The ceilings and the results on
codes of `Main.lean` take a function `pr` in two hypotheses.  One is a condition: each outcome
`k` of a set `A` occurs with either value of the bit, `pr k v > 0`.  The other is the premise
`Sources.P1.outcomes_at_positions`: an outcome that occurs with a value of the bit is at a cell
with that value.  Some `pr` meets the two exactly when each outcome of `A` has a cell of either
bit.  In those results `pr` occurs in these two hypotheses only, so no statement says that it is
the probabilities of a state.  The docstrings read it as the probabilities of the state that the
register holds. -/
lemma outcomes_iff_cells {K : Type*} (e : Cell → K) (b : Cell → Bool) (A : Set K) :
    (∃ pr : K → Bool → ℝ, (∀ k ∈ A, 0 < pr k true ∧ 0 < pr k false) ∧
      (∀ k v, 0 < pr k v → ∃ x, e x = k ∧ b x = v)) ↔
    ∀ k ∈ A, (∃ x, e x = k ∧ b x = true) ∧ (∃ y, e y = k ∧ b y = false) := by
  classical
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨pr, hA, hout⟩ k hk
    exact ⟨hout k true (hA k hk).1, hout k false (hA k hk).2⟩
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun k v => if ∃ x, e x = k ∧ b x = v then 1 else 0, fun k hk => ?_, fun k v hkv => ?_⟩
    · simp [(h k hk).1, (h k hk).2]
    · by_contra hno
      simp [hno] at hkv
        TheoremCapacity.one_cell_blockline 175
        /-- **A block of one cell** has the fraction 0 or 1 (Sec. IV.A, Sec. V): a state of the
Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger type needs only blocks of fraction 0 or 1, one cell each, and a string
of `L` blocks of one cell uses all its bits with every fraction 0 or 1. -/
theorem one_cell_block (b : Cell → Bool) (B : Finset Cell) (h : B.card = 1) :
    frac b B = 0 ∨ frac b B = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Finset.card_eq_one.1 h
  unfold frac
  cases hb : b x <;> simp [Finset.filter_singleton, hb]

        
variable [Fintype Cell]
        DefinitionCapacity.blockline 186
        /-- the block with the label `σ`: the cells of the later string on which the earlier qubits show
an outcome (`e`) whose label (`s`) is `σ`; with `s` the identity it is the paper's block of the
joint outcome `σ` -/
def block {K S : Type*} [DecidableEq S] (e : Cell → K) (s : K → S) (σ : S) : Finset Cell :=
  univ.filter (fun x => s (e x) = σ)
        LemmaCapacity.disjoint_blocksline 192
        /-- Different labels have disjoint blocks. -/
lemma disjoint_blocks {K S : Type*} [DecidableEq S] (e : Cell → K) (s : K → S) {σ τ : S}
    (h : σ ≠ τ) : Disjoint (block e s σ) (block e s τ) := by
  rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
  intro x hx hx'
  simp only [block, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and] at hx hx'
  exact h (hx.symm.trans hx')
        TheoremCapacity.ceiling_softline 200
        /-- **The ceiling if each block needs `r` cells** (Sec. V): a block of `r` cells resolves the last
qubit's conditional probability and phase to one part in `r`.  With `2^(N−1)` joint outcomes of
the earlier qubits, each with a block of at least `r` cells, a string of `L` cells gives
`2^(N−1) r ≤ L`, that is `N ≤ log₂(2L/r)`. -/
theorem ceiling_soft {S : Type*} [DecidableEq S] (N L r : ℕ) (hL : Fintype.card Cell = L)
    (e : Cell → Fin (2 ^ (N - 1))) (s : Fin (2 ^ (N - 1)) → S) (hs : Function.Injective s)
    (hr : ∀ k, r ≤ (block e s (s k)).card) :
    2 ^ (N - 1) * r ≤ L := by
  classical
  have hdisj : ((univ : Finset (Fin (2 ^ (N - 1)))) : Set (Fin (2 ^ (N - 1)))).PairwiseDisjoint
      (fun k => block e s (s k)) := by
    intro k _ k' _ hkk'
    exact disjoint_blocks e s (hs.ne hkk')
  have hcard := card_le_card (subset_univ ((univ : Finset (Fin (2 ^ (N - 1)))).biUnion
    (fun k => block e s (s k))))
  rw [card_biUnion hdisj, card_univ, hL] at hcard
  have h := card_nsmul_le_sum (univ : Finset (Fin (2 ^ (N - 1)))) (fun k => (block e s (s k)).card)
    r (fun k _ => hr k)
  simp only [card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul] at h
  omega
        TheoremCapacity.ceilingline 221
        /-- **The ceiling**, Eq. (nmax) (Sec. IV.A).  Measure a state of `N` qubits jointly; let `e` give
the joint outcome of the first `N − 1` qubits that each cell of the last string shows, `s` an
injective labeling of the outcomes, and `b` the last string's bits.  When each of the `2^(N−1)`
joint outcomes occurs with the last qubit's bit given it at a probability strictly between 0 and 1,
as in a random state and in a product state of superposed qubits, each block has a fraction of 1s
strictly between 0 and 1.  Each block then needs at least two cells, and the string of `L` cells has
room for them only if `2^N ≤ L`. -/
theorem ceiling {S : Type*} [DecidableEq S] (N L : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hL : Fintype.card Cell = L)
    (e : Cell → Fin (2 ^ (N - 1))) (s : Fin (2 ^ (N - 1)) → S) (hs : Function.Injective s)
    (b : Cell → Bool)
    (hrandom : ∀ k, 0 < frac b (block e s (s k)) ∧ frac b (block e s (s k)) < 1) :
    2 ^ N ≤ L := by
  have h := ceiling_soft N L 2 hL e s hs
    (fun k => (two_le_card_of_frac b (block e s (s k)) (hrandom k).1 (hrandom k).2).1)
  have e2 : 2 ^ (N - 1) * 2 = 2 ^ N := by
    rw [← pow_succ]
    congr 1
    omega
  rwa [e2] at h
        TheoremCapacity.ceiling_by_outcomeline 241
        /-- **The ceiling with the paper's blocks** (Sec. IV.A): the blocks are indexed by joint outcome
(`s` the identity), `block e id k` being the cells of the last string paired with the outcome
`k`.  When every joint outcome occurs with the last qubit's bit given it at a probability strictly
between 0 and 1, `2^N ≤ L`.  A random state is such a state; so is a product state of `N` qubits
each in a superposition, whose `2^(N−1)` conditional probabilities all equal the last qubit's own:
the bound holds for every state in which all `2^N` joint outcomes occur.  No sample shows which
outcomes are missing (Sec. IV.A); what sets the random state apart is that its last qubit has a
different conditional state for each joint outcome of the others, so that its string has too few
cells to hold them all once `2^N > L`, where a product state's string has one conditional state to
hold.  A linear cluster state followed by one layer of generic single-qubit rotations has as many
conditional states as a random state (`Cluster.chain_card`), and the paper derives the same limit
for it (Sec. IV.A). -/
theorem ceiling_by_outcome (N L : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hL : Fintype.card Cell = L)
    (e : Cell → Fin (2 ^ (N - 1))) (b : Cell → Bool)
    (hall : ∀ k, 0 < frac b (block e id k) ∧ frac b (block e id k) < 1) :
    2 ^ N ≤ L :=
  ceiling N L hN hL e id Function.injective_id b hall
        TheoremCapacity.ceiling_logicalline 259
        /-- **The ceiling for logical qubits** (Sec. IV.A).  A string whose cells fall into `2^N` blocks,
each with a fraction of 1s strictly between 0 and 1, needs two cells for each block, so
`2^(N+1) ≤ L` (`ceiling_by_outcome` at `N + 1`).  In a Calderbank–Shor–Steane code a physical bit,
given the earlier physical bits, is fixed, balanced, or equal or opposite to the logical bit.  Where
the equal and the opposite case both occur, as for the last bit of a line in the surface code, the
fullest physical string of a random state of `N` logical qubits has a conditional state for each
joint outcome of the earlier logical qubits and each case, `2^N` in all, twice as many as a logical
string, each held on a block of its own, and no physical string has more conditional states to hold,
which the files prove with the blocks read in order.
`Coding.lean` proves that step (`Coding.css_conditional_joint`, `Coding.LineCode.jointBitGiven_rest`,
`Coding.card_condStates_le`, `Coding.LineCode.card_lineStates`) and the count with blocks by
conditional state (`Coding.two_mul_card_states_le`, `Coding.ceiling_both_cases`,
`Coding.ceiling_line_code`); `Numerics.logical_ceiling_cos` gives `203` logical qubits at
`L_cos`. -/
theorem ceiling_logical (N L : ℕ) (hL : Fintype.card Cell = L)
    (e : Cell → Fin (2 ^ N)) (b : Cell → Bool)
    (hall : ∀ k, 0 < frac b (block e id k) ∧ frac b (block e id k) < 1) :
    2 ^ (N + 1) ≤ L :=
  ceiling_by_outcome (N + 1) L (by omega) hL e b hall
        DefinitionCapacity.jointOutcomeline 279
        /-- **Strings read in step** (Sec. IV.A, how "measured jointly" is read).  A joint measurement is
one measurement, so its possible outcomes are the positions, each one among the `L`, the same on
every string of the qubits it measures, since the shift carries every string one cell per tick and
keeps them in step (Postulate 1); the outcome at a position is the bits there.  So the joint outcome of the first `N − 1` qubits that a position `x` of the last string shows is
their bits at `x`.  Here `bits i` is the string of the `i`-th qubit, indexed by the common
positions. -/
def jointOutcome {N : ℕ} (bits : Fin N → Cell → Bool) (x : Cell) : Fin (N - 1) → Bool :=
  fun i => bits (Fin.castLE (Nat.sub_le N 1) i) x
        TheoremCapacity.ceiling_in_stepline 288
        /-- **The ceiling for strings read in step** (Sec. IV.A), Eq. (nmax).  With the pairing of
`jointOutcome`, the bits of the strings at one position, the block of a joint outcome `ω` is the
set of positions at which the first `N − 1` strings show `ω`.  When every `ω` occurs with the last
qubit's bit given it at a probability strictly between 0 and 1, `2^N ≤ L`: `ceiling_by_outcome`
with the pairing supplied by the strings, no function chosen. -/
theorem ceiling_in_step (N L : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hL : Fintype.card Cell = L)
    (bits : Fin N → Cell → Bool)
    (hall : ∀ ω : Fin (N - 1) → Bool,
      0 < frac (bits ⟨N - 1, by omega⟩) (univ.filter (fun x => jointOutcome bits x = ω)) ∧
      frac (bits ⟨N - 1, by omega⟩) (univ.filter (fun x => jointOutcome bits x = ω)) < 1) :
    2 ^ N ≤ L := by
  have hcard : Fintype.card (Fin (N - 1) → Bool) = 2 ^ (N - 1) := by
    rw [Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_bool, Fintype.card_fin]
  let φ : (Fin (N - 1) → Bool) ≃ Fin (2 ^ (N - 1)) := Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq hcard
  refine ceiling_by_outcome N L hN hL (fun x => φ (jointOutcome bits x)) (bits ⟨N - 1, by omega⟩)
    (fun k => ?_)
  have hb : block (fun x => φ (jointOutcome bits x)) id k
      = univ.filter (fun x => jointOutcome bits x = φ.symm k) := by
    ext x
    simp only [block, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, id, ← Equiv.eq_symm_apply]
  rw [hb]
  exact hall (φ.symm k)
        TheoremCapacity.share_readline 311
        /-- **The outcome is the bit of a cell of a set with the probability of the set's share of the
cells** (Secs. IV.A, IV.C): each cell's bit is one possible outcome among the `L` (Postulate 1,
`halike`), so the outcome is the bit of a cell of `A` with the probability `|A|/L`. -/
theorem share_read (q : Cell → ℝ) (halike : ∀ x, q x = 1 / Fintype.card Cell)
    (A : Finset Cell) : ∑ x ∈ A, q x = A.card / Fintype.card Cell := by
  rw [sum_congr rfl (fun x _ => halike x), sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
  ring
        DefinitionCapacity.condProbline 319
        /-- **The probability of the outcome `1` given a block** (Sec. IV.A): with `q x` the probability
that the outcome is the bit of the cell `x`, the probability that the outcome is the bit of a cell
of the block `B` that reads `1`, over the probability that it is the bit of a cell of `B`. -/
noncomputable def condProb (q : Cell → ℝ) (b : Cell → Bool) (B : Finset Cell) : ℝ :=
  (∑ x ∈ B.filter (fun x => b x = true), q x) / (∑ x ∈ B, q x)
        TheoremCapacity.block_fraction_readline 325
        /-- **A block's fraction is a conditional probability** (Sec. IV.A).  With each cell's bit one
possible outcome among the `L` (`share_read`), the outcome is the bit of a cell of a set `B` with
the probability `|B|/L`, and of a cell of `B` with the bit `1` with the probability of the cells of
`B` that show `1`.  So, given that it is the bit of a cell of `B`, it is `1` with the probability
`frac b B`, the fraction of 1s on `B` (for an empty block both sides are `0`, by Lean's
`x/0 = 0`, and the probability given the block is not defined).  For the block of a
joint outcome this is the probability of the last qubit's outcome `1` given that joint outcome,
which the ceiling theorems take as the block's fraction (`frac` in `hrandom` and `hall`; `hshare`
of the theorems of `Coding.lean`). -/
theorem block_fraction_read (q : Cell → ℝ)
    (halike : ∀ x, q x = 1 / Fintype.card Cell) (b : Cell → Bool) (B : Finset Cell) :
    condProb q b B = frac b B := by
  unfold condProb
  rcases B.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | hB
  · simp [frac]
  rw [share_read q halike, share_read q halike]
  have hc : (Fintype.card Cell : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    obtain ⟨x, -⟩ := hB
    have : 0 < Fintype.card Cell := Fintype.card_pos_iff.2 ⟨x⟩
    exact_mod_cast this.ne'
  have hB' : (B.card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hB.card_pos.ne'
  unfold frac
  field_simp
        TheoremCapacity.nmax_iffline 349
        /-- **The largest `N` with `2^N ≤ L`**: when `2^N₀ ≤ L < 2^(N₀+1)`, `2^N ≤ L` exactly when
`N ≤ N₀`, so `N_max = ⌊log₂ L⌋ = N₀`. -/
theorem nmax_iff {L : ℝ} (N₀ : ℕ) (h1 : (2 : ℝ) ^ N₀ ≤ L) (h2 : L < 2 ^ (N₀ + 1)) (N : ℕ) :
    (2 : ℝ) ^ N ≤ L ↔ N ≤ N₀ := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hN
    have : (2 : ℝ) ^ (N₀ + 1) ≤ 2 ^ N := pow_le_pow_right₀ (by norm_num) (by omega)
    linarith
  · intro hN
    have : (2 : ℝ) ^ N ≤ 2 ^ N₀ := pow_le_pow_right₀ (by norm_num) hN
    linarith
        LemmaCapacity.palmer_stepline 362
        /-- The step of Palmer's bit count: with `u(N) = 2^(N+1) − 2 − NL`, `u(N+1) ≥ 2u(N) + 2` for
`N ≥ 1`. -/
lemma palmer_step (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    2 * ((2 : ℝ) ^ (N + 1) - 2 - N * L) + 2 ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (N + 1 + 1) - 2 - ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * L := by
  have hN' : (1 : ℝ) ≤ N := by exact_mod_cast hN
  have e : (2 : ℝ) ^ (N + 1 + 1) = 2 * 2 ^ (N + 1) := by ring
  rw [e]
  push_cast
  nlinarith
        TheoremCapacity.palmer_thresholdline 372
        /-- **Palmer's bit count** `2^(N+1) − 2 ≤ NL` (Sec. V): if it holds at `N₀ ≥ 1` and fails at
`N₀ + 1`, it holds exactly for `N ≤ N₀`.  Above `N₀` doubling keeps it failing, and below `N₀`
halving keeps it holding (`palmer_step`). -/
theorem palmer_threshold (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L) (N₀ : ℕ) (hN₀ : 1 ≤ N₀)
    (hyes : (2 : ℝ) ^ (N₀ + 1) - 2 ≤ N₀ * L)
    (hno : ((N₀ + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * L < 2 ^ (N₀ + 1 + 1) - 2) (N : ℕ) :
    (2 : ℝ) ^ (N + 1) - 2 ≤ N * L ↔ N ≤ N₀ := by
  -- above `N₀` it fails
  have up : ∀ k : ℕ, ((N₀ + 1 + k : ℕ) : ℝ) * L < 2 ^ (N₀ + 1 + k + 1) - 2 := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero => simpa using hno
    | succ k ih =>
      have hs := palmer_step L hL (N₀ + 1 + k) (by omega)
      have e : N₀ + 1 + (k + 1) = N₀ + 1 + k + 1 := by ring
      rw [e]
      linarith
  -- at and below `N₀`, down to `1`, it holds
  have down : ∀ k N : ℕ, N + k = N₀ → 1 ≤ N → (2 : ℝ) ^ (N + 1) - 2 ≤ N * L := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero => intro N hN _; rw [add_zero] at hN; rw [hN]; exact hyes
    | succ k ih =>
      intro N hN h1
      have hnext := ih (N + 1) (by omega) (by omega)
      have hs := palmer_step L hL N h1
      push_cast at hnext hs
      linarith
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hN
    obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ : ∃ k, N = N₀ + 1 + k := ⟨N - (N₀ + 1), by omega⟩
    have := up k
    linarith
  · intro hN
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos N with h0 | h0
    · subst h0; norm_num
    · exact down (N₀ - N) N (by omega) h0

        import RegisterGravity.Capacity
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.BigOperators
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Field
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Sigma
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fintype
import Mathlib.Order.Interval.Finset.Nat
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.Positivity
import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Ring.Finset
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.Arg
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Intervals

/-!
# The pairing of strings measured jointly (Sec. IV.A)

Formal counterpart of the sentences of Sec. IV.A on what the register holds for a state of
several qubits, and of the overlap bound above the ceiling.

A joint measurement is one measurement, so its possible outcomes are the positions, the same on
every string of the qubits it measures, and the outcome at a position is the bits there
(Postulate 1, Sec. IV.A).  A *pairing* is a function `e` from the positions, the cells of the type
`Cell`, to the joint outcomes: `e x` is the joint outcome at the position `x`.  Each position is
one possible outcome among the ring's (`Sources.P1.ring_bits_alike`), and the probability of a set
of outcomes is the sum of theirs, so the probability of a joint outcome is the share of the
positions that show it, `freq e k` (`Main.joint_frequency` states this from the premise).  What
follows is counting.  The number of the positions is the number of the ring's cells, written `L`
in the comments: it is `L` on a largest ring, and a result of `Main.lean` that needs the bound
takes it as a premise.

* `freq_multiple`: every joint frequency that a pairing shows is a multiple of `1/L`.
* `shown_le_cells`: "no pairing of `L` positions shows more than `L` joint outcomes".
* `sum_freq`: the frequencies of a pairing sum to one.
* `shown_exactly_iff`: a pairing shows every joint outcome with its probability exactly when
  every probability is a multiple of `1/L` and the multiples sum to `L`.
* `jointPhase`, `state_of_strings`: "Where a pairing shows every joint outcome with its frequency,
  the strings in that pairing, with their blocks' phases, are the state".  A state whose
  probabilities are the frequencies of `N` strings read in step is, up to its global phase, those
  frequencies with one phase on each block of each string.
* `pairing_misses`: where more than `L` joint outcomes occur, every pairing gives one of them the
  frequency zero, so the pairing is approximate ("even where the joint outcomes of its physical
  qubits outnumber `L`").
* `product_multiple_iff`, `product_not_shown`: "two qubits prepared apart, with the fractions
  `m₁/L` and `m₂/L`, have the joint frequency `m₁m₂/L²` for the outcome `(1,1)`, a multiple of
  `1/L` only when `L` divides `m₁m₂`".
* `most_products_not_shown`: "Most product states are not held exactly": for a first qubit in a
  superposition, the fractions of a second one for which `L` does not divide `m₁m₂` outnumber
  those for which it does.
* `pairing_within_one_cell`: two strings, each fixed, have a pairing that shows the outcome
  `(1,1)` within one cell of the product of their fractions, `1/L` in frequency, and exactly
  where `L` divides `m₁m₂` ("held with its strings exact and its pairing approximate").  A
  pairing of two strings is a one-to-one map `π` of the positions: the cell `x` of the first is
  read with the cell `π x` of the second.  Each string is a fixed set of cells, so it keeps its
  bits where they are, its fraction and its cyclic position, in every pairing; the map `π` alone
  varies.
* `pairing_not_fixed`: the strings do not fix the pairing: two strings, each in a superposition,
  have two pairings that show the outcome `(1,1)` at different numbers of positions ("the
  postulates do not say which pairing").
* `strings_in_step`: `N` strings read in step show joint frequencies that are multiples of `1/L`
  and sum to one, and the frequency of `1` on each string is that string's own fraction, in every
  pairing ("`N` exact strings read in step, in some pairing, with a phase on each block").  Here
  `bits i x` is the bit that the string `i` shows at the position `x` of the pairing: the string
  as the pairing reads it.
* `blockOf`, `freq_chain`: "the probability of a joint outcome is the product, string by string,
  of the frequencies of its bits on its blocks".
* `BlockPhase`, `block_resolution`: a block of `r` cells holds a conditional probability that
  is a multiple of `1/r` and a phase that is one of `r` cyclic positions (Secs. IV.A and V).
* `sample_outcomes_le`: a sample of `n` shots shows at most `n` outcomes.
* `overlap_le`: a state that gives the outcomes outside a set the probability zero overlaps
  another state by at most the probability that the other gives the outcomes of the set
  (Sec. IV.A: "its overlap with the random state is at most the probability that the random state
  gives the outcomes that remain").  `Main.overlap_bound` states it for what the register holds.

As in `Capacity.lean`, the bit `true` is the outcome `1` and `false` the outcome `−1`, and a string
is given by its bits, or by the set of its cells that read `1`.
-/

open Finset

namespace Register
namespace Pairing

variable {Cell : Type*} [Fintype Cell]
        DefinitionPairing.freqline 88
        /-- **The frequency of a joint outcome in a pairing** (Sec. IV.A): the share of the positions `x`
at which the pairing `e` shows the joint outcome `k`, their number over the number `L` of the
positions. -/
noncomputable def freq {K : Type*} [DecidableEq K] (e : Cell → K) (k : K) : ℝ :=
  ((univ.filter (fun x => e x = k)).card : ℝ) / Fintype.card Cell

        /-- **Every joint frequency is a multiple of `1/L`** (Sec. IV.A): a pairing of `L` positions shows

theorem block_resolution {Cell : Type*} (b : Cell → Bool) (B : Finset Cell) :
    (∃ k : ℕ, k ≤ B.card ∧ Capacity.frac b B = k / B.card) ∧

def before {N : ℕ} (i : ℕ) (σ : Fin N → Bool) : Fin N → Bool :=
  fun j => if j.val < i then σ j else true
        DefinitionPairing.jointPhaseline 561
        /-- **The phase of a joint outcome, from the blocks' phases** (Sec. IV.A: "The block's phase
(above) is the later qubit's phase given that outcome").  `φ i τ` is the phase on the block of the
string `i` that is paired with the joint outcome of the earlier strings in `τ`: the phase of the
qubit `i` given that outcome, which its amplitude carries where it reads `−1`.  The phase of the
joint outcome `σ` is the sum of these over the strings that read `−1` in `σ`; the block of the
string `i` is read off the earlier bits of `σ` alone (`before`). -/
noncomputable def jointPhase {N : ℕ} (φ : Fin N → (Fin N → Bool) → ℝ) (σ : Fin N → Bool) : ℝ :=

        Statement of the paperPairing.state_of_stringsline 570
        /-- **The strings in a pairing, with their blocks' phases, are the state** (Sec. IV.A: "Where a
pairing shows every joint outcome with its frequency, the strings in that pairing, with their
blocks' phases, are the state").  `ψ` is a state of `N` qubits, and the `N` strings read in step

such that the amplitude of every joint outcome is the square root of its frequency times the
phase that the blocks give it (`jointPhase`).  A block of `r` cells holds one of `r` phases
(`block_resolution`); the phases here are real numbers. -/

    rw [hθ σ]

theorem overlap_le {K : Type*} [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] (φ ψ : K → ℂ) (S : Finset K)
