        /-- the probability that the string on ring `l` has the sense `b`, under the joint distribution `P`
of all the strings' senses -/
def marginal (P : (ι → Bool) → ℝ) (l : ι) (b : Bool) : ℝ :=
  ∑ ω : ι → Bool, if ω l = b then P ω else 0
        DefinitionEntropy.othersProbline 81
        /-- the probability that the strings other than the one on ring `l` have the senses of `ω`, the
string on `l` having either sense -/
def othersProb (P : (ι → Bool) → ℝ) (l : ι) (ω : ι → Bool) : ℝ :=
  ∑ b : Bool, P (Function.update ω l b)
        DefinitionEntropy.correlationline 86
        /-- **The correlation of a string with the other strings**: the joint distribution of the strings'
senses less the product of the string's own distribution and that of the others.  It is zero at
every joint sense exactly when the string's sense is independent of the others'. -/
def correlation (P : (ι → Bool) → ℝ) (l : ι) (ω : ι → Bool) : ℝ :=
  P ω - marginal P l (ω l) * othersProb P l ω
        TheoremEntropy.correlation_jointProbline 92
        /-- **Free strings are uncorrelated**: under the joint distribution of independent strings
(`jointProb`), each string's own distribution is its factor, the others' is the product of
theirs, and every string's correlation with the others is zero. -/
theorem correlation_jointProb (p : ι → ℝ) (l : ι) (ω : ι → Bool) :
    correlation (jointProb p) l ω = 0 := by
  -- the string's own distribution
  have hm : marginal (jointProb p) l (ω l) = senseProb p l (ω l) := by
    have h := sum_jointProb_mul p l (fun b => if b = ω l then (1 : ℝ) else 0)
    simp only [mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero] at h
    unfold marginal
    rw [h]
    simp
  -- the others' distribution
  have ho : othersProb (jointProb p) l ω = ∏ k ∈ univ.erase l, senseProb p k (ω k) := by
    unfold othersProb jointProb
    have e : ∀ b, ∏ k, senseProb p k (Function.update ω l b k) =
        senseProb p l b * ∏ k ∈ univ.erase l, senseProb p k (ω k) := by
      intro b
      rw [← mul_prod_erase univ (fun k => senseProb p k (Function.update ω l b k)) (mem_univ l),
        Function.update_self]
      congr 1
      exact prod_congr rfl fun k hk => by rw [Function.update_of_ne (mem_erase.1 hk).1]
    simp_rw [e]
    rw [← sum_mul, sum_senseProb, one_mul]
  unfold correlation
  rw [hm, ho]
  unfold jointProb
  rw [← mul_prod_erase univ (fun k => senseProb p k (ω k)) (mem_univ l), sub_self]
        TheoremEntropy.shannon_jointProbline 121
        /-- **The entropy of independent strings adds** (known mathematics): the Shannon entropy of the
joint distribution of the strings' senses, the strings independent, is the sum of the binary
entropies of the strings.  The identity holds for any real weights `p l`; for `0 ≤ p l ≤ 1` the
joint distribution is a probability distribution. -/
theorem shannon_jointProb (p : ι → ℝ) :
    shannon (jointProb p) = ∑ l, Real.binEntropy (p l) := by
  -- the entropy of each joint sense splits over the rings
  have hsplit : ∀ ω : ι → Bool, Real.negMulLog (jointProb p ω) =
      ∑ l, jointProb p ω * (-Real.log (senseProb p l (ω l))) := by
    intro ω
    by_cases h0 : ∀ l, senseProb p l (ω l) ≠ 0
    · unfold jointProb Real.negMulLog
      rw [Real.log_prod (fun l _ => h0 l), mul_sum]
      exact sum_congr rfl fun l _ => by ring
    · push Not at h0
      obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := h0
      have hz : jointProb p ω = 0 := by
        unfold jointProb
        exact prod_eq_zero (mem_univ l) hl
      simp [hz]
  unfold shannon
  simp_rw [hsplit]
  rw [sum_comm]
  refine sum_congr rfl fun l _ => ?_
  rw [sum_jointProb_mul p l (fun b => -Real.log (senseProb p l b))]
  rw [Fintype.sum_bool]
  simp only [senseProb, Bool.false_eq_true, ite_true, ite_false]
  rw [Real.binEntropy_eq_negMulLog_add_negMulLog_one_sub]
  unfold Real.negMulLog
  ring

        
/-! ### The thermal distribution derived: the distribution of most entropy over the
distinguishable configurations (thermodynamics as mathematics; Sec. IV.E) -/
        DefinitionEntropy.gibbsline 155
        /-- **The Gibbs distribution** on a finite set `Ω` of distinguishable configurations with energies
`E`, at the inverse temperature `β`: `e^{−βE}` over its sum. -/
noncomputable def gibbs {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] (E : Ω → ℝ) (β : ℝ) (ω : Ω) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp (-β * E ω) / ∑ ω', Real.exp (-β * E ω')
        LemmaEntropy.sum_exp_posline 160
        /-- the sum of the Boltzmann factors is positive -/
lemma sum_exp_pos {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω] (E : Ω → ℝ) (β : ℝ) :
    0 < ∑ ω, Real.exp (-β * E ω) :=
  sum_pos (fun _ _ => Real.exp_pos _) univ_nonempty
        LemmaEntropy.gibbs_posline 165
        /-- every configuration has positive weight -/
lemma gibbs_pos {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω] (E : Ω → ℝ) (β : ℝ) (ω : Ω) :
    0 < gibbs E β ω :=
  div_pos (Real.exp_pos _) (sum_exp_pos E β)
        LemmaEntropy.sum_gibbsline 170
        /-- the Gibbs distribution sums to one -/
lemma sum_gibbs {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω] (E : Ω → ℝ) (β : ℝ) :
    ∑ ω, gibbs E β ω = 1 := by
  unfold gibbs
  rw [← sum_div, div_self (sum_exp_pos E β).ne']
        LemmaEntropy.log_gibbsline 176
        /-- the logarithm of a Gibbs weight -/
lemma log_gibbs {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω] (E : Ω → ℝ) (β : ℝ) (ω : Ω) :
    Real.log (gibbs E β ω) = -β * E ω - Real.log (∑ ω', Real.exp (-β * E ω')) := by
  unfold gibbs
  rw [Real.log_div (Real.exp_pos _).ne' (sum_exp_pos E β).ne', Real.log_exp]
        LemmaEntropy.negMulLog_add_mul_log_leline 182
        /-- **Gibbs' inequality**, one configuration at a time: for `0 ≤ p` and `0 < q`,
`−p log p + p log q ≤ q − p`. -/
lemma negMulLog_add_mul_log_le {p q : ℝ} (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hq : 0 < q) :
    Real.negMulLog p + p * Real.log q ≤ q - p := by
  rcases hp.lt_or_eq with hp' | rfl
  · unfold Real.negMulLog
    have h1 : Real.log (q / p) ≤ q / p - 1 := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (div_pos hq hp')
    rw [Real.log_div hq.ne' hp'.ne'] at h1
    have h2 : p * (Real.log q - Real.log p) ≤ p * (q / p - 1) :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h1 hp'.le
    have h3 : p * (q / p - 1) = q - p := by field_simp
    rw [h3] at h2
    linarith
  · simp [Real.negMulLog]; exact hq.le
        TheoremEntropy.shannon_le_shannon_gibbsline 197
        /-- **Of all distributions on the distinguishable configurations with a given mean energy, the
Gibbs distribution has the most entropy** (thermodynamics as mathematics; Sec. IV.E).  Let
`P` be a distribution on `Ω` whose mean energy is that of the Gibbs distribution at `β`.  Then the
Shannon entropy of `P` is at most that of the Gibbs distribution: by Gibbs' inequality
(`negMulLog_add_mul_log_le`), `−Σ P log P ≤ −Σ P log g`, and `−log g = βE + log Z` is linear in
the energy, so the right side is `β` times the mean energy plus `log Z`, which is the entropy of
`g` itself.  So the thermal state of a system in equilibrium at a temperature, the Gibbs state, is
the distribution of most entropy over its distinguishable configurations at its mean energy, and
nothing else: this is what "Thermodynamics distributes a system over its distinguishable
configurations" says (Sec. IV.E).
For a free string the distinguishable configurations are the two outcomes of its qubit, its two
senses, with one energy (`hsense` of `Qubit.Tick`), and the Gibbs distribution on them is
`1/2, 1/2` (`Qubit.Tick.state_eq`): one bit, and the string's one energy, at every temperature.  The
hidden global phase is no configuration, since no law depends on it (Postulate 1), so it carries
neither entropy nor a distribution. -/
theorem shannon_le_shannon_gibbs {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω] (E : Ω → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
    (P : Ω → ℝ) (hP : ∀ ω, 0 ≤ P ω) (hPsum : ∑ ω, P ω = 1)
    (hmean : ∑ ω, P ω * E ω = ∑ ω, gibbs E β ω * E ω) :
    shannon P ≤ shannon (gibbs E β) := by
  set Z := ∑ ω', Real.exp (-β * E ω') with hZ
  -- Gibbs' inequality, summed
  have hG : ∑ ω, (Real.negMulLog (P ω) + P ω * Real.log (gibbs E β ω)) ≤ 0 := by
    calc ∑ ω, (Real.negMulLog (P ω) + P ω * Real.log (gibbs E β ω))
        ≤ ∑ ω, (gibbs E β ω - P ω) :=
          sum_le_sum fun ω _ => negMulLog_add_mul_log_le (hP ω) (gibbs_pos E β ω)
      _ = 0 := by rw [sum_sub_distrib, sum_gibbs, hPsum, sub_self]
  -- `−Σ P log g = β ⟨E⟩_P + log Z`
  have hlin : ∀ Q : Ω → ℝ, ∑ ω, Q ω = 1 →
      -∑ ω, Q ω * Real.log (gibbs E β ω) = β * ∑ ω, Q ω * E ω + Real.log Z := by
    intro Q hQ
    simp_rw [log_gibbs]
    rw [← hZ]
    have : ∑ ω, Q ω * (-β * E ω - Real.log Z) = -β * ∑ ω, Q ω * E ω - Real.log Z * ∑ ω, Q ω := by
      rw [mul_sum, mul_sum]
      rw [← sum_sub_distrib]
      exact sum_congr rfl fun ω _ => by ring
    rw [this, hQ]
    ring
  -- the entropy of the Gibbs distribution is `β ⟨E⟩_g + log Z`
  have hg : shannon (gibbs E β) = β * ∑ ω, gibbs E β ω * E ω + Real.log Z := by
    rw [← hlin _ (sum_gibbs E β)]
    unfold shannon Real.negMulLog
    rw [← sum_neg_distrib]
    exact sum_congr rfl fun ω _ => by ring
  have hP' : shannon P ≤ -∑ ω, P ω * Real.log (gibbs E β ω) := by
    unfold shannon
    rw [sum_add_distrib] at hG
    linarith
  rw [hlin P hPsum, hmean, ← hg] at hP'
  exact hP'
        TheoremEntropy.gibbs_two_equalline 248
        /-- **Two distinguishable configurations of one energy are weighted alike at every temperature**
(Secs. II and IV.E): the Gibbs distribution on a free string's two senses, which have one energy
(`hsense` of `Qubit.Tick`), is `1/2, 1/2`, whatever `β`; so the string holds one bit, whatever its
one energy (`Qubit.Tick.state_eq` is the same statement for
the qubit's density matrix). -/
theorem gibbs_two_equal (E : Bool → ℝ) (β : ℝ) (hE : E true = E false) (b : Bool) :
    gibbs E β b = 1 / 2 := by
  unfold gibbs
  rw [Fintype.sum_bool, hE]
  have h : 0 < Real.exp (-β * E false) := Real.exp_pos _
  have key : Real.exp (-β * E false) / (Real.exp (-β * E false) + Real.exp (-β * E false)) =
      1 / 2 := by
    field_simp
    ring
  cases b
  · exact key
  · rw [hE]; exact key

/-!
# The qubit of a free string (Secs. II and IV.E)

Postulate 1 makes quantum mechanics granular: a string is one qubit, and its state is given up to a
global phase.  This file holds the small part of the quantum mechanics of one qubit that the paper
uses, so that the steps below are theorems and not premises argued in words.  What it takes of
quantum mechanics is in the words of the postulates and of Sec. II's definitions: a state is a
linear combination of outcomes of its
qubits (Postulate 1), so a qubit's states are the vectors over its two outcomes and a tick is a
linear map on them (`Vec`, `Op`); the bits are the possible outcomes of one measurement, so the
probability of an outcome is its share of the bits (Postulate 1; with Eqs. (qubit) and (raqm), `stringState`); and
the tick of a state of energy `E` is the factor `e^{−iEt_c/ℏ}`, by Sec. II's definition of energy
(`Sources.P1.string_energies`, a premise of `Main.string_energy`, not a definition of this file:
the strings' mean energy comes from the Gibbs distribution at the horizon's temperature,
Sec. IV.E, and the definition then gives the factor of a tick of that energy, `e^{−i/L}`).  That a tick is a linear map
on the states (`Op`) is Sec. II's "The tick is linear, since a state is a linear combination of
outcomes (Postulate 1)", with the qubit a two-level quantum system by Sec. II's definition; it is
what carries one factor from the two senses to every superposition of them.  `L ≠ 0` is assumed where a ring's
length enters a bound (`[NeZero L]`).

**The two outcomes, and what a free tick does** (the paper's Sec. II, "The entropy"; these are the
paper's statements, and the fields below take of them only what they say): the shift of
Postulate 1 is a translation along the ring, and a translation along a ring can go two ways, with
the ring or against it, the two senses.  Reading which sense a string has is a measurement with two
values, and the string's bits are its possible outcomes: by the definition of the bit values, `e₁`
is the outcome `1`, the string of all 1s, the sense with the ring, and `e₂` the outcome `−1`, the
string of all −1s, the sense against it (the register paper's doublet).  A string
is one qubit (Postulate 1), two outcomes and a phase, its cyclic position being the phase: it has
no further states; a moving string's further states, its momentum, are the register paper's larger
model and are not used here.  A string with `m` 1s is a superposition of the two
senses, `m/L` the probability of the first (Eq. (raqm)), and its cyclic position, the qubit's phase
(Postulate 1), is the relative phase of the two.  A string of one sense has the same bit on every
cell, so the shift leaves it as it is up to its global phase, and that phase changes alike in
either sense (`hsense`, the sentence as written): no bit moves, and the one thing that changes
from tick to tick is the global phase common to both senses (`Tick.phase_unique`).  Read instead
as a pattern of bits that the tick moves one cell, "the string's cyclic position on its ring is the
qubit's phase" would turn the phase by one cell per tick, `U ∝ diag(1, e^{2πi/L})`, the tick of earlier
versions, which `hsense` excludes.

* `Tick`: the free tick on the qubit, one sentence of the paper taken once, in its words.
  Sec. II: "A string of one sense has the same bit on every cell, so the shift leaves it as it is,
  up to its global phase (Postulate 1), and that phase changes alike in either sense, since no law
  depends on the ring's direction (Postulate 2)": the tick keeps each of the two strings of one
  sense up to one and the same phase (`hsense`).  A global phase is a factor `e^{iγ}` on all the
  amplitudes (Sec. II's definition), so the factor has modulus one: the field says of it what the
  sentence says, and no more.
* `Tick.phase_unique`: the tick is a linear map on the states (quantum mechanics; a state is a
  linear combination of the outcomes, Postulate 1), so with one factor on both senses it is
  diagonal in them (`eq_diagonal_of_keeps`) with that factor on both, `U = c • 1`.  The energy is
  then the same for every state of the string, so it adds no state (Sec. IV.E), and no relative
  phase of the two senses turns under the free tick.
* `Tick.norm_scalar`: the factor is a phase, `‖c‖ = 1`, the phase of `hsense`.
* `Tick.ofPhase`: the tick of factor `e^{−iθ}` on every state, for any angle `θ`; it meets
  `hsense`, so the free tick of a string of any energy exists (`Reg.string_tick` gives the factor
  of a string of energy `k_BT_dS`, `e^{−i/L}`, from Sec. II's definition of energy).  The tick fixes its
  factor and nothing more: a phase is defined only up to whole turns, so the factor alone does not
  fix an energy, and the files fix none; the strings' mean energy comes from the Gibbs
  distribution at the horizon's temperature (Sec. IV.E, `Carriers.string_energy`).
* `Tick.factor`, `Tick.factor_eq`, `Tick.energy`, `Tick.energy_eq`: the tick multiplies the string
  of each sense by a factor (`Tick.mulVec_e₁`, `Tick.mulVec_e₂`), and the two factors are one
  (`hsense`).  Sec. II defines the energy of a state by the factor of its tick, "A state that one
  tick multiplies by `e^{−iΔ}` has energy `ℏΔ/t_c`", so the energy of a string of one
  sense is a function `En` of its factor, which every statement leaves open.  One factor is then
  one energy: the two senses of a free string have one energy, whatever `En` is.
* `thermal_of_equal`, `bornProb_thermal`, `entropy_thermal`: the thermal state of a qubit whose two
  basis states have one energy is half the identity, whatever the temperature.  It gives either
  outcome of any measurement the probability `1/2` (the Born rule, `bornProb`; `prob` reads the
  same probability off the diagonal), and its entropy is one bit, `ln 2`: the sense bit of Sec. II
  is the qubit's bit, one and the same.
* `Tick.state`, `Tick.state_eq`, `Tick.bornProb_state`, `Tick.prob_state`, `Tick.entropy_state`:
  the thermal state of a free string is the Gibbs state over its two senses, each at its energy.
  The definition does not put the two energies equal: `Tick.state_eq` derives from
  `Tick.energy_eq` that the state is half the identity, so that the string holds one bit
  (`Main.string_one_bit`).  `Solution.state_same` carries this state in the state at a crossing,
  and `Bridge.horizon_entropy` sums the bit over the strings.
* `stringState`, `share_stringState`, `expected_share`, `half_bits_thermal`: the state of a string
  with `m` 1s and the relative phase `2πn/L`, Eq. (qubit), with the share of the bits as the
  probability of the outcome `1` (Postulate 1; Eq. (raqm)); the probability of `1` in it is `m/L`; under any
  mixture of strings the expected share is the Born probability of `1` in its density matrix; so
  half the bits of a string in the horizon's thermal state are 1s, on average (Sec. II), since that
  state is half the identity.  `half_bits_model` meets the hypothesis.
-/

open Matrix

namespace Register.Qubit

/-! ### The qubit's space, its two senses, and the tick on it -/
        Input · Postulate 1 (structure)Qubit.Vecline 100
        /-- a vector of the qubit's two-dimensional space -/
abbrev Vec := Fin 2 → ℂ
        Input · Postulate 1 (structure)Qubit.Opline 102
        /-- an operator on it -/
abbrev Op := Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ
        DefinitionQubit.e₁line 105
        /-- the basis state of the outcome `1`: the string of all 1s, the sense with the ring -/
def e₁ : Vec := ![1, 0]
        DefinitionQubit.e₂line 107
        /-- the basis state of the outcome `-1`: the string of all −1s, the sense against the ring -/
def e₂ : Vec := ![0, 1]
        TheoremQubit.eq_diagonal_of_keepsline 110
        /-- **A map that keeps both senses up to a factor is diagonal in them** (linear algebra): its
columns are its values on `e₁` and `e₂`. -/
theorem eq_diagonal_of_keeps (T : Op) (c₁ c₂ : ℂ) (h₁ : T *ᵥ e₁ = c₁ • e₁)
    (h₂ : T *ᵥ e₂ = c₂ • e₂) : T = Matrix.diagonal ![c₁, c₂] := by
  have a0 := congrFun h₁ 0
  have a1 := congrFun h₁ 1
  have b0 := congrFun h₂ 0
  have b1 := congrFun h₂ 1
  simp [e₁, e₂, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Fin.sum_univ_two] at a0 a1 b0 b1
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [Matrix.diagonal, a0, a1, b0, b1]
        Input · Postulate 1 and Postulate 2 (structure)Qubit.Tickline 122
        /-- **The free tick on a string's qubit** (Secs. II and IV.E), for a string on a ring of `L` cells:
`U` is the tick, a linear map on the qubit's states (Sec. II: a state is a linear combination of
outcomes, Postulate 1, so the tick is linear).  One sentence of the paper is taken, once, in its words.  Sec. II: "A string of
one sense has the same bit on every cell, so the shift leaves it as it is, up to its global phase
(Postulate 1), and that phase changes alike in either sense, since no law depends on the ring's
direction (Postulate 2)."  The strings of one sense are the strings of all 1s and of all −1s, the
two outcomes (Sec. II, by the definition of the bit values), so the tick keeps each of them up to a
global phase, a factor `e^{iγ}` on all the amplitudes (Sec. II's definition of the global phase),
and the phase is the same for both (`hsense`).  Nothing else is assumed: that the tick is one
factor on every state (`Tick.phase_unique`) follows.  A reversal of a bit's sense is a change of a
bit, so it is an interaction (Postulate 1) and no part of a free tick. -/
structure Tick (L : ℕ) where
  /-- the tick -/
  U : Op
  /-- the tick keeps each string of one sense, the string of all 1s and the string of all −1s, up
  to one and the same phase, a factor of modulus one (Sec. II: the shift leaves a string of one
  sense as it is up to its global phase, Postulate 1, and that phase changes alike in either sense,
  Postulate 2) -/
  hsense : ∃ c : ℂ, ‖c‖ = 1 ∧ U *ᵥ e₁ = c • e₁ ∧ U *ᵥ e₂ = c • e₂

        
variable {L : ℕ}
        TheoremQubit.eq_smul_one_of_keepsline 144
        /-- a map with one factor on both senses is that factor times the identity
(`eq_diagonal_of_keeps`) -/
theorem eq_smul_one_of_keeps (T : Op) (c : ℂ) (h₁ : T *ᵥ e₁ = c • e₁) (h₂ : T *ᵥ e₂ = c • e₂) :
    T = c • (1 : Op) := by
  rw [eq_diagonal_of_keeps T c c h₁ h₂]
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [Matrix.diagonal]
        Statement of the paperQubit.Tick.phase_uniqueline 152
        /-- **The tick's factor is one for all the string's states** (Sec. IV.E): one factor on both senses
(`hsense`), and the tick is a linear map on the states (quantum mechanics; a state is a linear
combination of the outcomes, Postulate 1), so it is diagonal in the senses (`eq_diagonal_of_keeps`)
with one entry, `U = c • 1`.  This is the whole of a free string's energy: no relative phase of the
two senses turns under the free tick. -/
theorem Tick.phase_unique (T : Tick L) : ∃ c : ℂ, T.U = c • (1 : Op) := by
  obtain ⟨c, -, h₁, h₂⟩ := T.hsense
  exact ⟨c, eq_smul_one_of_keeps T.U c h₁ h₂⟩
        DefinitionQubit.Tick.scalarline 161
        /-- the factor of the tick, `U = c • 1` (`phase_unique`) -/
noncomputable def Tick.scalar (T : Tick L) : ℂ := Classical.choose T.phase_unique
        TheoremQubit.Tick.scalar_specline 164
        /-- the tick is its factor times the identity -/
theorem Tick.scalar_spec (T : Tick L) : T.U = T.scalar • (1 : Op) :=
  Classical.choose_spec T.phase_unique
        TheoremQubit.Tick.scalar_eqline 168
        /-- the factor of a tick is the one it multiplies every state by -/
theorem Tick.scalar_eq (T : Tick L) (c : ℂ) (h : T.U = c • (1 : Op)) : T.scalar = c := by
  have hs := T.scalar_spec
  rw [h] at hs
  have h00 := congrFun (congrFun hs 0) 0
  simpa using h00.symm
        Statement of the paperQubit.Tick.norm_scalarline 175
        /-- **The tick's factor is a phase**: its modulus is one, the modulus of the global phase of
`hsense`.  So the tick is unitary, as the tick of quantum mechanics is. -/
theorem Tick.norm_scalar (T : Tick L) : ‖T.scalar‖ = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc, h₁, h₂⟩ := T.hsense
  rw [T.scalar_eq c (eq_smul_one_of_keeps T.U c h₁ h₂)]
  exact hc
        ModelQubit.Tick.ofPhaseline 182
        /-- **The tick of factor `e^{−iθ}`**: that factor on every state is the tick of a free string, for
any angle `θ`.  It keeps each string of one sense up to that one factor, a phase (`hsense`). -/
noncomputable def Tick.ofPhase (θ : ℝ) : Tick L where
  U := Complex.exp (-(θ : ℂ) * Complex.I) • (1 : Op)
  hsense := ⟨Complex.exp (-(θ : ℂ) * Complex.I),
    by simpa using Complex.norm_exp_ofReal_mul_I (-θ),
    by rw [Matrix.smul_mulVec, Matrix.one_mulVec], by rw [Matrix.smul_mulVec, Matrix.one_mulVec]⟩

        
/-! ### The thermal state of a free string, the Born rule and the bit -/
        DefinitionQubit.weightline 192
        /-- the Boltzmann weight of the first of two states, of energies `E₁` and `E₂`, at the inverse
temperature `β` (thermodynamics) -/
noncomputable def weight (β E₁ E₂ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp (-(β * E₁)) / (Real.exp (-(β * E₁)) + Real.exp (-(β * E₂)))
        DefinitionQubit.thermalline 197
        /-- **The thermal state** `e^{−βH}/Z` of a qubit whose basis states `e₁`, `e₂` have the energies
`E₁`, `E₂` (thermodynamics): diagonal in that basis, with the Boltzmann weights. -/
noncomputable def thermal (β E₁ E₂ : ℝ) : Op :=
  Matrix.diagonal ![(weight β E₁ E₂ : ℂ), (weight β E₂ E₁ : ℂ)]
        LemmaQubit.weight_of_equalline 202
        /-- **Equal energies, equal weights**: with `E₁ = E₂` each weight is `1/2`. -/
lemma weight_of_equal (β E : ℝ) : weight β E E = 1 / 2 := by
  unfold weight
  have h := Real.exp_pos (-(β * E))
  field_simp
  ring
        TheoremQubit.thermal_of_equalline 209
        /-- **The thermal state of a qubit whose two states have one energy is half the identity**, at every
temperature: `e^{−βH}/Z` with `H` a multiple of the identity.  A free string is such a qubit, its
two senses having one energy (`Tick.energy_eq`, from `hsense`). -/
theorem thermal_of_equal (β E : ℝ) : thermal β E E = (1 / 2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op) := by
  unfold thermal
  rw [weight_of_equal]
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [Matrix.diagonal]
        DefinitionQubit.bornProbline 218
        /-- the probability of the outcome `v`, a unit vector, in the state `ρ`: `⟨v, ρ v⟩`, the square of
the outcome's amplitude for a pure state and the average for a mixture.  For a string's state
(`stringState`) it is the string's share of the bits (`share_stringState`), as Postulate 1 says. -/
noncomputable def bornProb (ρ : Op) (v : Vec) : ℝ := (star v ⬝ᵥ ρ *ᵥ v).re
        LemmaQubit.e₁_unitline 223
        /-- the basis state `e₁` is a unit vector -/
lemma e₁_unit : star e₁ ⬝ᵥ e₁ = 1 := by
  simp [e₁, dotProduct, Fin.sum_univ_two]
        TheoremQubit.bornProb_halfline 227
        /-- **Half the identity gives every outcome the probability `1/2`**: for a unit vector `v`,
`⟨v, v/2⟩ = 1/2`. -/
theorem bornProb_half (v : Vec) (hv : star v ⬝ᵥ v = 1) :
    bornProb ((1 / 2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op)) v = 1 / 2 := by
  unfold bornProb
  rw [Matrix.smul_mulVec, Matrix.one_mulVec, dotProduct_smul, hv]
  norm_num
        TheoremQubit.bornProb_thermalline 235
        /-- **A free string reads a `1` with the probability `1/2`**: its thermal state is half the identity
(`thermal_of_equal`), and the Born rule gives the outcome `e₁` the probability `1/2`
(`bornProb_half`). -/
theorem bornProb_thermal (β E : ℝ) : bornProb (thermal β E E) e₁ = 1 / 2 := by
  rw [thermal_of_equal]
  exact bornProb_half e₁ e₁_unit
        DefinitionQubit.probline 242
        /-- the probability of the basis outcome `i` in the state `ρ`: the diagonal entry `ρ i i`, the
Born probability of the basis vector -/
noncomputable def prob (ρ : Op) (i : Fin 2) : ℝ := (ρ i i).re
        TheoremQubit.prob_thermalline 246
        /-- the thermal state of a qubit whose two states have one energy gives each basis outcome the
probability `1/2` -/
theorem prob_thermal (β E : ℝ) (i : Fin 2) : prob (thermal β E E) i = 1 / 2 := by
  rw [thermal_of_equal]
  fin_cases i <;> simp [prob]
        DefinitionQubit.entropyline 252
        /-- the entropy of a state diagonal in the basis, with the weight `p` on `e₁`: the binary entropy
`−p ln p − (1 − p) ln (1 − p)`, the von Neumann entropy of `diag(p, 1 − p)` -/
noncomputable def entropy (p : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.binEntropy p
        TheoremQubit.entropy_thermalline 256
        /-- **A free string holds one bit** (Sec. II, "The entropy"): the thermal state of a qubit whose two
states have one energy has the weight `1/2` on each, and the entropy `ln 2`, the most a state
diagonal in the senses can hold (`Real.binEntropy_le_log_two`).  The two states are the two senses,
so this bit is the sense bit of Sec. II. -/
theorem entropy_thermal (β E : ℝ) :
    entropy (prob (thermal β E E) 0) = Real.log 2 ∧ ∀ p, entropy p ≤ Real.log 2 := by
  refine ⟨?_, fun p => Real.binEntropy_le_log_two⟩
  rw [prob_thermal, entropy, one_div, Real.binEntropy_two_inv]

        
/-! ### The thermal state of a free string -/
        DefinitionQubit.Tick.factorline 267
        /-- **The factor by which the tick multiplies the string of one sense**: `true` is the sense with
the ring, the string of all 1s, `e₁`, and `false` the sense against it, the string of all −1s,
`e₂` (`Tick.mulVec_e₁`, `Tick.mulVec_e₂`). -/
def Tick.factor (T : Tick L) (s : Bool) : ℂ := if s then T.U 0 0 else T.U 1 1
        Statement of the paperQubit.Tick.mulVec_e₁line 272
        /-- the tick multiplies the string of all 1s by its factor -/
theorem Tick.mulVec_e₁ (T : Tick L) : T.U *ᵥ e₁ = T.factor true • e₁ := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := T.phase_unique
  simp [Tick.factor, hc, Matrix.smul_mulVec]
        Statement of the paperQubit.Tick.mulVec_e₂line 277
        /-- the tick multiplies the string of all −1s by its factor -/
theorem Tick.mulVec_e₂ (T : Tick L) : T.U *ᵥ e₂ = T.factor false • e₂ := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := T.phase_unique
  simp [Tick.factor, hc, Matrix.smul_mulVec]
        TheoremQubit.Tick.factor_eqline 282
        /-- **The two senses have one factor** (Sec. II: "that phase changes alike in either sense, since
no law depends on the ring's direction (Postulate 2)"; `hsense`, through `phase_unique`). -/
theorem Tick.factor_eq (T : Tick L) : T.factor true = T.factor false := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := T.phase_unique
  simp [Tick.factor, hc]
        DefinitionQubit.Tick.energyline 288
        /-- **The energy of a string of one sense**: the energy of the factor by which the tick multiplies
it.  Sec. II defines the energy of a state by that factor, "A state that one tick multiplies by
`e^{−iΔ}` has energy `ℏΔ/t_c`, as in quantum mechanics", so the
energy is a function `En` of the factor.  A factor fixes `Δ` only up to whole turns, and `En` is
that function for whatever choice of the turn: nothing below depends on the choice. -/
def Tick.energy (T : Tick L) (En : ℂ → ℝ) (s : Bool) : ℝ := En (T.factor s)
        TheoremQubit.Tick.energy_eqline 295
        /-- **The two senses of a free string have one energy** (Secs. II and IV.E): one factor
(`factor_eq`), so one energy, whatever function of the factor the energy is. -/
theorem Tick.energy_eq (T : Tick L) (En : ℂ → ℝ) : T.energy En true = T.energy En false :=
  congrArg En T.factor_eq
        DefinitionQubit.Tick.stateline 300
        /-- **The thermal state of a free string** at the inverse temperature `β` (thermodynamics): the
Gibbs state `e^{−βH}/Z` over the string's two senses, each at its energy, the energy `En` of the
factor by which the tick multiplies it (`Tick.energy`).  That the two energies are one is not put
in here: `Tick.state_eq` derives it from `hsense`.  The strings' energies differ from string to
string with their factors; their mean, `k_BT_dS`, is `Carriers.string_energy`. -/
noncomputable def Tick.state (T : Tick L) (β : ℝ) (En : ℂ → ℝ) : Op :=
  thermal β (T.energy En true) (T.energy En false)
        TheoremQubit.Tick.state_eqline 308
        /-- **A free string's thermal state is half the identity**, at every temperature: its two senses
have one energy (`energy_eq`, from `hsense`), so the Gibbs state weights them equally
(`thermal_of_equal`). -/
theorem Tick.state_eq (T : Tick L) (β : ℝ) (En : ℂ → ℝ) :
    T.state β En = (1 / 2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op) := by
  unfold Tick.state
  rw [T.energy_eq En]
  exact thermal_of_equal _ _
        TheoremQubit.Tick.bornProb_stateline 317
        /-- **A free string reads a `1` with the probability `1/2`**: the Born rule in its thermal state.
With `expected_share` it gives `half_bits_thermal`. -/
theorem Tick.bornProb_state (T : Tick L) (β : ℝ) (En : ℂ → ℝ) :
    bornProb (T.state β En) e₁ = 1 / 2 := by
  unfold Tick.state
  rw [T.energy_eq En]
  exact bornProb_thermal _ _
        TheoremQubit.Tick.prob_stateline 325
        /-- each basis outcome has the probability `1/2` in a free string's thermal state: each sense -/
theorem Tick.prob_state (T : Tick L) (β : ℝ) (En : ℂ → ℝ) (i : Fin 2) :
    prob (T.state β En) i = 1 / 2 := by
  unfold Tick.state
  rw [T.energy_eq En]
  exact prob_thermal _ _ i
        TheoremQubit.Tick.entropy_stateline 332
        /-- **A free string holds one bit** (Sec. II, "The entropy"): the entropy of its thermal state,
read on the two senses, is `ln 2`, since the senses have one energy (`energy_eq`,
`entropy_thermal`). -/
theorem Tick.entropy_state (T : Tick L) (β : ℝ) (En : ℂ → ℝ) :
    entropy (prob (T.state β En) 0) = Real.log 2 := by
  unfold Tick.state
  rw [T.energy_eq En]
  exact (entropy_thermal _ _).1

        
/-! ### The state of a string, Eq. (qubit), and its share of 1s, Eq. (raqm) -/
        DefinitionQubit.stringStateline 343
        /-- **The state of a string with `m` ones and the relative phase `2πn/L`**, Eq. (qubit) of the paper
(a unit vector for `m ≤ L`):
the probability of the outcome `1`, the first sense, is its share of the bits, `m/L` (Postulate 1:
the bits are the possible outcomes of one measurement of the qubit), the amplitude of an outcome is
the square root of its probability (Eq. (qubit)), and the string's cyclic position is the qubit's
phase, `2πn/L`, the relative phase of the two senses (Postulate 1; Eq. (raqm)).  Every state is a
linear combination of the outcomes (Postulate 1), here of `e₁` and `e₂`. -/
noncomputable def stringState (L m n : ℕ) : Vec :=
  ![(Real.sqrt (m / L) : ℂ),
    Complex.exp (2 * Real.pi * Complex.I * n / L) * (Real.sqrt (1 - m / L) : ℂ)]
        DefinitionQubit.projline 354
        /-- the projector `|v⟩⟨v|` onto a state, the density matrix of the pure state `v` -/
noncomputable def proj (v : Vec) : Op := Matrix.vecMulVec v (star v)
        TheoremQubit.bornProb_projline 357
        /-- the Born probability of `e₁` in a pure state is the squared modulus of its first amplitude -/
theorem bornProb_proj (v : Vec) : bornProb (proj v) e₁ = Complex.normSq (v 0) := by
  unfold bornProb proj
  simp [e₁, mulVec, dotProduct, Fin.sum_univ_two, vecMulVec, Complex.normSq_apply]
        TheoremQubit.share_stringStateline 362
        /-- **The probability of the outcome `1` in a string's state is its share of the bits**, `m/L`
(Postulate 1 with Eq. (raqm)): the square of the amplitude is the share it is the square root of. -/
theorem share_stringState (L m n : ℕ) : bornProb (proj (stringState L m n)) e₁ = m / L := by
  rw [bornProb_proj]
  simp only [stringState, Matrix.cons_val_zero]
  rw [Complex.normSq_ofReal, Real.mul_self_sqrt (by positivity)]
        TheoremQubit.expected_shareline 369
        /-- **Under a mixture of strings, the expected share of 1s is the Born probability of `1` in the
mixture's density matrix**: the probability of `1` is linear in the state, and in each string's
state it is the string's share (`share_stringState`). -/
theorem expected_share {S : Type*} [Fintype S] (L : ℕ) (m n : S → ℕ) (p : S → ℝ) (ρ : Op)
    (hρ : ρ = ∑ s, (p s : ℂ) • proj (stringState L (m s) (n s))) :
    ∑ s, p s * (m s / L) = bornProb ρ e₁ := by
  subst hρ
  unfold bornProb
  rw [Matrix.sum_mulVec, dotProduct_sum, Complex.re_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun s _ => ?_
  rw [Matrix.smul_mulVec, dotProduct_smul, smul_eq_mul, Complex.mul_re, Complex.ofReal_re,
    Complex.ofReal_im, zero_mul, sub_zero]
  have h := share_stringState L (m s) (n s)
  unfold bornProb at h
  rw [h]
        TheoremQubit.half_bits_thermalline 385
        /-- **Half the bits of a string in the thermal state are 1s** (Sec. II, "The entropy"), on
average over the thermal mixture: a free string's thermal state is half the identity
(`Tick.state_eq`), whose Born probability of `1` is `1/2` (`Tick.bornProb_state`), so a mixture of
strings `p` that realizes it (`hρ`) has the expected share of 1s `1/2` (`expected_share`); the
theorem says nothing about which strings realize it (`half_bits_model` is one mixture).  This is
the `hones` that `Solution.state_same` took from `hborn` until 19 October, now a theorem. -/
theorem half_bits_thermal {S : Type*} [Fintype S] (T : Tick L) (β : ℝ) (En : ℂ → ℝ)
    (m n : S → ℕ) (p : S → ℝ)
    (hρ : T.state β En = ∑ s, (p s : ℂ) • proj (stringState L (m s) (n s))) :
    ∑ s, p s * (m s / L) = 1 / 2 := by
  rw [expected_share L m n p _ hρ, T.bornProb_state]
        ModelQubit.half_bits_modelline 397
        /-- the hypothesis of `half_bits_thermal` can be met: the equal mixture of the all-1 string and
the all-−1 string, the two senses, is half the identity -/
theorem half_bits_model [NeZero L] (T : Tick L) (β : ℝ) (En : ℂ → ℝ) :
    T.state β En = ∑ s : Fin 2, ((1 / 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) • proj (stringState L (![L, 0] s) 0) := by
  rw [T.state_eq]
  have hL : (0 : ℝ) < L := by exact_mod_cast Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (NeZero.ne L)
  have hs : Real.sqrt L ≠ 0 := Real.sqrt_ne_zero'.2 hL
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
    simp [Fin.sum_univ_two, proj, vecMulVec, stringState]
  rw [div_self (by exact_mod_cast hs)]
  norm_num

        
end Register.Qubit

        RegisterGravity/Bridge.lean451 lines

        import RegisterGravity.Galactic
import RegisterGravity.RouteB
import RegisterGravity.Crossing
import RegisterGravity.Geodesics
import RegisterGravity.Models
import RegisterGravity.DeSitter
import RegisterGravity.Entropy
import RegisterGravity.Qubit

/-!
# The count and the chain, joined

`Horizon.lean` and `RouteB.lean` count the cells and rings of a `Horizon L`, with `L` a natural
number.  `Chain.lean` and `Galactic.lean` derive the laws over a register `Reg` whose `L` is a
positive real, with the horizon's counts entered as `L²/2` and `L²/4`.  The theorems here join them
for any register whose `L` is that of the horizon:

* `counts_exact`: the rings and cells of the horizon number the chain's `R_hor = L²/4` and
  `C_hor = L²/2` times `1 − 2/L + 4/L²` (Eq. (counts) with `Reg.counts_leading_order`), so the
  chain's counts are the horizon's to relative order `2/L`;
* `horizonWeight`, `horizonWeight_quarter`: with its horizon `x` cells from the body
  (`horizonWeight`), the count's horizon taken to be the solution's, at the proper distance
  `Lℓ_c/4` (`Reg.proper_distance`), since a ring's cells, segments of length `ℓ_c` of its geodesic,
  measure proper distance along it (`hx` of `Main.horizon_quarter`; Postulate 2's last sentence):
  then `x = L/4` (`Main.horizon_quarter`), and a cell's weight inside that horizon is the count's
  (`horizonWeight_quarter`); `ring_distance_model` shows
  that the hypotheses can be met.
* `horizon_entropy_count`: every largest ring has half its cells inside any observer's horizon,
  and at one bit per ring the horizon's entropy, `card Loop · ln 2`, is the chain's `S_hor` to
  relative order `2/L`; a ring's share of the horizon's area is that area over this count.
* `horizon_entropy`: the bit per ring, Eq. (S).  The two senses of a free string have the same
  energy (Postulate 2, no law depends on the direction), so the horizon's Boltzmann weighting
  weights them equally, and the strings on the rings hold `card Loop · ln 2`.  A free string's
  own thermal state is half the identity (`Qubit.Tick.state_eq`: every state of a free string has
  one energy), so each of its two outcomes has the probability `1/2` and it holds exactly one bit
  (`Main.string_one_bit`).
* `sphere_strings`: the strings of a sphere (Sec. II, "Counting in the bulk").  With the largest
  rings drawn as great circles of the three-sphere of radius `R_Λ`, a sphere of areal radius `r`
  holds, averaged over its position, the number of rings times `(r/R_Λ)²`
  (`Crossing.Drawing.meanStrings_eq`, Archimedes' hat-box theorem in four dimensions).  With the
  register's count of rings this is the chain's `N_s(r) = (L²/4)(r/R_Λ)²`, Eq. (N), times
  `1 − 2/L + 4/L²`: on average, one string for each ring's share of the sphere's area, `4ℓ_c²/π`,
  at every radius.  The count about a given position depends on how the rings are drawn, which the
  postulates do not fix; the average does not.  Averaged over the rotations `x ↦ φ⁻¹(qφ(x))` of the
  drawing, with `q` a unit quaternion and `φ` an isometry of the space onto `ℍ`, the count about any
  point is the average, exactly, in any four-dimensional space (`Center.sphere_strings_centered_of`,
  `Center.sphere_strings_of_rings_centered`).
* `sphere_strings_of_rings`, `sphere_strings_deSitter`: the same count with the drawing derived.
  If every largest ring is a closed geodesic of the space at an instant of de Sitter space with the
  cosmological constant `Λ`, then `Λ > 0`, since a spacelike ring needs that space, the quadric
  `form X X = 3/Λ`, to be a sphere; `Λ = 3/R_Λ²`, that space is the three-sphere of radius `R_Λ`,
  and the rings are its great circles (`Geodesics.lean`).  `sphere_strings_model` shows that the
  hypotheses of `sphere_strings_of_rings` can be met together.
* `ring_through_two_cells`: the last sentence of Postulate 2, that every largest ring is a closed
  geodesic of space, matches the register on pairs of cells: two cells that are not opposite lie on
  exactly one largest ring, and two points of space that are not antipodal lie on exactly one
  geodesic (`TwoCells.geodesic_through_two`).

The paper's definition of a cell, one bit of each ring through it, gives each largest ring exactly
one string, a bit on each of its cells; so the horizon's state is one sense, or one outcome, for
each ring, the type `H.Loop → Bool` of `horizon_entropy`, and the entropy sums one bit for each
ring.
-/

open Finset

namespace Register
namespace Bridge

variable {L : ℕ} (H : Horizon L) (R : Reg)
        TheoremBridge.counts_exactline 72
        /-- **The exact counts in the chain's terms** (Sec. II, Eq. (counts)).  For a register whose `L`
is that of the horizon `H`, `L ≥ 4`, the largest rings of `H` number `R_hor (1 − 2/L + 4/L²)` and
its cells `C_hor (1 − 2/L + 4/L²)`, with the chain's `R_hor = L²/4` and `C_hor = L²/2`. -/
theorem counts_exact (hL : 4 ≤ L) (hRL : R.L = L) :
    (Fintype.card H.Loop : ℝ) = R.Rhor * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) ∧
    (Fintype.card H.Cell : ℝ) = R.Chor * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) := by
  obtain ⟨-, hC, hR, -⟩ := H.counts hL
  have hC' : 2 * (Fintype.card H.Cell : ℝ) + 2 * L = (L : ℝ) ^ 2 + 4 := by exact_mod_cast hC
  have hR' : 4 * (Fintype.card H.Loop : ℝ) + 2 * L = (L : ℝ) ^ 2 + 4 := by exact_mod_cast hR
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := R.counts_leading_order
  rw [← h1, ← h2, hRL]
  constructor <;> linarith
        TheoremBridge.horizon_entropy_countline 85
        /-- **Half of every ring lies inside every horizon** (Sec. II, "What the manifold contributes";
Sec. IV.D).  Every largest ring has half its cells inside any observer's horizon, counting a cell on
it as half (`Horizon.Positions.horizon_weight_ring`), so every ring crosses the horizon
(`Horizon.Positions.crossesHorizon`), and the horizon counts every ring
(`horizon_counts_every_ring`).  At one bit per ring (`horizon_entropy`) the horizon's entropy is
`card Loop · ln 2`, which is the chain's `S_hor = (L²/4) ln 2` times `1 − 2/L + 4/L²`
(`counts_exact`).  A ring's share of the horizon's area, `A_hor/R` (`Reg.ringShare`), is then the
solution's area over this count, a quotient, not an identification. -/
theorem horizon_entropy_count [NeZero L] (P : H.Positions) (hL : 4 ≤ L) (hRL : R.L = L)
    (B : H.Cell) :
    (∀ l : H.Loop,
      ∑ X ∈ H.cells l, Horizon.Positions.weight (L := L) (P.dist B X) = (L : ℝ) / 2) ∧
    (Fintype.card H.Loop : ℝ) * R.ln2 = R.Shor * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) := by
  refine ⟨fun l => P.horizon_weight_ring hL B l, ?_⟩
  rw [(counts_exact H R hL hRL).1]
  unfold Reg.Shor
  ring
        DefinitionBridge.horizonEntropyline 103
        /-- **A horizon's entropy** (Sec. II, "The entropy"; Sec. III): the Shannon entropy of the
horizon's state `P`.  A horizon is thermal, so its entropy is that of its thermal state
(thermodynamics, Sec. III).  That state is a state of the strings and of nothing else: the
horizon's entropy depends only on strings.  This is Postulate 1's second sentence, a state a linear
combination of outcomes of its qubits, with the first, every physical law and quantity defined by
qubits (the thesis of the paper): a horizon's state that depended on anything else would not be
defined by qubits.  It enters here as the type of the state.  `P` is a distribution on the strings' senses, `H.Loop → Bool`; the probability of a
string's first sense is the weight of its first outcome in the thermal state of its tick, the
senses being the outcomes (`hq` of `horizon_entropy`, thermodynamics with Sec. II's reading); on
a string's own thermal state, in the basis of its outcomes, the entropy is the same, one bit
(`Main.string_one_bit`), so the type loses nothing.  The state is the whole register's, so it is a distribution on the senses of every string,
`l : H.Loop`: no string is left out.  What the state is, the product of the strings' own thermal
states, is the hypothesis of `horizon_entropy`. -/
noncomputable def horizonEntropy (P : (H.Loop → Bool) → ℝ) : ℝ := Entropy.shannon P
        TheoremBridge.horizonEntropy_eq_sumline 118
        /-- **The entropy of the strings adds** (known mathematics, `Entropy.shannon_jointProb`): the
entropy of a state that is the product of one distribution per string, the strings independent, is
the sum over the strings of the binary entropy of each string's sense probability. -/
theorem horizonEntropy_eq_sum (q : H.Loop → ℝ) :
    horizonEntropy H (Entropy.jointProb q) = ∑ l, Real.binEntropy (q l) :=
  Entropy.shannon_jointProb q
        TheoremBridge.horizon_entropyline 125
        /-- **The bit per ring**, Eq. (S) (Sec. II, "The entropy").  A horizon's entropy is that of its
state, a state of the strings alone (`horizonEntropy`).  Between interactions the strings are
free, so the state is the product of the strings' own thermal states (`hfree`, Sec. II), and it
is the sum of their binary entropies (`horizonEntropy_eq_sum`).  A free string's two senses are
the two outcomes of its qubit (Sec. II), and the qubit is in the thermal state of its tick
(`Qubit.Tick.state`, thermodynamics), so the probability of the first sense is that state's weight
on the first outcome (`hq`).  The tick keeps each string of one sense up to one and the same
factor, since the shift leaves it as it is up to its global phase and that phase changes alike in
either sense, no law depending on the ring's direction (Sec. II, Postulates 1 and 2; `hsense` of
`Qubit.Tick`), so the two senses have one energy and the thermal state is half the identity: each
sense has the
probability `1/2` (`Qubit.Tick.prob_state`), and two senses weighted equally hold one bit
(`Reg.one_bit`).  On a string's own thermal state the entropy is the same (`Main.string_one_bit`).
So the entropy is `card Loop · ln 2`, which is the chain's `S_hor = (L²/4) ln 2` times
`1 − 2/L + 4/L²` (`counts_exact`); the definition `Reg.Shor` is the entropy of the strings to
relative order `2/L`. -/
theorem horizon_entropy (hL : 4 ≤ L) (hRL : R.L = L) [NeZero L] (T : H.Loop → Qubit.Tick L)
    (β : ℝ) (En : ℂ → ℝ) (P : (H.Loop → Bool) → ℝ) (q : H.Loop → ℝ) (hfree : P = Entropy.jointProb q)
    (hq : ∀ l, q l = Qubit.prob ((T l).state β En) 0) :
    horizonEntropy H P = Fintype.card H.Loop * Real.log 2 ∧
    (Fintype.card H.Loop : ℝ) * Real.log 2 = R.Shor * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) := by
  constructor
  · rw [hfree, horizonEntropy_eq_sum]
    have h : ∀ l, Real.binEntropy (q l) = Real.log 2 := by
      intro l
      rw [hq l, Qubit.Tick.prob_state]
      exact Reg.one_bit.1
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun l _ => h l), Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]
  · rw [(counts_exact H R hL hRL).1, ← R.ln2_def]
    unfold Reg.Shor
    ring
        TheoremBridge.horizon_counts_every_ringline 157
        /-- **The horizon counts every ring**, Eq. (S) (Sec. II, "What the manifold contributes" and "The
entropy").  A horizon's entropy is that of its state, a state of the whole register, so of every
string (`horizonEntropy`).  Each string holds one bit, its two senses being the two outcomes of
its qubit, which have one energy (`hsense` of `Qubit.Tick`) and so equal thermal weight
(`horizon_entropy`), so the entropy is `card Loop · ln 2`,
the chain's `S_hor = (L²/4) ln 2` times `1 − 2/L + 4/L²`.  The count and the horizon also agree
ring by ring: every ring crosses every observer's horizon, with half its cells inside
(`Horizon.Positions.crossesHorizon`), so no string lies wholly inside a horizon or wholly beyond
it. -/
theorem horizon_counts_every_ring [NeZero L] (Pos : H.Positions) (hL : 4 ≤ L) (hRL : R.L = L)
    (B : H.Cell) (T : H.Loop → Qubit.Tick L) (β : ℝ) (En : ℂ → ℝ) (P : (H.Loop → Bool) → ℝ)
    (q : H.Loop → ℝ) (hfree : P = Entropy.jointProb q)
    (hq : ∀ l, q l = Qubit.prob ((T l).state β En) 0) :
    (∀ l, Pos.CrossesHorizon B l) ∧
    horizonEntropy H P = R.Shor * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) := by
  refine ⟨fun l => Pos.crossesHorizon hL B l, ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := horizon_entropy H R hL hRL T β En P q hfree hq
  rw [h1, h2]
        TheoremBridge.sphere_stringsline 176
        /-- **The strings of a sphere**, Eq. (N) (Sec. II, "Counting in the bulk").  Let the register's
largest rings be drawn as great circles of the three-sphere of radius `R_Λ`, the solution's space
at an instant (`Crossing.Drawing`, Sec. IV.D), in a four-dimensional real inner product space `E`
with a Haar measure `μ`.  Let the sphere be the points at distance `s` from a point of the
three-sphere, no larger than a great sphere, `0 < s` and `s² ≤ 2R_Λ²`, with areal radius `r`,
`r² = s² − s⁴/4R_Λ²` (`Crossing.Drawing.meanStrings_eq`).  Averaged over the sphere's position, with no
position preferred, it holds the number of rings times `(r/R_Λ)²`
(`Crossing.Drawing.meanStrings_eq`), and the rings of `H` number `R_hor (1 − 2/L + 4/L²)`
(`counts_exact`).  So, averaged over its position, the sphere holds the chain's
`N_s(r) = R_hor (r/R_Λ)²` strings, Eq. (N), times `1 − 2/L + 4/L²`: one for each ring's share of
its area, `4πr²/ringShare`, the same average density at every radius.  The drawing keeps only the
rings, as great circles; where on them the cells lie it does not use.  At the horizon's own radius, `s² = 2R_Λ²` and `r = R_Λ`, the
sphere holds every ring from almost every position, which the register gives on its own
(`horizon_entropy_count`).  With `R.pi` the real `π`, a great circle of radius `R_Λ` has the length
`Lℓ_c` of a largest ring and `4πr²` is the sphere's area; the equalities hold for any `R.pi`. -/
theorem sphere_strings (hL : 4 ≤ L) (hRL : R.L = L) {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] (hE : Module.finrank ℝ E = 4)
    (D : Crossing.Drawing H.Loop E R.RL) {s r : ℝ} (hs0 : 0 < s) (hs : s ^ 2 ≤ 2 * R.RL ^ 2)
    (hr : r ^ 2 = s ^ 2 - s ^ 4 / (4 * R.RL ^ 2)) :
    D.meanStrings μ s = R.Ns r * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) ∧
    D.meanStrings μ s = R.Rhor * (r / R.RL) ^ 2 * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) ∧
    D.meanStrings μ s = 4 * R.pi * r ^ 2 / R.ringShare * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) := by
  rw [D.meanStrings_eq μ hE R.RL_pos hs0 hs hr, (counts_exact H R hL hRL).1]
  obtain ⟨h1, h3⟩ := R.ratio_of_areas r
  refine ⟨?_, by ring, ?_⟩
  · rw [h1]
    ring
  · rw [← h3, h1]
    ring
        TheoremBridge.sphere_strings_of_ringsline 207
        /-- **The strings of a sphere, with the rings as closed geodesics of space** (Sec. II, "Counting in
the bulk"; Sec. IV.D).  Let every largest ring of `H`, of length `Lℓ_c`, be a closed spacelike
geodesic of the space at an instant of de Sitter space of radius `ρ` (`Geodesic.IsGeodesic`,
`Geodesic.InSpace`, `Geodesic.HasLength`), in a four-dimensional real inner product space `E` with a
Haar measure `μ`.  Then `ρ = R_Λ`, with `R.pi` the real `π`, since every such geodesic has the
length `2πρ` (`Geodesic.IsGeodesic.hasLength`); the rings are great circles of the three-sphere of
radius `R_Λ` (`Crossing.Drawing.ofRings`, `Geodesic.ofRings_circle`); and, averaged over its
position, a sphere of areal radius `r` holds `N_s(r)(1 − 2/L + 4/L²)` strings
(`sphere_strings`). -/
theorem sphere_strings_of_rings (hL : 4 ≤ L) (hRL : R.L = L)
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure]
    (hE : Module.finrank ℝ E = 4) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (γ : H.Loop → Geodesic.Curve ℝ E)
    (hgeo : ∀ l, Geodesic.IsGeodesic (ρ ^ 2) (γ l)) (hsp : ∀ l, Geodesic.IsSpacelike (γ l))
    (hin : ∀ l, Geodesic.InSpace (γ l)) (hlen : ∀ l, Geodesic.HasLength (γ l) (R.L * R.ℓc))
    {s r : ℝ} (hs0 : 0 < s) (hs : s ^ 2 ≤ 2 * ρ ^ 2) (hr : r ^ 2 = s ^ 2 - s ^ 4 / (4 * ρ ^ 2)) :
    ρ = R.RL ∧
    (Crossing.Drawing.ofRings hρ γ hgeo hsp hin).meanStrings μ s =
      R.Ns r * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) := by
  -- a ring exists
  obtain ⟨-, -, hR, -⟩ := H.counts hL
  have hpos : 0 < Fintype.card H.Loop := by
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (Fintype.card H.Loop) with h0 | h0
    · rw [h0] at hR
      nlinarith
    · exact h0
  obtain ⟨l₀⟩ := Fintype.card_pos_iff.1 hpos
  -- its length gives the radius of space
  have h1 := (hlen l₀).unique ((hgeo l₀).hasLength (by positivity) (hsp l₀))
  rw [Real.sqrt_sq hρ.le] at h1
  have hρeq : ρ = R.RL := by
    have := R.pi_pos
    unfold Reg.RL
    rw [R.pi_def, h1]
    field_simp
  refine ⟨hρeq, ?_⟩
  subst hρeq
  exact (sphere_strings H R hL hRL μ hE _ hs0 hs hr).1

        
open RealInnerProductSpace in
        TheoremBridge.sphere_strings_deSitterline 247
        /-- **The strings of a sphere in de Sitter space with the cosmological constant `Λ`** (Secs. II and
IV.D).  Let every largest ring of `H`, of length `Lℓ_c`, be a closed spacelike geodesic of the space
at an instant of de Sitter space with the cosmological constant `Λ`, the quadric `form X X = 3/Λ`
of `ℝ × E`, as the last sentence of Postulate 2 says.  Then `Λ > 0`, since in the space at an
instant the quadric is the sphere `‖x‖² = 3/Λ`, on which a spacelike ring needs `3/Λ > 0`; and
`Λ = 3/R_Λ²`; the rings are the great circles of a drawing on the

        import RegisterGravity.Bridge
import Mathlib.Analysis.Quaternion

/-!
# The drawing made from the center of the three-sphere (Sec. II, "Counting in the bulk")

The largest rings are drawn as great circles of the three-sphere of radius `ρ`, each the section of
the three-sphere by a plane through its center.  Made from that center, the drawing singles out no
point of space: a rotation about the center keeps the center, carries the
drawing to a drawing of the same rings (`Crossing.Drawing.rotate`), and the rotations carry any
point to any other.  The postulates fix how many rings there are, not which great circle each one
is, and every physical law and quantity is defined by qubits (Postulate 1), so the drawing is no
part of the state, and no law prefers one rotation of it to another.  The count about a body
depends only on the strings, not on the drawing: this is Postulate 1's first sentence (the thesis
of the paper).  With every rotation weighted alike, the count is defined as its average over the
rotations, a value that does not depend on the drawing (Sec. II).  The files prove the average;
taking it as the count is where the thesis enters, a definition and not a theorem.
This file weights the rotations `x ↦ qx` by the unit sphere's measure; `Weighting.lean` derives
that weighting from the sentence, since a weighting that prefers no rotation is the unit sphere's
measure, normalized.

The space that holds the three-sphere is first taken to be the quaternions `ℍ`, a four-dimensional
real inner product space, so that the rotations `x ↦ qx` by the unit quaternions `q` (`leftRot`)
are at hand.  Any
four-dimensional real inner product space `E`, such as that of `Geodesics.lean`, is isometric to
`ℍ` (`exists_isometry_quaternion`), and an isometry `φ : E ≃ ℍ` carries these rotations to the
rotations `x ↦ φ⁻¹(qφ(x))` of `E` about its center (`rotOf`).

`strings_rotation_mean`: for every drawing and every point `p` of the three-sphere, the strings of a
sphere no larger than a great sphere, of areal radius `r`, about `p`, averaged over the rotations
`x ↦ qx` with `q` weighted by the measure of the unit sphere, are the number of rings times
`(r/ρ)²`, exactly.  Turning the drawing by `q` is moving the point by `q⁻¹`
(`Crossing.Drawing.strings_rotate`), and `q ↦ q⁻¹p/ρ` keeps the unit sphere's measure (`starRight`,
`Crossing.toSphere_preserving`), so the average over the rotations is the average over positions of
`Crossing.Drawing.meanStrings_eq`.  For one drawing the count about a
point depends on the point; averaged over the rotations `x ↦ qx` it does not.
`sphere_strings_centered` puts in the register's count of rings: the average is the chain's
`N_s(r)` times `1 − 2/L + 4/L²` about every point, and `sphere_strings_centered_model` shows that
its hypotheses can be met together.  `strings_rotation_mean_of` and `sphere_strings_centered_of`
carry both to any four-dimensional `E`, averaging over the rotations `x ↦ φ⁻¹(qφ(x))`, and
`sphere_strings_of_rings_centered` applies them to the drawing of the rings as closed geodesics of
space (`Crossing.Drawing.ofRings`), with `sphere_strings_of_rings_centered_model`.
`observer_strings_mean` gives the count of an observer at a cell, his `L/2` rings taken where the
drawing places them and the others turned: the average, plus the number of his rings that cross
the sphere, less `(L/2)(r/ρ)²`.
-/

open MeasureTheory Metric Module RealInnerProductSpace
open scoped Quaternion

namespace Center

open Crossing Quaternion

variable {ρ s : ℝ}

  have hq : ‖(q : ℍ)‖ = 1 := mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.1 q.2
  rw [star_mul_self, normSq_eq_norm_mul_self, hq, mul_one]

        /-- a unit quaternion times its conjugate is one -/
lemma mul_star_unit (q : sphere (0 : ℍ) 1) : (q : ℍ) * star (q : ℍ) = 1 := by
  have hq : ‖(q : ℍ)‖ = 1 := mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.1 q.2

        /-- **A rotation about the center**: left multiplication by a unit quaternion `q`, `x ↦ qx`, a

noncomputable def leftRot (q : sphere (0 : ℍ) 1) : ℍ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℍ where

    simp only
    rw [mul_assoc, mul_star_unit, mul_one, star_star]
  right_inv y := by
    simp only
    rw [star_star, mul_assoc, star_mul_unit, mul_one]
  norm_map' x := by
    simp only [LinearEquiv.coe_mk, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk]
    rw [norm_mul, Quaternion.norm_star, mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.1 ξ₀.2, mul_one]

        
/-! ### Any four-dimensional space

The space that holds the three-sphere is any four-dimensional real inner product space `E`, such as
that of `Geodesics.lean`.  A linear isometry `φ : E ≃ ℍ` exists (`exists_isometry_quaternion`), and
it carries the rotations `x ↦ qx` of `ℍ` to rotations of `E` about its center,
`x ↦ φ⁻¹(qφ(x))` (`rotOf`). -/

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]

        /-- **A four-dimensional real inner product space is isometric to `ℍ`**: an orthonormal basis of

lemma exists_isometry_quaternion [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (hE : finrank ℝ E = 4) :
    Nonempty (E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℍ) :=
  ⟨((stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ E).reindex
      (finCongr (hE.trans Quaternion.finrank_eq_four.symm))).repr.trans
    (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ ℍ).repr.symm⟩

        /-- **A rotation of `E` about the center**: the rotation `x ↦ qx` of `ℍ` carried to `E` by a linear

noncomputable def rotOf (φ : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℍ) (q : sphere (0 : ℍ) 1) : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] E :=
  (φ.trans (leftRot q)).trans φ.symm

        lemma rotOf_symm_apply (φ : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℍ) (q : sphere (0 : ℍ) 1) (x : E) :
    (rotOf φ q).symm x = φ.symm ((leftRot q).symm (φ x)) := rfl

        /-- **The strings of a sphere that an observer counts** (Sec. II, after Eq. (N)).  Let `B` be the
observer's cell.  His rings, the `L/2` through `B` (`Horizon.two_mul_card_through`), are taken where
the drawing `D` places them; the other rings are turned about the center, `x ↦ qx`, with `q`
weighted by `μ.toSphere` as for the whole drawing.  His count, the strings on his rings in `D` plus
the average of the strings on the other rings over the turning, is the average of the whole drawing
over the turning (`strings_rotation_mean`), plus the number of his rings that cross the sphere,
less `(L/2)(r/ρ)²`: in the average each ring has the weight `(r/ρ)²`.  At most all `L/2` of his
rings cross (`Crossing.Drawing.strings_le_card`). -/
theorem observer_strings_mean {L : ℕ} (H : Horizon L) (hL : 4 ≤ L) (D : Drawing H.Loop ℍ ρ)
    (B : H.Cell) (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hs0 : 0 < s) (hs : s ^ 2 ≤ 2 * ρ ^ 2) {r : ℝ}
    (hr : r ^ 2 = s ^ 2 - s ^ 4 / (4 * ρ ^ 2)) (ξ₀ : sphere (0 : ℍ) 1) :
    ((D.restrict (· ∈ H.through B)).strings (ρ • (ξ₀ : ℍ)) s : ℝ) +
        (∫ q, (((D.restrict (· ∉ H.through B)).rotate (leftRot q)).strings (ρ • (ξ₀ : ℍ)) s : ℝ)
          ∂μ.toSphere) / μ.toSphere.real Set.univ =
      (∫ q, ((D.rotate (leftRot q)).strings (ρ • (ξ₀ : ℍ)) s : ℝ) ∂μ.toSphere) /
          μ.toSphere.real Set.univ +
        (D.restrict (· ∈ H.through B)).strings (ρ • (ξ₀ : ℍ)) s - L / 2 * (r / ρ) ^ 2 ∧
    ((D.restrict (· ∈ H.through B)).strings (ρ • (ξ₀ : ℍ)) s : ℝ) ≤ L / 2 := by
  classical
  rw [strings_rotation_mean μ (D.restrict (· ∉ H.through B)) hρ hs0 hs hr ξ₀,
    strings_rotation_mean μ D hρ hs0 hs hr ξ₀]
  have hc1 : Fintype.card {l // l ∈ H.through B} = (H.through B).card := Fintype.card_coe _
  have hc0 : Fintype.card {l // l ∉ H.through B} = (H.through B)ᶜ.card := by
    rw [Fintype.card_subtype, Finset.filter_not, Finset.filter_mem_eq_inter, Finset.univ_inter,
      Finset.compl_eq_univ_sdiff]
  have hc2 : Fintype.card {l // l ∉ H.through B} + (H.through B).card = Fintype.card H.Loop := by
    rw [hc0, Finset.card_compl]
    have := Finset.card_le_univ (H.through B)
    omega
  have h2 := H.two_mul_card_through hL B
  have hle := (D.restrict (· ∈ H.through B)).strings_le_card (ρ • (ξ₀ : ℍ)) s
  rw [hc1] at hle
  have hc2' : (Fintype.card {l // l ∉ H.through B} : ℝ) + (H.through B).card =
      Fintype.card H.Loop := by exact_mod_cast hc2
  have h2' : 2 * ((H.through B).card : ℝ) = L := by exact_mod_cast h2
  have hle' : ((D.restrict (· ∈ H.through B)).strings (ρ • (ξ₀ : ℍ)) s : ℝ) ≤
      (H.through B).card := by exact_mod_cast hle
  refine ⟨?_, by linarith⟩
  linear_combination (r / ρ) ^ 2 * hc2' - (r / ρ) ^ 2 / 2 * h2'
        TheoremCenter.sphere_strings_centeredline 204
        /-- **The strings of a sphere about any point, with the drawing made from the center** (Sec. II,
"Counting in the bulk").  With the register's count of rings (`Register.Bridge.counts_exact`), the
average of `strings_rotation_mean` over the rotations `x ↦ qx` of the drawing is the
chain's `N_s(r) = (L²/4)(r/R_Λ)²`, Eq. (N), times `1 − 2/L + 4/L²`, about every point of the
three-sphere of radius `R_Λ`, for every drawing of the rings (`Register.Bridge.sphere_strings`). -/
theorem sphere_strings_centered {L : ℕ} (H : Horizon L) (R : Register.Reg) (hL : 4 ≤ L)
    (hRL : R.L = L) (D : Drawing H.Loop ℍ R.RL) {s r : ℝ} (hs0 : 0 < s)
    (hs : s ^ 2 ≤ 2 * R.RL ^ 2) (hr : r ^ 2 = s ^ 2 - s ^ 4 / (4 * R.RL ^ 2))
    (ξ₀ : sphere (0 : ℍ) 1) :
    (∫ q, ((D.rotate (leftRot q)).strings (R.RL • (ξ₀ : ℍ)) s : ℝ) ∂μ.toSphere) /
      μ.toSphere.real Set.univ = R.Ns r * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) := by
  rw [strings_rotation_mean μ D R.RL_pos hs0 hs hr ξ₀,
    ← D.meanStrings_eq μ Quaternion.finrank_eq_four R.RL_pos hs0 hs hr]
  exact (Register.Bridge.sphere_strings H R hL hRL μ Quaternion.finrank_eq_four D hs0 hs hr).1
        TheoremCenter.strings_rotation_mean_ofline 219
        /-- **The strings about any point, averaged over the rotations of the drawing, in any
four-dimensional space** (Sec. II, "Counting in the bulk").  For every drawing `D` of the rings as
great circles of the three-sphere of radius `ρ` in a four-dimensional real inner product space `E`,
every linear isometry `φ : E ≃ ℍ`, every point `ρξ₀` of the three-sphere, and every sphere no
larger than a great sphere, of areal radius `r`, the strings of the sphere about `ρξ₀` in the
drawing turned by `x ↦ φ⁻¹(qφ(x))`, averaged over the unit quaternions `q` in the measure
`μ.toSphere`, are the number of rings times `(r/ρ)²`.  The drawing turned by `rotOf φ q` has about
`ρξ₀` the strings that the drawing carried to `ℍ` by `φ`, turned by `x ↦ qx`, has about `ρφ(ξ₀)`
(`Crossing.Drawing.strings_rotate`), so `strings_rotation_mean` gives the average. -/
theorem strings_rotation_mean_of {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    (φ : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℍ) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (D : Drawing ι E ρ) (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hs0 : 0 < s)
    (hs : s ^ 2 ≤ 2 * ρ ^ 2) {r : ℝ} (hr : r ^ 2 = s ^ 2 - s ^ 4 / (4 * ρ ^ 2))
    (ξ₀ : sphere (0 : E) 1) :
    (∫ q, ((D.rotate (rotOf φ q)).strings (ρ • (ξ₀ : E)) s : ℝ) ∂μ.toSphere) /
      μ.toSphere.real Set.univ = Fintype.card ι * (r / ρ) ^ 2 := by
  obtain ⟨ξ₁, hξ₁⟩ : ∃ ξ₁ : sphere (0 : ℍ) 1, (ξ₁ : ℍ) = φ ξ₀ := ⟨⟨φ ξ₀, by simp⟩, rfl⟩
  have h : ∀ q : sphere (0 : ℍ) 1, ((D.rotate (rotOf φ q)).strings (ρ • (ξ₀ : E)) s : ℝ) =
      (((D.rotate φ).rotate (leftRot q)).strings (ρ • (ξ₁ : ℍ)) s : ℝ) := fun q => by
    rw [Drawing.strings_rotate, Drawing.strings_rotate, Drawing.strings_rotate, rotOf_symm_apply,
      LinearIsometryEquiv.map_smul, hξ₁]
  simp_rw [h]
  exact strings_rotation_mean μ (D.rotate φ) hρ hs0 hs hr ξ₁
        TheoremCenter.sphere_strings_centered_ofline 242
        /-- **The strings of a sphere about any point, in any four-dimensional space** (Sec. II, "Counting

the rotations `x ↦ φ⁻¹(qφ(x))` of a drawing in a four-dimensional real inner product space `E` is
the chain's `N_s(r)` times `1 − 2/L + 4/L²`, about every point of the three-sphere of radius `R_Λ`,
for every drawing of the rings (`sphere_strings_centered` for the drawing carried to `ℍ`). -/
theorem sphere_strings_centered_of {L : ℕ} (H : Horizon L) (R : Register.Reg) (hL : 4 ≤ L)
    (hRL : R.L = L) {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    (φ : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℍ) (D : Drawing H.Loop E R.RL) {s r : ℝ} (hs0 : 0 < s)
    (hs : s ^ 2 ≤ 2 * R.RL ^ 2) (hr : r ^ 2 = s ^ 2 - s ^ 4 / (4 * R.RL ^ 2))
    (ξ₀ : sphere (0 : E) 1) :
    (∫ q, ((D.rotate (rotOf φ q)).strings (R.RL • (ξ₀ : E)) s : ℝ) ∂μ.toSphere) /
      μ.toSphere.real Set.univ = R.Ns r * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) := by
  obtain ⟨ξ₁, -⟩ : ∃ ξ₁ : sphere (0 : ℍ) 1, (ξ₁ : ℍ) = φ ξ₀ := ⟨⟨φ ξ₀, by simp⟩, rfl⟩
  rw [strings_rotation_mean_of μ φ D R.RL_pos hs0 hs hr ξ₀,
    ← strings_rotation_mean μ (D.rotate φ) R.RL_pos hs0 hs hr ξ₁]

        TheoremCenter.sphere_strings_of_rings_centeredline 259
        /-- **The strings of a sphere about any point, with the rings as closed geodesics of space**
(Secs. II and IV.D).  Let every largest ring of `H`, of length `Lℓ_c`, be a closed spacelike
geodesic of the space at an instant of de Sitter space of radius `ρ`, in a four-dimensional real
inner product space `E` (the hypotheses of `Register.Bridge.sphere_strings_of_rings`), and let
`φ : E ≃ ℍ` be a linear isometry (`exists_isometry_quaternion`).  Then `ρ = R_Λ`, and the strings of
a sphere of areal radius `r` about any point of the three-sphere, in the drawing of the rings
(`Crossing.Drawing.ofRings`) turned by `x ↦ φ⁻¹(qφ(x))` and averaged over the unit quaternions
`q`, are `N_s(r)(1 − 2/L + 4/L²)`. -/
theorem sphere_strings_of_rings_centered {L : ℕ} (H : Horizon L) (R : Register.Reg) (hL : 4 ≤ L)
    (hRL : R.L = L) {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (hE : finrank ℝ E = 4)
    (φ : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℍ) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (γ : H.Loop → Geodesic.Curve ℝ E)
    (hgeo : ∀ l, Geodesic.IsGeodesic (ρ ^ 2) (γ l)) (hsp : ∀ l, Geodesic.IsSpacelike (γ l))
    (hin : ∀ l, Geodesic.InSpace (γ l)) (hlen : ∀ l, Geodesic.HasLength (γ l) (R.L * R.ℓc))
    {s r : ℝ} (hs0 : 0 < s) (hs : s ^ 2 ≤ 2 * ρ ^ 2) (hr : r ^ 2 = s ^ 2 - s ^ 4 / (4 * ρ ^ 2))
    (ξ₀ : sphere (0 : E) 1) :
    ρ = R.RL ∧
    (∫ q, (((Drawing.ofRings hρ γ hgeo hsp hin).rotate (rotOf φ q)).strings (ρ • (ξ₀ : E)) s : ℝ)
        ∂μ.toSphere) / μ.toSphere.real Set.univ = R.Ns r * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) := by
  let _ : MeasurableSpace E := borel E
  have _ : BorelSpace E := ⟨rfl⟩
  have hρeq := (Register.Bridge.sphere_strings_of_rings H R hL hRL Measure.addHaar hE hρ γ hgeo
    hsp hin hlen hs0 hs hr).1
  refine ⟨hρeq, ?_⟩
  subst hρeq
  exact sphere_strings_centered_of μ H R hL hRL φ _ hs0 hs hr ξ₀

        
end Mean

  rw [sphere_strings_centered Measure.addHaar Horizon.fano Register.Bridge.regSix (by norm_num)

        RegisterGravity/Weighting.lean112 lines

        import RegisterGravity.Center
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Field.UnitBall
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.Unique

/-!
# No rotation of the drawing preferred: the rotations weighted alike (Sec. II, "Counting in the
bulk")

The drawing of the largest rings as great circles of the three-sphere is no part of the state
(Sec. II), so no rotation of it is preferred: the paper weights the rotations alike.  `Center.lean`
averages over the rotations `x ↦ qx` of `ℍ`, the unit quaternions `q` weighted by the unit sphere's
measure.  This file derives that weighting from the sentence: a weighting of the rotations that
prefers none, a probability measure `m` on the unit quaternions that following every rotation by a
fixed one leaves unchanged (`m.IsMulLeftInvariant`), is the unit sphere's measure, normalized
(`eq_toSphere_of_invariant`): the unit quaternions are a compact group, a measure on it that left
multiplication keeps is a multiple of its Haar measure (Mathlib's
`Measure.isMulInvariant_eq_smul_of_compactSpace`, the uniqueness of Haar measure), and the unit
sphere's measure is one (`toSphere_isMulLeftInvariant`, `toSphere_isHaarMeasure`).  So an average
over such a weighting is the average over the unit sphere's measure (`integral_normalized`), the one
`Center.lean` computes; `Main.sphere_strings` and `Main.observer_count` take the
sentence as their premise (`Sources.P1.no_rotation_preferred`) and reduce to `Center.lean` through
this file.

The premise can be met: the unit sphere's measure, normalized (`evenWeight`), has total one and is
unchanged when every rotation is followed by a fixed one (`weighting_model`).
-/
open MeasureTheory Metric Crossing Module Center
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Quaternion

namespace Weighting

section Quaternion
        LemmaWeighting.mul_eq_sphereEquivline 34
        /-- left multiplication by a unit quaternion on the unit sphere is the rotation `x ↦ qx` -/
lemma mul_eq_sphereEquiv (q : sphere (0 : ℍ) 1) :
    (fun ξ : sphere (0 : ℍ) 1 => q * ξ) = sphereEquiv (leftRot q) := by
  funext ξ
  exact Subtype.ext rfl

        
variable [MeasurableSpace ℍ] [BorelSpace ℍ] (μ : Measure ℍ) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure]
        TheoremWeighting.toSphere_isMulLeftInvariantline 42
        /-- the unit sphere's measure is kept by every rotation `x ↦ qx` (`Crossing.toSphere_preserving`) -/
instance toSphere_isMulLeftInvariant : μ.toSphere.IsMulLeftInvariant where
  map_mul_left_eq_self q := by
    rw [mul_eq_sphereEquiv]
    exact (toSphere_preserving μ (leftRot q)).map_eq
        TheoremWeighting.toSphere_isHaarMeasureline 48
        /-- the unit sphere's measure is a Haar measure of the unit quaternions: finite, kept by left
multiplication, and positive on open sets -/
instance toSphere_isHaarMeasure : μ.toSphere.IsHaarMeasure := {}
        TheoremWeighting.eq_toSphere_of_invariantline 52
        /-- **A probability measure on the unit three-sphere that every rotation `x ↦ qx` keeps is the unit
sphere's measure, normalized** (Sec. II).  The unit quaternions form a compact group, and a measure
on it that left multiplication keeps is a multiple of the unit sphere's measure, a Haar measure of
the group (`Measure.isMulInvariant_eq_smul_of_compactSpace`); the total `1` fixes the multiple. -/
theorem eq_toSphere_of_invariant (m : Measure (sphere (0 : ℍ) 1)) [IsProbabilityMeasure m]
    [m.IsMulLeftInvariant] : m = (μ.toSphere Set.univ)⁻¹ • μ.toSphere := by
  have h := Measure.isMulInvariant_eq_smul_of_compactSpace m μ.toSphere
  have h1 : (m.haarScalarFactor μ.toSphere : ℝ≥0∞) * μ.toSphere Set.univ = 1 := by
    have := congrArg (fun ν : Measure (sphere (0 : ℍ) 1) => ν Set.univ) h
    simp only [measure_univ, Measure.smul_apply] at this
    rw [this]
    rfl
  have h2 : (m.haarScalarFactor μ.toSphere : ℝ≥0∞) = (μ.toSphere Set.univ)⁻¹ :=
    ENNReal.eq_inv_of_mul_eq_one_left h1
  conv_lhs => rw [h]
  ext t ht
  rw [Measure.smul_apply, Measure.smul_apply, ← h2]
  rfl

        
omit [BorelSpace ℍ] [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] in
        LemmaWeighting.integral_normalizedline 72
        /-- the average of a function over the unit sphere's measure, normalized -/
lemma integral_normalized (f : sphere (0 : ℍ) 1 → ℝ) :
    ∫ ξ, f ξ ∂((μ.toSphere Set.univ)⁻¹ • μ.toSphere) =
      (∫ ξ, f ξ ∂μ.toSphere) / μ.toSphere.real Set.univ := by
  rw [integral_smul_measure, ENNReal.toReal_inv, smul_eq_mul, measureReal_def, div_eq_inv_mul]

        
end Quaternion

variable [MeasurableSpace ℍ] [BorelSpace ℍ]

  rw [evenWeight, Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]

        /-- **The premise that no rotation is preferred can be met**: the unit sphere's measure,
