        import RegisterGravity.Symmetry
import RegisterGravity.Quotients
import RegisterGravity.Einstein
import RegisterGravity.RouteB

/-!
# The space at an instant, and the solution it determines (Sec. IV.D)

Section IV.D finds the solution without a mass from its space at an instant.  This file carries
the step without taking completeness as a separate premise, and without the solution itself: the
space at an instant is complete because every geodesic of it closes along a ring (`hclose`,
Postulate 1's first sentence applied to space; the first link below), and its rings, with the
rings through the observer's cell drawn in it, make it the three-sphere, from which Einstein's
constraint gives `Λ`.  Starting from the spacetime would need its completeness as a premise, since
a homogeneous spacetime of constant curvature need not be
complete: the steady-state half of de Sitter space is one, and it is a quotient of none of the
three maximally symmetric spacetimes.  The step runs instead through the space at an instant of an
observer at rest, `Σ`, in three links.

* **The space forms** (`SpaceForm`).  `Σ` is totally geodesic, since the geometry about an observer
  at rest does not change in time (Sec. II); its geometry is the same at every place and in every
  direction (`Solution.geometry_same`), so its curvature is one number `K` (Schur's lemma); and it is
  complete, since a ring runs along every geodesic of space (Postulate 1's first sentence applied to
  `Σ`), so every geodesic closes.  By the Killing–Hopf theorem, `Σ` is the three-sphere of curvature
  `K`, Euclidean space or hyperbolic space, divided by a group `Γ` of isometries acting freely and
  properly discontinuously (`Sources.Geometry.space_form`); by Einstein's constraint on a time-symmetric
  slice without matter, `3K = Λ` (`Sources.Geometry.constraint`).
* **The slice's rings exclude the flat and hyperbolic forms** (`flat_space_no_rings`,
  `hyperbolic_space_no_rings`): a ring along every geodesic of `Σ`, of one length, would carry the
  center of a ball onto every point of a sphere about it by the group's maps, which a group acting
  properly discontinuously cannot do (`not_spread_space`).  So `K > 0` (`slice_sphere`).
* **The slice's rings exclude every quotient of the three-sphere** (`sphere_rings`).  Every great
  circle closes in the quotient with one length, so every map of `Γ` is `±1` on space: a map that
  is neither turns some plane by an angle below `2π` (`Quotients.exists_rotation_plane`), and the
  circle of that plane would close sooner than the circle of a plane that no map but `±1` turns
  onto itself (`Quotients.exists_plane_not_turned`).  And `−1` is excluded by the rings through the
  observer's cell, drawn in space (`RingsDrawn`, `Sources.P2.rings_drawn`: Sec. II's cell, a place
  on a ring, and Postulate 2's last sentence, with its first clause, the same opposite cell halfway
  around every largest ring through a cell).  With the antipodal points identified every ring
  closes after half a turn, so the opposite cell, halfway along, is a quarter turn from the
  observer's cell on every ring through it; two rings drawn through the one place of the observer's
  cell and the one place of its opposite lie on one great circle, and the cell one step on from the
  observer's cell along one falls on the place of the cell one step on, or back, along the other:
  two cells at one place, so one cell on both, while two rings through a cell share only it and its
  opposite.  So `Γ` is trivial, the space is the three-sphere itself, and every
  great circle has the length `2π√(1/K)`.

`cosmological_constant_of_sources` puts the links together: `Lℓ_c = 2π√(1/K) = 2π√(3/Λ)`, so
`Λ = 3/R_Λ²`.
-/

open Geodesic Quotients Symmetry RealInnerProductSpace

namespace Space

/-! ### Quotients of the three-sphere -/

section Sphere

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
        ObjectSpace.SphereQuotientline 62
        /-- **A quotient of the three-sphere** of radius `√k`, the waist of de Sitter space `form X X = k`
of `ℝ × E`, by a finite group `Γ` of rotations of space: its maps are linear maps of `ℝ × E` that
keep the form and the time of every point, so each rotates space and leaves time alone; those other
than the identity fix no point of the sphere; and there are finitely many, as a group acting
properly discontinuously on a compact sphere has. -/
structure SphereQuotient (k : ℝ) (Γ : Subgroup ((ℝ × E) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × E))) : Prop where
  iso : ∀ g ∈ Γ, ∀ x y : ℝ × E, form (g x) (g y) = form x y
  time : ∀ g ∈ Γ, ∀ x : ℝ × E, (g x).1 = x.1
  free : ∀ g ∈ Γ, ∀ y : E, ‖y‖ ^ 2 = k → g ((0 : ℝ), y) = ((0 : ℝ), y) → g = 1
  finite : (Γ : Set ((ℝ × E) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × E))).Finite
        DefinitionSpace.spaceMapline 73
        /-- the map of space that a map of `ℝ × E` makes: `y ↦ (g (0, y)).2`, the map `g` makes of the
places when it leaves time alone -/
def spaceMap (g : (ℝ × E) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × E)) : E →ₗ[ℝ] E :=
  LinearMap.snd ℝ ℝ E ∘ₗ ((g : (ℝ × E) →ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × E)) ∘ₗ LinearMap.inr ℝ ℝ E)
        LemmaSpace.spaceMap_applyline 78
        lemma spaceMap_apply (g : (ℝ × E) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × E)) (y : E) : spaceMap g y = (g ((0 : ℝ), y)).2 := rfl
        LemmaSpace.spaceMap_oneline 80
        lemma spaceMap_one (y : E) : spaceMap (1 : (ℝ × E) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × E)) y = y := rfl

        
end Sphere

/-! ### The flat and hyperbolic space forms have no rings -/

section Space

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
        TheoremSpace.not_spread_spaceline 90
        /-- **A group acting properly discontinuously on space does not carry a point onto every point of a
sphere about it**: the maps that do, one for each
unit vector `u`, are infinitely many, since the points `r u` are, and each carries the center `0` of
the ball of radius `r` into the ball. -/
theorem not_spread_space (hE : 2 ≤ Module.finrank ℝ E) {Γ : Set (Equiv.Perm E)}
    (hprop : ProperOn Γ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r)
    (h : ∀ u : E, ‖u‖ = 1 → ∃ g ∈ Γ, g 0 = r • u) : False := by
  obtain ⟨f₁, f₂, h1, h2, h12⟩ := exists_orthonormal_pair hE
  have hu : ∀ θ : ℝ, ‖Real.cos θ • f₁ + Real.sin θ • f₂‖ = 1 := fun θ => by
    have h := Crossing.norm_comb_sq h12 h1 h2 (Real.cos θ) (Real.sin θ)
    rw [Real.cos_sq_add_sin_sq, one_pow, one_mul] at h
    rw [← Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _), h, Real.sqrt_one]
  choose G hGΓ hG using fun θ : ℝ => h _ (hu θ)
  have hK : IsCompact (Metric.closedBall (0 : E) r) := isCompact_closedBall _ _
  have hinj : Set.InjOn G (Set.Icc 0 Real.pi) := by
    intro θ hθ θ' hθ' hGG
    have e : r • (Real.cos θ • f₁ + Real.sin θ • f₂) = r • (Real.cos θ' • f₁ + Real.sin θ' • f₂) := by
      rw [← hG θ, ← hG θ', hGG]
    have e2 := congrArg (fun p : E => ⟪f₁, p⟫) e
    simp only [inner_add_right, real_inner_smul_right, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, h1, h12] at e2
    apply Real.injOn_cos hθ hθ'
    have := mul_left_cancel₀ hr.ne' e2
    linarith
  have hmaps : Set.MapsTo G (Set.Icc 0 Real.pi)
      {g | g ∈ Γ ∧ ((⇑g) '' Metric.closedBall (0 : E) r ∩ Metric.closedBall 0 r).Nonempty} := by
    intro θ _
    refine ⟨hGΓ θ, G θ 0, ⟨0, Metric.mem_closedBall_self hr.le, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
    rw [hG θ, Metric.mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos hr,
      hu, mul_one]
  exact Set.infinite_of_injOn_mapsTo hinj hmaps (Set.Icc_infinite Real.pi_pos) (hprop _ hK)
        TheoremSpace.flat_space_no_ringsline 121
        /-- **Euclidean space has no quotient with rings** (Sec. IV.D): if every straight line closed in
the quotient by `Γ` with the length `len`, the line from `0` along each unit vector `u` would close
after `len`, at `len u`, which `not_spread_space` excludes.  Only that `Γ` acts properly
discontinuously is used. -/
theorem flat_space_no_rings (hE : 2 ≤ Module.finrank ℝ E) {Γ : Set (Equiv.Perm E)}
    (hprop : ProperOn Γ) {len : ℝ}
    (hring : ∀ u : E, ‖u‖ = 1 → ClosesIn Γ (fun t : ℝ => t • u) (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) len) :
    False := by
  obtain ⟨f₁, -, hf₁, -, -⟩ := exists_orthonormal_pair hE
  obtain ⟨P₀, hP₀, -, -, hlen₀⟩ := hring f₁ hf₁
  have hlen : 0 < len := by rw [← hlen₀ 0, one_mul]; exact hP₀
  refine not_spread_space hE hprop hlen fun u hu => ?_
  obtain ⟨P, -, ⟨g, hg, hgP⟩, -, hlenP⟩ := hring u hu
  have hPeq : P = len := by rw [← hlenP 0, one_mul]
  refine ⟨g, hg, ?_⟩
  have h0 := hgP 0
  simp only [zero_add, zero_smul] at h0
  rw [← h0, hPeq]
        TheoremSpace.hyperbolic_space_no_ringsline 140
        /-- **Hyperbolic space has no quotient with rings** (Sec. IV.D).  Hyperbolic space of radius `ℓ` is
the upper sheet of the quadric `form X X = −ℓ²` of `ℝ × E`, and the projection to `E` is a chart of
it on which `Γ` acts.  If every geodesic closed in the quotient with the length `len`, the geodesic
from the lowest point along each unit vector `u`, `t ↦ (ℓ cosh t, ℓ sinh t · u)`, of speed `ℓ`,
would close after `len/ℓ`, at `ℓ sinh(len/ℓ) · u` in the chart, which `not_spread_space` excludes.
Only that `Γ` acts properly discontinuously is used. -/
theorem hyperbolic_space_no_rings (hE : 2 ≤ Module.finrank ℝ E) {ℓ : ℝ} (hℓ : 0 < ℓ)
    {Γ : Set (Equiv.Perm E)} (hprop : ProperOn Γ) {len : ℝ}
    (hring : ∀ γ : Curve ℝ E, IsGeodesic (-(ℓ ^ 2)) γ → 0 < (γ.pos 0).1 →
      ClosesIn Γ (fun t => (γ.pos t).2) (speed γ) len) : False := by
  have hlift : ∀ u : E, ‖u‖ = 1 →
      ClosesIn Γ (fun t => (ℓ * Real.sinh t) • u) (fun _ => ℓ) len := by
    intro u hu
    have ha : ‖(ℓ : ℝ)‖ = ℓ := by rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos hℓ]
    have hb : ‖ℓ • u‖ = ℓ := by rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos hℓ, hu, mul_one]
    have hspeed : ∀ t, speed (hypCurve (ℓ : ℝ) (ℓ • u)) t = ℓ := fun t => by
      show Real.sqrt (-⟪Real.sinh t • (ℓ : ℝ), Real.sinh t • (ℓ : ℝ)⟫ +
        ⟪Real.cosh t • (ℓ • u), Real.cosh t • (ℓ • u)⟫) = ℓ
      rw [real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, norm_smul (Real.sinh t),
        norm_smul (Real.cosh t), ha, hb, Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs, mul_pow, mul_pow,
        sq_abs, sq_abs]
      have e : -(Real.sinh t ^ 2 * ℓ ^ 2) + Real.cosh t ^ 2 * ℓ ^ 2 = ℓ ^ 2 := by
        nlinarith [Real.cosh_sq t]
      rw [e, Real.sqrt_sq hℓ.le]
    have h0 : 0 < ((hypCurve (ℓ : ℝ) (ℓ • u)).pos 0).1 := by
      show 0 < Real.cosh 0 • (ℓ : ℝ)
      rw [Real.cosh_zero, one_smul]
      exact hℓ
    have hpos : (fun t => ((hypCurve (ℓ : ℝ) (ℓ • u)).pos t).2) = fun t => (ℓ * Real.sinh t) • u :=
      funext fun t => by
        show Real.sinh t • (ℓ • u) = (ℓ * Real.sinh t) • u
        rw [smul_smul, mul_comm]
    have hsp : speed (hypCurve (ℓ : ℝ) (ℓ • u)) = fun _ => ℓ := funext hspeed
    have hc := hring _ (hypCurve_geodesic ha hb) h0
    rw [hpos, hsp] at hc
    exact hc
  obtain ⟨f₁, -, hf₁, -, -⟩ := exists_orthonormal_pair hE
  obtain ⟨P₀, hP₀, -, -, hlen₀⟩ := hlift f₁ hf₁
  have hlen : 0 < len := by rw [← hlen₀ 0]; exact mul_pos hℓ hP₀
  have hsinh : 0 < Real.sinh (len / ℓ) := by
    rw [Real.sinh_eq]
    have := Real.exp_lt_exp.2 (show -(len / ℓ) < len / ℓ by linarith [div_pos hlen hℓ])
    linarith
  refine not_spread_space hE hprop (mul_pos hℓ hsinh) fun u hu => ?_
  obtain ⟨P, -, ⟨g, hg, hgP⟩, -, hlenP⟩ := hlift u hu
  have hPeq : P = len / ℓ := by
    rw [← hlenP 0]
    field_simp
  refine ⟨g, hg, ?_⟩
  have h0 := hgP 0
  simp only [zero_add, Real.sinh_zero, mul_zero, zero_smul] at h0
  rw [← h0, hPeq]

        
end Space

/-! ### The space forms of the space at an instant -/
        ObjectSpace.SpaceFormline 197
        /-- **The space forms of dimension three** (Sec. IV.D): by the Killing–Hopf theorem a complete,
connected Riemannian 3-manifold of constant curvature `K` is the three-sphere of curvature `K`,
Euclidean space or hyperbolic space, divided by a group `Γ` of isometries acting freely and properly
discontinuously [J. M. Lee, *Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds*, 2nd ed. (2018), p. 348;
H. Hopf, Math. Ann. **95**, 313 (1926)].  The sphere is the waist of de Sitter space
`form X X = 1/K` of `ℝ × ℝ⁴`, and `Γ` a finite group of rotations of space kept as maps of
`ℝ × ℝ⁴` (`SphereQuotient`); Euclidean space is `ℝ³`; hyperbolic space is the upper sheet of
`form X X = 1/K` of `ℝ × ℝ³`, on whose chart `ℝ³` the group acts. -/
inductive SpaceForm (K : ℝ) : Type
  /-- the three-sphere of curvature `K`, divided by `Γ` -/
  | sphere (Γ : Subgroup ((ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4))))
      (hK : 0 < K) (hΓ : SphereQuotient (1 / K) Γ)
  /-- Euclidean space, divided by `Γ` -/
  | flat (Γ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)))) (hK : K = 0)
      (hΓ : ProperOn (Γ : Set (Equiv.Perm (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)))))
  /-- hyperbolic space of curvature `K`, divided by `Γ` -/
  | hyperbolic (Γ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)))) (hK : K < 0)
      (hΓ : ProperOn (Γ : Set (Equiv.Perm (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)))))
        DefinitionSpace.sphereSlotsline 216
        /-- the great circles of the waist of de Sitter space `form X X = k`: the geodesics of the
three-sphere of radius `√k` -/
def sphereSlots (k : ℝ) : Set (Curve ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4))) :=
  {γ | IsGeodesic k γ ∧ InSpace γ ∧ IsSpacelike γ}
        DefinitionSpace.lineSlotsline 221
        /-- the straight lines of Euclidean space, each by a point and a velocity -/
def lineSlots : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) := {pv | pv.2 ≠ 0}
        DefinitionSpace.hypSlotsline 224
        /-- the geodesics of hyperbolic space, the upper sheet of the quadric `form X X = k < 0` -/
def hypSlots (k : ℝ) : Set (Curve ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))) :=
  {γ | IsGeodesic k γ ∧ 0 < (γ.pos 0).1}
        DefinitionSpace.SpaceForm.Slotline 228
        /-- the slots of a space form, the type in which the files name its geodesics: curves of the
three-sphere's ambient space, lines of Euclidean space by a point and a velocity, curves of the
hyperboloid -/
def SpaceForm.Slot {K : ℝ} : SpaceForm K → Type
  | .sphere _ _ _ => Curve ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4))
  | .flat _ _ _ => EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

        /-- a geodesic of a space form closes in the quotient by its group with the length `len` -/
def SpaceForm.closes {K : ℝ} (len : ℝ) : (c : SpaceForm K) → c.Slot → Prop
  | .sphere Γ _ _ => fun γ =>
      ClosesIn (Γ : Set ((ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4))))
        γ.pos (speed γ) len
  | .flat Γ _ _ => fun pv =>
      ClosesIn (Γ : Set (Equiv.Perm (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)))) (fun t => pv.1 + t • pv.2)
        (fun _ => ‖pv.2‖) len
  | .hyperbolic Γ _ _ => fun γ =>
      ClosesIn (Γ : Set (Equiv.Perm (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)))) (fun t => (γ.pos t).2) (speed γ) len

theorem slice_sphere {H : Horizon L} {len K : ℝ} (c : SpaceForm K) (h : SliceIsQubits H len c) :

    rw [finrank_euclideanSpace_fin]; norm_num

    have hm := (mem_described_admissible _ _).1 (h ((0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)), u) hu0)

    exfalso

      have : 1 / K < 0 := one_div_neg.2 hK
      linarith

lemma sphereSlots_pos {k : ℝ} (hk : 0 < k) {γ : Curve ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4))}

        DefinitionSpace.RingsDrawnline 318
        /-- **The rings through the cell `B`, drawn in the space at an instant** (Sec. II and Postulate 2
at the observer's cell; `Sources.P2.rings_drawn`), the space being the three-sphere of radius `√k`
divided by `Γ`.  "A ring is a closed line of translation in space; a cell is a place on a ring"
(Sec. II), and "every largest ring is a closed geodesic of space, made of its cells as segments of
length `ℓ_c`" (Postulate 2): each largest ring `l` through `B` runs along a great circle `γ l` that
closes in the quotient with the length `Lℓ_c`, `L` its number of cells, and the cell `j` steps
from `B` along `l` (`Horizon.Positions.offset`) is placed at the point of `γ l` at the arc length
`jℓ_c`, its place `pl l X`, up to `Γ`, where its segment begins.  Any other point of the segment
would do, by starting `γ l` elsewhere: the proof uses differences of arc length only.  The cells
of the drawn rings are places, Sec. II's "a cell is a place" read as an identity, in both
directions: the same cell drawn on two of the rings is at one place (`←`), and two cells are two
places (`→`).  The cells that two of the rings share are `B` itself and its opposite, "one
opposite, the same cell halfway around every largest ring through it" (Postulate 2, first clause;
`Horizon.Positions.offset_opp_self`); `→` is the direction with which `sphere_rings` excludes the
antipodal quotient.  So at the observer's cell the files take a cell's place to be a point of the
manifold, for the rings through it, as Sec. II states: "For an observer at rest, the manifold
describes the register's incidence, that is, which rings share a cell, only for the rings through
his cell".  Every cell lies on a ring through `B`
(`Horizon.exists_loop_through`), so every cell is drawn, at one place.  Nothing is said of the
rings off `B`: drawn through the places of their cells as well, the rings would draw the register's
incidence with its cells as points and its rings as great circles, which the Sylvester–Gallai
theorem forbids for `L ≥ 6` [P. Erdős, Problem 4065, Amer. Math. Monthly 50, 65 (1943);
R. Steinberg, solution, ibid. 51, 169 (1944)]; the rings of one cell are all that `sphere_rings`

def RingsDrawn (H : Horizon L) (P : H.Positions) (k : ℝ)
    (Γ : Subgroup ((ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4))))

        /-- **The rings of the space at an instant exclude every quotient of the three-sphere** (Sec. IV.D).
Let the space be the three-sphere of radius `√k` divided by a finite group `Γ` of rotations acting
freely (`SphereQuotient`), let every great circle close in the quotient with the length `len`
(`hring`), and let the rings through the cell `B` be drawn in it (`hdrawn`, `RingsDrawn`).  Then
`Γ` is trivial and `len = 2π√k`.
* Every map of `Γ` is `±1` on space.  A great circle's least period is `len/√k`, the same for all.
  A map `g` other than `±1` turns some plane of space by an angle `0 < θ < 2π`
  (`Quotients.exists_rotation_plane`), so the circle in that plane returns after `θ`: `len/√k ≤ θ`.
  Some plane is turned onto itself by no map of `Γ` other than `±1`
  (`Quotients.exists_plane_not_turned`), and its circle returns only by `1`, after a multiple of
  `2π`, or by `−1`, after `π` and then `len/√k ≥ π`; in the first case `len/√k ≥ 2π > θ`.  In the
  second, `−g` is in `Γ` and turns the plane of `g` by `θ + π`, so `len/√k ≤ θ ± π < π` unless
  `θ = π`, when `−g` fixes a vector of the plane, which a map of `Γ` other than `1` cannot, and
  `g = −1`.
* No map of `Γ` is `−1` on space.  Were one, every great circle would return after `π` and by
  `±1` at its least period, so `len = π√k`, and the places of a drawn ring would be up to sign.
  A drawn ring closes with `Lℓ_c`, the one length, so its cell `j` steps from `B` sits at the angle
  `jπ/L` from `B`'s place, and its opposite cell, `L/2` steps on
  (`Horizon.Positions.offset_opp_self`), a quarter turn on.  Two different rings through `B`
  (`Horizon.two_mul_card_through`) are drawn through the one place of `B`, up to sign, and the one
  place of its opposite, up to sign, so they lie on one great circle, one the other reflected or
  not.  Then the cell one step from `B` on the second falls on the place of the cell one step from
  `B` on the first, or of the cell one step back, up to sign; two cells at one place are one cell
  (`RingsDrawn`), on both rings, and not `B` or its opposite, while two rings through `B` share

multiple of `2π` and at `2π`: `len = 2π√k`. -/

          nlinarith [Real.pi_pos]
        nlinarith [Real.pi_pos]
      -- `h * g` is in `Γ`, is `−g` on space, and turns the plane of `g` by `θ + π`
      have hhg : h * g ∈ Γ := Γ.mul_mem hh hg
      have hAhg : ∀ y, spaceMap (h * g) y = -(spaceMap g y) := fun y => by
        rw [hAmul h g hh hg, hneg]
      have hAu' : spaceMap (h * g) u = Real.cos (θ + Real.pi) • u + Real.sin (θ + Real.pi) • w := by
        rw [hAhg, hAu, Real.cos_add_pi, Real.sin_add_pi]
        module
      have hAw' : spaceMap (h * g) w =
          (-Real.sin (θ + Real.pi)) • u + Real.cos (θ + Real.pi) • w := by
        rw [hAhg, hAw, Real.cos_add_pi, Real.sin_add_pi]
        module
      rcases lt_trichotomy θ Real.pi with hlt | heq | hgt
      · linarith
      · -- `θ = π`: `h * g` fixes `u`, so `h * g = 1` and `g = −1` on space
        have hfixu : spaceMap (h * g) u = u := by
          rw [hAu', heq, ← two_mul, Real.cos_two_pi, Real.sin_two_pi, one_smul, zero_smul, add_zero]
        have hhg1 : h * g = 1 := by
          by_contra hne
          have := hAfix (h * g) hhg hne u hfixu
          rw [this, norm_zero] at hu
          exact zero_ne_one hu
        apply hgneg.elim
        intro y hy
        have := hAhg y
        rw [hhg1, spaceMap_one] at this
        exact hy (neg_eq_iff_eq_neg.1 this.symm)
      · -- `θ > π`: the plane returns after `θ − π < π`
        have hAu'' : spaceMap (h * g) u =
            Real.cos (θ - Real.pi) • u + Real.sin (θ - Real.pi) • w := by
          rw [hAu', Real.cos_sub_pi, Real.sin_sub_pi, Real.cos_add_pi, Real.sin_add_pi]
        have hAw'' : spaceMap (h * g) w =
            (-Real.sin (θ - Real.pi)) • u + Real.cos (θ - Real.pi) • w := by
          rw [hAw', Real.cos_sub_pi, Real.sin_sub_pi, Real.cos_add_pi, Real.sin_add_pi]
        have := hleast (θ - Real.pi) (by linarith)
          ⟨h * g, hhg, hturn u w (h * g) hhg _ hAu'' hAw''⟩
        linarith
  -- no map of `Γ` is `−1` on space: the rings through `B` are drawn through one place of `B` and
  -- one place of its opposite
  have hone : ∀ g ∈ Γ, g = 1 := by
    intro g hg
    rcases hpm g hg with h | hneg
    · exact h
    · exfalso
      obtain ⟨b, hbdef⟩ : ∃ b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin 4) ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)),
        b = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 4) ℝ := ⟨_, rfl⟩
      have hb : ∀ i j, ⟪b i, b j⟫ = if i = j then 1 else 0 := orthonormal_iff_ite.1 b.orthonormal
      have hbn : ∀ i, ‖b i‖ = 1 := b.orthonormal.1
      have hb12 : ⟪b 1, b 2⟫ = 0 := by rw [hb]; simp
      -- every great circle returns after `π`: `len/s ≤ π`
      obtain ⟨hP0, ⟨h₁, hh₁, hh₁P⟩, hleast⟩ := hP (b 1) (b 2) (hbn 1) (hbn 2) hb12
      have hPπ : len / s ≤ Real.pi := hleast Real.pi Real.pi_pos ⟨g, hg, hturn _ _ g hg Real.pi
        (by rw [hneg, Real.cos_pi, Real.sin_pi]; module)
        (by rw [hneg, Real.cos_pi, Real.sin_pi]; module)⟩
      -- and the return after the least period `len/s` is by `±1`, so `len/s = π`
      obtain ⟨h1, -⟩ := hret (b 1) (b 2) h₁ hh₁ _ hh₁P
      have hcosP : Real.cos (len / s) = ⟪spaceMap h₁ (b 1), b 1⟫ := by
        rw [h1, inner_add_left, real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_left,
          real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hbn 1, real_inner_comm, hb12]
        ring
      have hlen : len = Real.pi * s := by
        rcases hpm h₁ hh₁ with rfl | hneg₁
        · rw [spaceMap_one, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hbn 1, one_pow] at hcosP
          obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := (Real.cos_eq_one_iff _).1 hcosP
          have hpos' : (0 : ℝ) < n * (2 * Real.pi) := by rw [hn]; exact hP0
          have hn1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ n := by
            have : (0 : ℝ) < n := pos_of_mul_pos_left hpos' (by positivity)
            exact_mod_cast (show (0 : ℤ) < n by exact_mod_cast this)
          exfalso
          nlinarith [Real.pi_pos]
        · rw [hneg₁, inner_neg_left, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hbn 1, one_pow] at hcosP
          obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := Real.cos_eq_neg_one_iff.1 hcosP
          have h0 : (0 : ℝ) < Real.pi + n * (2 * Real.pi) := by rw [hn]; exact hP0
          have h1' : Real.pi + n * (2 * Real.pi) ≤ Real.pi := by rw [hn]; exact hPπ
          have hlt : (-1 : ℝ) < 2 * n := by nlinarith [Real.pi_pos]
          have hle : (2 * n : ℝ) ≤ 0 := by nlinarith [Real.pi_pos]
          have hlt' : (-1 : ℤ) < 2 * n := by exact_mod_cast hlt
          have hle' : 2 * n ≤ (0 : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast hle
          have hn0 : n = 0 := by omega
          rw [hn0] at hn
          simp only [Int.cast_zero, zero_mul, add_zero] at hn
          rw [hn]
          field_simp
      -- two different largest rings through `B`
      have hL : 4 ≤ L := H.four_le
      obtain ⟨l, l', hl, hl', hll'⟩ : ∃ l l' : H.Loop, B ∈ H.cells l ∧ B ∈ H.cells l' ∧ l ≠ l' := by
        have hcard := H.two_mul_card_through hL B
        obtain ⟨l, hl, l', hl', hne⟩ :=
          Finset.one_lt_card.1 (show 1 < (H.through B).card by omega)
        exact ⟨l, l', H.mem_through.1 hl, H.mem_through.1 hl', hne⟩
      obtain ⟨γ, pl, hrings, hcells, hplaces⟩ := hdrawn
      -- in this quotient a place is given up to sign
      have hsign : ∀ y z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4),
          (∃ g' ∈ Γ, ((0 : ℝ), y) = g' ((0 : ℝ), z)) ↔ (y = z ∨ y = -z) := by
        intro y z
        constructor
        · rintro ⟨g', hg', e⟩
          rw [hAy g' hg'] at e
          rcases hpm g' hg' with rfl | hneg'
          · left; rw [spaceMap_one] at e; exact (Prod.ext_iff.1 e).2
          · right; rw [hneg'] at e; exact (Prod.ext_iff.1 e).2
        · rintro (rfl | rfl)
          · exact ⟨1, Γ.one_mem, rfl⟩
          · exact ⟨g, hg, by rw [hAy g hg, hneg]⟩
      have hcomb : ∀ {y z w : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)},
          (y = z ∨ y = -z) → (z = w ∨ z = -w) → (y = w ∨ y = -w) := by
        rintro y z w (rfl | rfl) (rfl | rfl) <;> simp
      have hsymm : ∀ {y z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)}, (y = z ∨ y = -z) → (z = y ∨ z = -y) := by
        rintro y z (rfl | rfl) <;> simp
      have hnegl : ∀ {y z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)}, (-y = z ∨ -y = -z) → (y = z ∨ y = -z) := by
        rintro y z (h | h)
        · right; rw [← h, neg_neg]
        · left; exact neg_inj.1 h
      -- a drawn ring: its cell `j` steps from `B` sits at the angle `jπ/L` from `B`'s place
      have hL0 : (0 : ℝ) < L := by exact_mod_cast (show 0 < L by omega)
      have hcircle : ∀ (l₁ : H.Loop) (hl₁ : B ∈ H.cells l₁),
          ∃ a c : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4), ‖a‖ = s ∧ ‖c‖ = s ∧ ⟪a, c⟫ = 0 ∧
            ∀ X ∈ H.cells l₁, (Real.cos ((P.offset l₁ B X : ℝ) * Real.pi / L) • a +
              Real.sin ((P.offset l₁ B X : ℝ) * Real.pi / L) • c = pl l₁ hl₁ X) ∨
              (Real.cos ((P.offset l₁ B X : ℝ) * Real.pi / L) • a +
              Real.sin ((P.offset l₁ B X : ℝ) * Real.pi / L) • c = -pl l₁ hl₁ X) := by
        intro l₁ hl₁
        obtain ⟨hslot, hclose⟩ := hrings l₁ hl₁
        obtain ⟨a, c, ha, hc, hac, hpos'⟩ := sphereSlots_pos hk hslot
        rw [← hsdef] at ha hc hpos'
        -- the drawn ring closes with `Lℓ_c`, the one length `len`
        have hLℓ : (L : ℝ) * ℓc = len := by
          obtain ⟨P₁, hP₁, hret₁, hmin₁, hlen₁⟩ := hclose
          obtain ⟨P₂, hP₂, hret₂, hmin₂, hlen₂⟩ := hring _ hslot
          have e : P₁ = P₂ := le_antisymm (hmin₁ P₂ hP₂ hret₂) (hmin₂ P₁ hP₁ hret₁)
          rw [← hlen₁ 0, ← hlen₂ 0, e]
        have hv : 0 < speed (γ l₁ hl₁) 0 := Real.sqrt_pos.2 (hslot.2.2 0)
        refine ⟨a, c, ha, hc, hac, fun X hX => ?_⟩
        obtain ⟨g', hg', e⟩ := hcells l₁ hl₁ X hX
        have hin : ((γ l₁ hl₁).pos ((P.offset l₁ B X : ℝ) * ℓc / speed (γ l₁ hl₁) 0)).1 = 0 :=
          hslot.2.1 _
        have e' : ((0 : ℝ), ((γ l₁ hl₁).pos ((P.offset l₁ B X : ℝ) * ℓc / speed (γ l₁ hl₁) 0)).2)
            = g' ((0 : ℝ), pl l₁ hl₁ X) := by
          rw [← e]; exact Prod.ext hin.symm rfl
        have hℓ : ℓc = Real.pi * s / L := by rw [eq_div_iff hL0.ne', mul_comm, hLℓ, hlen]
        have hang : speed (γ l₁ hl₁) 0 / s * ((P.offset l₁ B X : ℝ) * ℓc / speed (γ l₁ hl₁) 0)
            = (P.offset l₁ B X : ℝ) * Real.pi / L := by
          rw [hℓ]
          field_simp
        have := (hsign _ _).1 ⟨g', hg', e'⟩
        rw [hpos', hang] at this
        exact this
      obtain ⟨a, c, ha, hc, hac, hA⟩ := hcircle l hl
      obtain ⟨a', c', ha', hc', hac', hA'⟩ := hcircle l' hl'
      -- the angles of `B`, of its opposite, and of the cells one step from `B`, on and back
      have hθ0 : ∀ l₁, (P.offset l₁ B B : ℝ) * Real.pi / L = 0 := fun l₁ => by
        rw [P.offset_self]; simp
      obtain ⟨hf, hL2, hh⟩ := H.exists_half hL
      have hθh : ∀ l₁ (hl₁ : B ∈ H.cells l₁),
          (P.offset l₁ B (H.opp B) : ℝ) * Real.pi / L = Real.pi / 2 := fun l₁ hl₁ => by
        rw [P.offset_opp_self hL l₁ B hl₁, hh]
        have hL' : (L : ℝ) = 2 * hf := by exact_mod_cast hL2
        have hf0 : (hf : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (show hf ≠ 0 by omega)
        rw [hL']
        field_simp
      have hθ1 : ((1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.pi / L = Real.pi / L := by simp
      have hθL : ((L - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.pi / L = Real.pi - Real.pi / L := by
        rw [Nat.cast_sub (by omega), Nat.cast_one]
        field_simp
      -- `B` is drawn at one place on both rings: `a' = ±a`
      have hBl := hA B hl
      have hBl' := hA' B hl'
      rw [hθ0, Real.cos_zero, Real.sin_zero, one_smul, zero_smul, add_zero] at hBl hBl'
      have hBB : pl l hl B = pl l' hl' B ∨ pl l hl B = -pl l' hl' B :=
        (hsign _ _).1 ((hplaces l hl l' hl' B hl B hl').2 rfl)
      have haa : a' = a ∨ a' = -a := hcomb hBl' (hcomb (hsymm hBB) (hsymm hBl))
      -- and so is its opposite, a quarter turn on: `c' = ±c`
      have hOl := hA (H.opp B) (H.opp_mem l B hl)
      have hOl' := hA' (H.opp B) (H.opp_mem l' B hl')
      rw [hθh l hl, Real.cos_pi_div_two, Real.sin_pi_div_two, zero_smul, one_smul, zero_add] at hOl
      rw [hθh l' hl', Real.cos_pi_div_two, Real.sin_pi_div_two, zero_smul, one_smul,
        zero_add] at hOl'
      have hOO : pl l hl (H.opp B) = pl l' hl' (H.opp B) ∨
          pl l hl (H.opp B) = -pl l' hl' (H.opp B) :=
        (hsign _ _).1 ((hplaces l hl l' hl' _ (H.opp_mem l B hl) _ (H.opp_mem l' B hl')).2 rfl)
      have hcc : c' = c ∨ c' = -c := hcomb hOl' (hcomb (hsymm hOO) (hsymm hOl))
      -- the cell one step from `B` on `l'`, and the cells one step from `B` on `l`, on and back
      obtain ⟨X', hX', hoX'⟩ := P.exists_offset l' B 1 (by omega)
      obtain ⟨X₁, hX₁, hoX₁⟩ := P.exists_offset l B 1 (by omega)
      obtain ⟨Y, hY, hoY⟩ := P.exists_offset l B (L - 1) (by omega)
      have hpX' := hA' X' hX'
      have hpX₁ := hA X₁ hX₁
      have hpY := hA Y hY
      rw [hoX', hθ1] at hpX'
      rw [hoX₁, hθ1] at hpX₁
      rw [hoY, hθL, Real.cos_pi_sub, Real.sin_pi_sub] at hpY
      -- two cells at one place are one cell, on both rings, and not `B` or its opposite
      have hcontra : ∀ Z ∈ H.cells l, Z ∈ H.cells l' → P.offset l B Z ≠ 0 →
          P.offset l B Z ≠ L / 2 → False := by
        intro Z hZ hZ' h0 hh'
        have hZB : Z ≠ B := fun e => h0 (by rw [e, P.offset_self])
        have hZO : Z ≠ H.opp B := fun e => hh' (by rw [e, P.offset_opp_self hL l B hl])
        exact hll' (H.unique_loop B Z l l' hZB hZO hl hZ hl' hZ')
      have hsame : ∀ Z ∈ H.cells l,
          (pl l hl Z = pl l' hl' X' ∨ pl l hl Z = -pl l' hl' X') → Z = X' :=
        fun Z hZ h => (hplaces l hl l' hl' Z hZ X' hX').1 ((hsign _ _).2 h)
      rcases haa with haa | haa <;> rcases hcc with hcc | hcc <;> rw [haa, hcc] at hpX'
      · -- the same circle, run the same way: `X'` falls on the cell one step on
        have hX₁X' : X₁ = X' := hsame X₁ hX₁ (hcomb (hsymm hpX₁) hpX')
        exact hcontra X₁ hX₁ (hX₁X' ▸ hX') (by omega) (by omega)
      · -- the same circle, run the other way: `X'` falls on the cell one step back
        have e : Real.cos (Real.pi / L) • a + Real.sin (Real.pi / L) • -c =
            -((-Real.cos (Real.pi / L)) • a + Real.sin (Real.pi / L) • c) := by module
        rw [e] at hpX'
        have hYX' : Y = X' := hsame Y hY (hcomb (hsymm hpY) (hnegl hpX'))
        exact hcontra Y hY (hYX' ▸ hX') (by omega) (by omega)
      · have e : Real.cos (Real.pi / L) • -a + Real.sin (Real.pi / L) • c =
            (-Real.cos (Real.pi / L)) • a + Real.sin (Real.pi / L) • c := by module
        rw [e] at hpX'
        have hYX' : Y = X' := hsame Y hY (hcomb (hsymm hpY) hpX')
        exact hcontra Y hY (hYX' ▸ hX') (by omega) (by omega)
      · have e : Real.cos (Real.pi / L) • -a + Real.sin (Real.pi / L) • -c =
            -(Real.cos (Real.pi / L) • a + Real.sin (Real.pi / L) • c) := by module
        rw [e] at hpX'
        have hX₁X' : X₁ = X' := hsame X₁ hX₁ (hcomb (hsymm hpX₁) (hnegl hpX'))
        exact hcontra X₁ hX₁ (hX₁X' ▸ hX') (by omega) (by omega)
  -- `Γ` is trivial, and a great circle returns only after a full turn
  have hbot : Γ = ⊥ := (Subgroup.eq_bot_iff_forall Γ).2 hone
  refine ⟨hbot, ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨f₁, f₂, hf₁, hf₂, hf₁₂⟩ := exists_orthonormal_pair hE
  obtain ⟨hP0, ⟨g, hg, hgP⟩, hleast⟩ := hP f₁ f₂ hf₁ hf₂ hf₁₂
  have hP2 : len / s ≤ 2 * Real.pi := hleast _ Real.two_pi_pos ⟨1, Γ.one_mem, hturn _ _ 1 Γ.one_mem
    (2 * Real.pi) (by rw [spaceMap_one, Real.cos_two_pi, Real.sin_two_pi]; module)
    (by rw [spaceMap_one, Real.cos_two_pi, Real.sin_two_pi]; module)⟩
  obtain rfl := hone g hg
  obtain ⟨h1, -⟩ := hret f₁ f₂ 1 Γ.one_mem _ hgP
  have hcosP : Real.cos (len / s) = 1 := by
    have e := congrArg (fun x => ⟪x, f₁⟫) h1
    simp only [spaceMap_one, inner_add_left, real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hf₁,
      one_pow, mul_one, real_inner_comm f₁ f₂, hf₁₂, mul_zero, add_zero] at e
    exact e.symm
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := (Real.cos_eq_one_iff _).1 hcosP
  have hpos' : (0 : ℝ) < n * (2 * Real.pi) := by rw [hn]; exact hP0
  have hn1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ n := by
    have : (0 : ℝ) < n := pos_of_mul_pos_left hpos' (by positivity)
    exact_mod_cast (show (0 : ℤ) < n by exact_mod_cast this)
  have hP2' : 2 * Real.pi ≤ len / s := by
    rw [← hn]
    nlinarith [Real.pi_pos]
  have e : len / s = 2 * Real.pi := le_antisymm hP2 hP2'
  rw [← hsdef, ← e]
  field_simp

        
/-! ### The cosmological constant -/
        TheoremSpace.cosmological_constant_of_sourcesline 791
        /-- **The cosmological constant from the sources** (Sec. IV.D), every link named.

* The geometry of the space at an instant is the same at every slot (`hsame`, proved in
  `Solution` from Postulate 1's first sentence applied to the geometry), and every geodesic of that
  space closes (`hclose`, Postulate 1's first sentence applied to the space at an instant, a ring
  along every geodesic).  By Schur's lemma, Hopf–Rinow and the Killing–Hopf theorem the space is a
  space form (`hKH`, Riemannian geometry, `Sources.Geometry.space_form`).
* Without matter the vacuum equations hold with `Λ` (`hvac`, derived in
  `Einstein.einstein_equations` and `Einstein.vacuum_of_field_equations`), and on the
  time-symmetric slice of an observer at rest Einstein's constraint gives `3K = Λ`
  (`hcon`, `Sources.Geometry.constraint`).
* The slice's rings make the form the sphere (`hslice`, `slice_sphere`), and with the rings
  through the observer's cell `B` drawn in it (`hdrawn`, Sec. II's cell and Postulate 2's last
  sentence with its first clause, `Sources.P2.rings_drawn`) they make its group trivial and its
  great circles of length `2π√(1/K)` (`sphere_rings`).

Then `len = 2π√(1/K) = 2π√(3/Λ)`, and with `len = Lℓ_c = 2πR_Λ`, `Λ = 3/R_Λ²`.  The drawn rings
close with `Lℓ_c`, `L` the register's number of cells per ring, and every great circle with
`R.L ℓ_c` (`hslice`), so the two hypotheses together give `L = R.L` (`Condition.same_L`), which
`sphere_rings` uses through the uniqueness of a closed curve's least period; where `L ≠ R.L` they
cannot both hold. -/
theorem cosmological_constant_of_sources {Slot Gm Sp : Type*} (H : Horizon L) [NeZero L]
    (P : H.Positions) (B : H.Cell)
    (R : Register.Reg) {Λ : ℝ} (geom : Slot → Gm) (hsame : ∀ σ τ : Slot, geom σ = geom τ)
    (Closes : Slot → Prop) (hclose : ringsAlong H Set.univ Closes)
    (sp : Sp) (embedSp : (K : ℝ) → SpaceForm K → Sp)
    (hKH : (∀ σ τ : Slot, geom σ = geom τ) → (∀ σ, Closes σ) →
      ∃ K, ∃ c : SpaceForm K, sp = embedSp K c)
    (M : Register.Einstein.Spacetime) (hvac : Register.Einstein.VacuumEinstein M Set.univ Λ)
    (hcon : Register.Einstein.VacuumEinstein M Set.univ Λ →
      ∀ K (c : SpaceForm K), sp = embedSp K c → 3 * K = Λ)
    (hslice : ∀ K (c : SpaceForm K), sp = embedSp K c → SliceIsQubits H (R.L * R.ℓc) c)
    (hdrawn : ∀ K Γ (hK : 0 < K) (hΓ : SphereQuotient (1 / K) Γ),
      sp = embedSp K (SpaceForm.sphere Γ hK hΓ) → RingsDrawn H P (1 / K) Γ R.ℓc B) :
    Λ = 3 / R.RL ^ 2 := by
  have hcl : ∀ σ, Closes σ := fun σ =>
    ((mem_described_admissible _ σ).1 (hclose σ (Set.mem_univ σ))).2
  obtain ⟨K, c, hc⟩ := hKH hsame hcl
  have h3K := hcon hvac K c hc
  obtain ⟨Γ, hK, hΓ, rfl⟩ := slice_sphere c (hslice K c hc)
  have hk : 0 < 1 / K := one_div_pos.2 hK
  have hS := hslice K _ hc
  obtain ⟨-, hlen⟩ := sphere_rings hk hΓ
    (fun γ hγ => ((mem_described_admissible _ _).1 (hS γ hγ)).2) H P B (hdrawn K Γ hK hΓ hc)
  -- `Lℓ_c = 2πR_Λ = 2π√(1/K)`, so `1/K = R_Λ²` and `Λ = 3K = 3/R_Λ²`
  have hRL := R.RL_pos
  have e : R.L * R.ℓc = 2 * Real.pi * R.RL := by
    unfold Register.Reg.RL
    rw [R.pi_def]
    field_simp
  rw [e] at hlen
  have hsq : Real.sqrt (1 / K) = R.RL := by
    have := Real.pi_pos
    nlinarith [hlen]
  have hK' : 1 / K = R.RL ^ 2 := by
    rw [← hsq, Real.sq_sqrt hk.le]
  rw [← h3K]
  field_simp
  rw [one_div] at hK'
  have : K = 1 / R.RL ^ 2 := by
    rw [← inv_inv K, hK', one_div]
  rw [this]
  field_simp

        
end Space

        import RegisterGravity.Symmetry
import RegisterGravity.Bridge
import RegisterGravity.Capacity
import RegisterGravity.Qubit
import RegisterGravity.Cosmo
import RegisterGravity.Space

/-!
# The solution without a mass, from the symmetry of space (Sec. IV.D)

Section IV.D finds the solution of Einstein's equations without a mass from the symmetry of space.
This file states each link: as a theorem, as the first sentence of Postulate 1 applied (every
physical law and quantity is defined by qubits, the thesis of the paper), or as a cited theorem of
geometry, with its inputs proved or taken from the postulates.

* **The state is the same at every crossing** (`state_same`, a theorem).  Without a mass every
  string's qubit is in the thermal state of its tick, at one inverse temperature `β` (`hthermal`,
  `Qubit.Tick.state`, thermodynamics); this is where "without a mass" enters.  The two senses are
  the qubit's two outcomes (Sec. II), and they have one energy, since the tick's phase changes
  alike in either sense, by the clause of Postulate 2 on directions (`hsense` of `Qubit.Tick`):
  the tick multiplies both by one factor, and a string's energy is the energy of its factor
  (`Qubit.Tick.factor_eq`, `Qubit.Tick.energy_eq`).  So the thermal state, the Gibbs state over
  the two senses at their energies (the definition `Qubit.Tick.state`), is half the identity
  (`Qubit.Tick.state_eq`): each sense has the probability `1/2`.  Each cell's bit is one possible outcome among the `L` (`halike`,
  Postulate 1).  So the state seen where a ring crosses a cell (`crossingState`) is the same at
  every crossing.  That state is the string's thermal state with the cell's bit as one possible
  outcome, and the string's correlation with the other strings, which free strings make zero
  (`hfree`, `Entropy.correlation_jointProb`).  `crossingState` names what it leaves out, and why:
  the string's bits, its phase and its own energy.  That half the bits of a string in that state
  are 1s, on average, is `Qubit.half_bits_thermal`.
* **The geometry is the same at every place and in every direction** (`geometry_same`, a theorem).
  The geometry of space at a slot, the curvature of the plane normal to the slot's direction and
  the rate at which that curvature changes, is qubits: it is read off the laws and the state at the
  slot (`hgeom : IsQubits …`).  This is Postulate 1's first sentence, every physical law and
  quantity defined by qubits, for the geometry of space (`Symmetry.IsQubits`, `Sources.P1.qubits`;
  `Symmetry.lean` lists every instance the files take): a geometry that depended on anything else
  would be a quantity the strings do not define.  The laws are the same at every slot (`Symmetry.lawAt_same`), and so is
  the state (`state_same`, `lawAt_const`), so the geometry is too
  (`Symmetry.IsQubits.eq_of_content_eq`): space has constant curvature and expands alike in every
  direction.
* **The vacuum equations and Newton's constant** (`vacuum_without_mass`, `jacobson_G_from_sources`,
  theorems).  The entropy density is a law, the same on every local horizon (`Symmetry.one_density`),
  and not zero.  Jacobson's step at every point (`hcl`, which `Main.jacobson_step` derives from the
  Raychaudhuri equation, the heat that crosses a local horizon and the register's entropy on it)
  gives the field equations up to a multiple of the metric (`Einstein.einstein_up_to_metric`); the first law (`hfirst`) and the contracted
  Bianchi identity (`hbianchi`) make them Einstein's equations with one constant `Λ`
  (`Einstein.einstein_equations`), which without matter are the vacuum equations; with matter at
  rest in a static weak field (`hweak`) Newton's law gives `G = c³k_B/(4ℏη)`
  (`Einstein.G_of_clausius`).
* **The three-sphere itself** (`cosmological_constant_from_sources`, a theorem; the links are in
  `Space.lean`).  Every geodesic of the space at an instant of an observer at rest has a ring along
  it (`hclose`, `hslice`, Postulate 1's first sentence applied to that space), so it closes; with
  the geometry the same at every slot, that space is a space form (`hKH`: Schur's lemma,
  Hopf–Rinow and the Killing–Hopf theorem), with `3K = Λ` by Einstein's constraint (`hcon`), and its rings make it a quotient of the
  three-sphere (`Space.slice_sphere`).  Its rings close with one length, which leaves only the
  three-sphere and its antipodal quotient, and the rings through the observer's cell, drawn in
  space (`hdrawn`, Sec. II's cell and Postulate 2's last sentence with its first clause,
  `Sources.P2.rings_drawn`), exclude the latter: the space is the three-sphere itself, its great
  circles of length `2π√(1/K)` (`Space.sphere_rings`), and `Λ = 3/R_Λ²`
  (`Space.cosmological_constant_of_sources`).  Lean has no Riemannian geometry in which to
  prove the cited theorems the route uses.  The space at an instant is a term `sp` of a type `Sp`,
  and `embedSp` places the space forms among the spaces.  Each cited theorem is a named hypothesis
  that asserts the theorem for these terms (`Sources.Geometry`).

`cosmological_constant_model` shows that the hypotheses of `cosmological_constant_from_sources` can
be met together, in the Fano register with `Bridge.regSix`; those on the entropy density it does
not list, and any constant nonzero `η` meets them, the model's Jacobson relation holding at every
`κ`.

-/

open Horizon Finset Symmetry Quotients

namespace Solution

variable {L : ℕ} {H : Horizon L}
        LemmaSolution.lawAt_eq_ofline 78
        /-- **A quantity that is the same at every crossing has that value at every slot**: its value at a
slot of the space the rings describe, `Symmetry.lawAt`, is its value at any crossing, whatever the
drawing.  `Symmetry.lawAt_eq` is the case of a law, which the two clauses of Postulate 2 make the
same at every crossing (`Symmetry.laws_same`). -/
lemma lawAt_eq_of {Slot W : Type*} (𝒟 : Set (H.Cell → H.Loop → Slot)) (s : H.Cell → H.Loop → W)
    (hs : ∀ l x, x ∈ H.cells l → ∀ l' y, y ∈ H.cells l' → s x l = s y l')
    (σ : described 𝒟) (l : H.Loop) (x : H.Cell) (hx : x ∈ H.cells l) :
    lawAt 𝒟 s σ = s x l := by
  have h := mem_described.1 σ.2
  have hl := Classical.choose_spec h
  have hx' := Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec hl.2)
  exact hs _ _ hx'.1 l x hx
        LemmaSolution.lawAt_constline 91
        /-- **A quantity that is the same at every crossing is the same at every slot** of the space the
rings describe. -/
lemma lawAt_const {Slot W : Type*} (𝒟 : Set (H.Cell → H.Loop → Slot)) (s : H.Cell → H.Loop → W)
    (hs : ∀ l x, x ∈ H.cells l → ∀ l' y, y ∈ H.cells l' → s x l = s y l')
    (σ τ : described 𝒟) : lawAt 𝒟 s σ = lawAt 𝒟 s τ := by
  obtain ⟨-, -, l, x, hx, -⟩ := mem_described.1 τ.2
  rw [lawAt_eq_of 𝒟 s hs σ l x hx, lawAt_eq_of 𝒟 s hs τ l x hx]
        LemmaSolution.described_univline 99
        /-- **Every slot is reached by some drawing**: when every drawing counts, not only the admissible
ones, the space the rings describe is every slot.  The drawing that puts every crossing at one slot
puts some crossing there (`Horizon.two_loops`, `Horizon.loops_meet`). -/
lemma described_univ {Slot : Type*} :
    described (Set.univ : Set (H.Cell → H.Loop → Slot)) = Set.univ := by
  ext σ
  simp only [Set.mem_univ, iff_true]
  obtain ⟨l₀, -, -⟩ := H.two_loops
  obtain ⟨x₀, h₀, -⟩ := H.loops_meet l₀ l₀
  exact ⟨fun _ _ => σ, Set.mem_univ _, l₀, x₀, h₀, rfl⟩
        DefinitionSolution.crossingStateline 110
        /-- **The state seen where ring `l` crosses cell `x`** (Secs. II and IV.A).  Without a mass the
string on ring `l` is in the horizon's thermal state (thermodynamics), and the function `F` of
`hgeom` (`Symmetry.IsQubits`), which gives the geometry, reads that thermal state with the cell's bit as one of the possible outcomes
of a measurement of the string.  So the entries are what every string in that state shares, which
`state_same` proves:

* the thermal state `ρ l` of its qubit, a density matrix on the two outcomes, which are the two
  senses (Sec. II); its diagonal entries are the probabilities of the senses (`Qubit.prob`, the
  Born probabilities of the basis outcomes), so the sense needs no entry of its own;
* the probability `read l x` that a measurement's outcome is the bit of the cell `x`; off the
  ring, where the string has no cell, this entry is `0`;
* the string's correlation with the other strings, `Entropy.correlation Pst l`: the joint
  distribution `Pst` of all the strings' senses, the horizon's thermal state, less the product of
  the string's own distribution and that of the others.  Free strings, whose joint distribution is
  the product of their own (`hfree`, Postulate 1 with thermodynamics), make it zero
  (`Entropy.correlation_jointProb`).

A quantity that is the same for every string, such as the inverse temperature, needs no entry,
since `F` may depend on it directly.  A quantity that varies within the thermal state enters only
through its distribution, which is also the same for every string.  So three things are left
out, each for a reason stated here.

* The string's bits, and so the bit the cell `x` shows, are left out because they are the
  possible outcomes of a measurement of the string, whose probabilities its state `ρ l` gives
  (Postulate 1), not a property of the crossing: half of them are 1s on average
  (`Qubit.half_bits_thermal`).
* The string's position on its ring, which is the qubit's phase (Postulate 1), is left out because
  the thermal state holds no phase: it is half the identity (`Qubit.Tick.state_eq`), since every
  state of a free string has one energy.
* The string's own energy is left out
  because it adds no state: the tick's factor multiplies both states of the string alike (Sec. IV.E,
  `Qubit.Tick.phase_unique`), so its two senses have one energy (`Qubit.Tick.energy_eq`), and the
  thermal state of the string's qubit, the Gibbs state over the two senses (`Qubit.Tick.state`),
  is the same whatever that energy is (`Qubit.Tick.state_eq`).  The
  energy differs from string to string with the mass a string holds (Sec. IV.E; its mean over the
  strings is one thermal energy of the horizon, `Main.string_energy`); `hthermal` of `state_same`
  gives each string the energy of its own tick's factor, `En` of it, whatever the function `En`. -/
noncomputable def crossingState (ρ : H.Loop → Register.Qubit.Op)
    (read : ∀ l : H.Loop, {X // X ∈ H.cells l} → ℝ) (Pst : (H.Loop → Bool) → ℝ) (x : H.Cell)
    (l : H.Loop) : Register.Qubit.Op × ℝ × ((H.Loop → Bool) → ℝ) :=
  (ρ l, if h : x ∈ H.cells l then read l ⟨x, h⟩ else 0, Register.Entropy.correlation Pst l)
        TheoremSolution.state_sameline 152
        /-- **Without a mass the state is the same at every crossing** (Secs. II and IV.A).  Without a mass
every string's qubit is in the thermal state of its tick (`hthermal`); this is where "without a
mass" enters.

* The string's qubit is in the thermal state of its tick `T l` (`hthermal`, `Qubit.Tick.state`,
  thermodynamics).  Its two outcomes are the two senses (Sec. II), which have one energy, since the
  tick's phase changes alike in either sense, no law depending on the direction in which a ring
  passes through a cell (Postulate 2, `hsense` of `Qubit.Tick`): the tick multiplies both by one
  factor, and a string's energy is the energy of its factor (`Qubit.Tick.factor_eq`,
  `Qubit.Tick.energy_eq`); the thermal state, the Gibbs state over the two senses at their
  energies (`Qubit.Tick.state`), is half the identity (`Qubit.Tick.state_eq`):
  each sense has the probability `1/2` (`Qubit.Tick.prob_state`).
* The bits of the string's cells are the possible outcomes of one measurement of the qubit
  (Postulate 1): the outcome is the bit of the cell `x` with the probability `read l x`, each
  cell's bit one possible outcome among the `L` (`halike`).
* Between interactions the strings are free (Sec. II; Postulate 1 says what an interaction is), so
  the horizon's thermal state is the
  product of the strings' own (`hfree`), and no string is correlated with the others
  (`Entropy.correlation_jointProb`).

So the state seen at every crossing, `crossingState`, is `(1/2 · 1, 1/L, 0)`.  Half the bits of a
string in that state are 1s, on average (`Qubit.half_bits_thermal`). -/
theorem state_same [NeZero L] (T : H.Loop → Register.Qubit.Tick L) (β : ℝ) (En : ℂ → ℝ)
    (ρ : H.Loop → Register.Qubit.Op) (hthermal : ∀ l, ρ l = (T l).state β En)
    (read : ∀ l : H.Loop, {X // X ∈ H.cells l} → ℝ) (halike : ∀ l x, read l x = 1 / (L : ℝ))
    (Pst : (H.Loop → Bool) → ℝ) (q : H.Loop → ℝ) (hfree : Pst = Register.Entropy.jointProb q) :
    ∀ l x, x ∈ H.cells l →
      crossingState ρ read Pst x l = ((1 / 2 : ℂ) • (1 : Register.Qubit.Op), 1 / (L : ℝ), 0) := by
  intro l x hx
  have hc : Register.Entropy.correlation Pst l = 0 := by
    funext ω
    rw [hfree]
    exact Register.Entropy.correlation_jointProb q l ω
  simp only [crossingState, hx, ↓reduceDIte, hthermal, (T l).state_eq, halike, hc]
        TheoremSolution.geometry_sameline 187
        /-- **The geometry is the same at every place and in every direction of the space the rings
describe** (Sec. IV.D).  The geometry of space at a slot, `geom`, is the curvature of the plane
normal to the slot's direction and the rate at which that curvature changes.  By Postulate 1's
first sentence applied to it, it is qubits (`hgeom`, `Symmetry.IsQubits`): it is read off the laws
and the state at the slot, as `Symmetry.lawAt` reads them.  The two clauses of Postulate 2 make
every law the same at every slot (`hsym`, `hdir`, `Symmetry.lawAt_same`).  The state is the same at
every crossing (`hs`, which `state_same` gives without a mass), so it is the same at every slot too
(`lawAt_const`).  So the geometry is the same at every slot of `described 𝒟`, the space the rings
describe (`Symmetry.IsQubits.eq_of_content_eq`): space has constant curvature and expands alike in
every direction. -/
theorem geometry_same {Slot V W G : Type*} (𝒟 : Set (H.Cell → H.Loop → Slot))
    (f : H.Cell → H.Loop → V)
    (hsym : ∀ x y : H.Cell, ∃ s : H.Symmetry, s.cellMap x = y ∧
      ∀ l, ∀ z ∈ H.cells l, f (s.cellMap z) (s.loopMap l) = f z l)
    (hdir : ∀ x l l', x ∈ H.cells l → x ∈ H.cells l' → f x l = f x l')
    (s : H.Cell → H.Loop → W)
    (hs : ∀ l x, x ∈ H.cells l → ∀ l' y, y ∈ H.cells l' → s x l = s y l')
    (geom : Slot → G)
    (hgeom : IsQubits (fun σ : described 𝒟 => (lawAt 𝒟 f σ, lawAt 𝒟 s σ))
      fun σ : described 𝒟 => geom σ)
    (σ τ : described 𝒟) : geom σ = geom τ :=
  hgeom.eq_of_content_eq (i := σ) (j := τ)
    (Prod.ext (lawAt_same 𝒟 f hsym hdir σ τ) (lawAt_const 𝒟 s hs σ τ))
        TheoremSolution.geometry_same_slotsline 211
        /-- **The geometry is the same at every slot of the space at an instant** (Sec. IV.D).  The laws are
the same at every crossing by the two clauses of Postulate 2 (`hsym`, `hdir`); the state is the same
at every crossing (`hs`, which `state_same` gives without a mass); and by Postulate 1's first
sentence applied to it the geometry at a slot is qubits, read off the laws and the state there
(`hgeom`, `Symmetry.IsQubits`).  Here every drawing counts, not only the admissible ones
(`Set.univ`), so every slot is reached (`described_univ`).  Which crossing a drawing puts at a slot
does not matter, since the laws and the state are the same at every crossing (`lawAt_eq_of`).  This
is the input of the Killing–Hopf theorem, the geometry the same at every place and in every
direction (`Sources.Geometry.space_form`). -/
theorem geometry_same_slots {Slot V W G : Type*} (f : H.Cell → H.Loop → V)
    (hsym : ∀ x y : H.Cell, ∃ s : H.Symmetry, s.cellMap x = y ∧
      ∀ l, ∀ z ∈ H.cells l, f (s.cellMap z) (s.loopMap l) = f z l)
    (hdir : ∀ x l l', x ∈ H.cells l → x ∈ H.cells l' → f x l = f x l')
    (s : H.Cell → H.Loop → W)
    (hs : ∀ l x, x ∈ H.cells l → ∀ l' y, y ∈ H.cells l' → s x l = s y l')
    (geom : Slot → G)
    (hgeom : IsQubits (fun σ : described (Set.univ : Set (H.Cell → H.Loop → Slot)) =>
      (lawAt Set.univ f σ, lawAt Set.univ s σ)) fun σ => geom σ) :
    ∀ σ τ : Slot, geom σ = geom τ := by
  intro σ τ
  have hσ : σ ∈ described (Set.univ : Set (H.Cell → H.Loop → Slot)) := by
    rw [described_univ]
    trivial
  have hτ : τ ∈ described (Set.univ : Set (H.Cell → H.Loop → Slot)) := by
    rw [described_univ]
    trivial
  exact geometry_same Set.univ f hsym hdir s hs geom hgeom ⟨σ, hσ⟩ ⟨τ, hτ⟩
        LemmaSolution.eta_posline 239
        /-- the count's entropy density is positive -/
lemma eta_pos (R : Register.Reg) : 0 < R.η := by
  have := R.Ahor_pos
  have := R.ln2_pos
  have := R.kB_pos
  have := R.L_pos
  unfold Register.Reg.η Register.Reg.Shor Register.Reg.Rhor
  positivity
        TheoremSolution.vacuum_without_massline 248
        /-- **The vacuum equations, from Jacobson's step and the first law** (Sec. III).  The entropy density
is a law, the same on every local horizon (`Symmetry.one_density`, the two clauses of Postulate 2),
its value at one crossing, whatever that value is: without matter the value does not enter.
Jacobson's step at every point (`hcl`, thermodynamics) gives `R(k,k) = κT(k,k)` for every null
`k`, with `κ = 2πk_B/(ℏcη)`; with the first law (`hfirst`) and the contracted Bianchi identity
(`hbianchi`), Einstein's equations hold with one constant (`Einstein.einstein_equations`).  Without
matter (`hnm`) they are the vacuum equations (`Einstein.vacuum_of_field_equations`), and their
constant is `Λ`, the one that the Ricci tensor shows at a point (`hΛ`). -/
theorem vacuum_without_mass (R : Register.Reg) (η : H.Cell → H.Loop → ℝ)
    (hsymη : ∀ x y : H.Cell, ∃ s : H.Symmetry, s.cellMap x = y ∧
      ∀ l, ∀ z ∈ H.cells l, η (s.cellMap z) (s.loopMap l) = η z l)
    (hdirη : ∀ x l l', x ∈ H.cells l → x ∈ H.cells l' → η x l = η x l')
    {l₀ : H.Loop} {x₀ : H.Cell} (h₀ : x₀ ∈ H.cells l₀) (hη0 : η x₀ l₀ ≠ 0)
    (M : Register.Einstein.Spacetime)
    (hcl : ∀ η₀ : ℝ, η₀ ≠ 0 → (∀ l x, x ∈ H.cells l → η x l = η₀) → ∀ p k,
      Register.Einstein.IsNull k → Register.Einstein.quad (M.ric p) k =
        (2 * R.pi * R.kB / (R.ℏ * R.c * η₀)) * Register.Einstein.quad (M.stress p) k)
    (hfirst : ∀ p u, Register.Einstein.IsTimelike u → dotProduct (M.divStress p) u = 0)
    (hbianchi : ∀ (κ : ℝ) (φ : M.Pt → ℝ),
      (∀ p, M.ric p - κ • Register.Einstein.symmPart (M.stress p) = φ p • Register.Einstein.eta) →
      (∀ p, M.divStress p = 0) →
      ∀ p q, φ p + κ / 2 * Register.Einstein.trace (Register.Einstein.symmPart (M.stress p)) =
        φ q + κ / 2 * Register.Einstein.trace (Register.Einstein.symmPart (M.stress q)))
    (hnm : ∀ p, M.stress p = 0) (Λ : ℝ) (hΛ : ∃ p, M.ric p = Λ • Register.Einstein.eta) :
    Register.Einstein.VacuumEinstein M Set.univ Λ := by
  have hη := one_density η hsymη hdirη h₀ (η x₀ l₀) rfl
  obtain ⟨Λ', hE⟩ := Register.Einstein.einstein_equations M _ (hcl _ hη0 hη) hfirst (hbianchi _)
  have hV := Register.Einstein.vacuum_of_field_equations M _ Λ' hE Set.univ fun p _ => hnm p
  obtain ⟨p₀, hp₀⟩ := hΛ
  have e : Λ' = Λ := by
    have h1 := hV p₀ trivial
    rw [hp₀] at h1
    have h00 := congrArg (fun A : Matrix (Fin 4) (Fin 4) ℝ => A 0 0) h1
    simp [Register.Einstein.eta, Matrix.diagonal] at h00
    linarith
  rw [← e]
  exact hV
        TheoremSolution.jacobson_G_from_sourcesline 286
        /-- **Newton's constant from Jacobson's step, without the conservation law** (Sec. III):
`G = c³k_B/(4ℏη₀)`.  The entropy density is one law, `η₀` on every local horizon (`one_density`);
the count gives its value, at leading order in `1/L` (`Main.jacobson_G`) or exactly
(`Main.jacobson_G_exact`).
Jacobson's step (`hcl`) gives Einstein's equations up to a multiple of the metric
(`Einstein.einstein_up_to_metric`), and with them the static weak field of matter at rest at the
point `p` has the Ricci tensor `A = ∇²Φ/c²` times the identity (`hweak`, Lorentzian geometry).
There the stress tensor is `diag(ρc², 0, 0, 0)` (`hdust`), and Newton's law `∇²Φ = 4πGρ` defines
`G` (`hN`); the null vector `(1, 1, 0, 0)` gives `κ = 8πG/c⁴` (`Einstein.G_of_clausius`). -/
theorem jacobson_G_from_sources (R : Register.Reg) (G : ℝ) (η : H.Cell → H.Loop → ℝ)
    (hsymη : ∀ x y : H.Cell, ∃ s : H.Symmetry, s.cellMap x = y ∧
      ∀ l, ∀ z ∈ H.cells l, η (s.cellMap z) (s.loopMap l) = η z l)
    (hdirη : ∀ x l l', x ∈ H.cells l → x ∈ H.cells l' → η x l = η x l')
    {l₀ : H.Loop} {x₀ : H.Cell} (h₀ : x₀ ∈ H.cells l₀) (η₀ : ℝ) (hη₀ : η₀ ≠ 0)
    (hcount : η x₀ l₀ = η₀)
    (M : Register.Einstein.Spacetime)
    (hcl : ∀ η₀ : ℝ, η₀ ≠ 0 → (∀ l x, x ∈ H.cells l → η x l = η₀) → ∀ p k,
      Register.Einstein.IsNull k → Register.Einstein.quad (M.ric p) k =
        (2 * R.pi * R.kB / (R.ℏ * R.c * η₀)) * Register.Einstein.quad (M.stress p) k)
    (p : M.Pt) (A ρ : ℝ)
    (hweak : ∀ κ : ℝ, Register.Einstein.TraceFree M κ →
      M.ric p = A • (1 : Matrix (Fin 4) (Fin 4) ℝ))
    (hρ : ρ ≠ 0) (hdust : M.stress p = Matrix.diagonal ![ρ * R.c ^ 2, 0, 0, 0])
    (hN : A = 4 * R.pi * G * ρ / R.c ^ 2) :
    G = R.c ^ 3 * R.kB / (4 * R.ℏ * η₀) := by
  have hη := one_density η hsymη hdirη h₀ η₀ hcount
  have h := hcl η₀ hη₀ hη
  have hR := hweak _ (Register.Einstein.einstein_up_to_metric M _ h)
  exact Register.Einstein.G_of_clausius hη₀ R.ℏ_pos.ne' R.c_pos.ne' hρ hR hdust (h p) hN
        TheoremSolution.cosmological_constant_from_sourcesline 316
        /-- **The cosmological constant, from the sources** (Sec. IV.D), every link named; the route of
`Space.cosmological_constant_of_sources`, with its first inputs derived here.

* The geometry of the space at an instant is the same at every slot (`geometry_same_slots`, from
  the two clauses of Postulate 2, the state without a mass, `state_same`, and Postulate 1's first
  sentence applied to the geometry, `hgeom`).
* Every geodesic of that space has a ring along it (`hclose`, Postulate 1's first sentence applied
  to the space at an instant), so it closes; with the geometry the same everywhere, Schur's lemma,
  Hopf–Rinow and the Killing–Hopf theorem make the space a space form (`hKH`, Riemannian geometry).
* The vacuum equations hold without a mass (`vacuum_without_mass`: Jacobson's step `hcl`, the first
  law `hfirst`, the contracted Bianchi identity `hbianchi`, no matter `hnm`, and `Λ` the vacuum's
  constant `hΛ`), and Einstein's constraint on the slice gives `3K = Λ` (`hcon`).
* The slice's rings make the form the sphere (`hslice`), and with the rings through the
  observer's cell `x₀` drawn in it (`hdrawn`, Sec. II's cell and Postulate 2's last sentence with
  its first clause) they make its group trivial (`Space.sphere_rings`).

Then `Λ = 3/R_Λ²`.  The drawn rings close with `Lℓ_c` and every great circle with `R.L ℓ_c`, so
`hdrawn` and `hslice` together give `L = R.L`; where that fails they cannot both hold. -/
theorem cosmological_constant_from_sources {Slot V Gm Sp : Type*} (R : Register.Reg) {Λ : ℝ}
    (P : H.Positions) (f : H.Cell → H.Loop → V)
    (hsym : ∀ x y : H.Cell, ∃ s : H.Symmetry, s.cellMap x = y ∧
      ∀ l, ∀ z ∈ H.cells l, f (s.cellMap z) (s.loopMap l) = f z l)
    (hdir : ∀ x l l', x ∈ H.cells l → x ∈ H.cells l' → f x l = f x l')
    [NeZero L] (T : H.Loop → Register.Qubit.Tick L) (β : ℝ) (En : ℂ → ℝ) (ρ : H.Loop → Register.Qubit.Op)
    (hthermal : ∀ l, ρ l = (T l).state β En)
    (Pst : (H.Loop → Bool) → ℝ) (q : H.Loop → ℝ) (hfree : Pst = Register.Entropy.jointProb q)
    (read : ∀ l : H.Loop, {X // X ∈ H.cells l} → ℝ) (halike : ∀ l x, read l x = 1 / (L : ℝ))
    (geom : Slot → Gm)
    (hgeom : IsQubits (fun σ : described (Set.univ : Set (H.Cell → H.Loop → Slot)) =>
      (lawAt Set.univ f σ, lawAt Set.univ (crossingState ρ read Pst) σ)) fun σ => geom σ)
    (Closes : Slot → Prop) (hclose : ringsAlong H Set.univ Closes)
    (sp : Sp) (embedSp : (K : ℝ) → Space.SpaceForm K → Sp)
    (hKH : (∀ σ τ : Slot, geom σ = geom τ) → (∀ σ, Closes σ) →
      ∃ K, ∃ c : Space.SpaceForm K, sp = embedSp K c)
    (η : H.Cell → H.Loop → ℝ)
    (hsymη : ∀ x y : H.Cell, ∃ s : H.Symmetry, s.cellMap x = y ∧
      ∀ l, ∀ z ∈ H.cells l, η (s.cellMap z) (s.loopMap l) = η z l)
    (hdirη : ∀ x l l', x ∈ H.cells l → x ∈ H.cells l' → η x l = η x l')
    {l₀ : H.Loop} {x₀ : H.Cell} (h₀ : x₀ ∈ H.cells l₀) (hη0 : η x₀ l₀ ≠ 0)
    (M : Register.Einstein.Spacetime)
    (hcl : ∀ η₀ : ℝ, η₀ ≠ 0 → (∀ l x, x ∈ H.cells l → η x l = η₀) → ∀ p k,
      Register.Einstein.IsNull k → Register.Einstein.quad (M.ric p) k =
        (2 * R.pi * R.kB / (R.ℏ * R.c * η₀)) * Register.Einstein.quad (M.stress p) k)
    (hfirst : ∀ p u, Register.Einstein.IsTimelike u → dotProduct (M.divStress p) u = 0)
    (hbianchi : ∀ (κ : ℝ) (φ : M.Pt → ℝ),
      (∀ p, M.ric p - κ • Register.Einstein.symmPart (M.stress p) = φ p • Register.Einstein.eta) →
      (∀ p, M.divStress p = 0) →
      ∀ p q, φ p + κ / 2 * Register.Einstein.trace (Register.Einstein.symmPart (M.stress p)) =
        φ q + κ / 2 * Register.Einstein.trace (Register.Einstein.symmPart (M.stress q)))
    (hnm : ∀ p, M.stress p = 0) (hΛ : ∃ p, M.ric p = Λ • Register.Einstein.eta)
    (hcon : Register.Einstein.VacuumEinstein M Set.univ Λ →
      ∀ K (c : Space.SpaceForm K), sp = embedSp K c → 3 * K = Λ)
    (hslice : ∀ K (c : Space.SpaceForm K), sp = embedSp K c →
      Space.SliceIsQubits H (R.L * R.ℓc) c)
    (hdrawn : ∀ K Γ (hK : 0 < K) (hΓ : Space.SphereQuotient (1 / K) Γ),
      sp = embedSp K (Space.SpaceForm.sphere Γ hK hΓ) → Space.RingsDrawn H P (1 / K) Γ R.ℓc x₀) :
    Λ = 3 / R.RL ^ 2 := by
  have hstate := state_same T β En ρ hthermal read halike Pst q hfree
  have hs : ∀ l x, x ∈ H.cells l → ∀ l' y, y ∈ H.cells l' →
      crossingState ρ read Pst x l = crossingState ρ read Pst y l' :=
    fun l x hx l' y hy => (hstate l x hx).trans (hstate l' y hy).symm
  have hsame := geometry_same_slots f hsym hdir _ hs geom hgeom
  have hvac := vacuum_without_mass R η hsymη hdirη h₀ hη0 M hcl hfirst hbianchi hnm Λ hΛ
  exact Space.cosmological_constant_of_sources H P x₀ R geom hsame Closes hclose sp embedSp hKH M
    hvac hcon hslice hdrawn
        TheoremSolution.chain_from_sourcesline 382
        /-- **Newton's constant, the cosmological constant, the horizon's temperature and the vacuum's
energy, from the sources** (Secs. III and IV.D).  The theorems of the chain keep three hypotheses
for brevity, and this theorem derives each from the sources and applies it.

* The horizon at `R_Λ` (`hdS`): `Λ = 3/R_Λ²` (`cosmological_constant_from_sources`), so the de
  Sitter solution's `f` vanishes at `R_Λ` (`Reg.deSitter`).
* Newton's constant (`hJ`): Jacobson's step without the conservation law, with Newton's law in the
  static weak field (`jacobson_G_from_sources`), at the count's density to leading order in `1/L`
  on the horizon of the solution without a mass (`hcount`), whose radius `rh` (`hrh`) the first
  link puts at `R_Λ` (`Reg.horizon_radius_eq`).
* The horizon's temperature in cells (`I1` in the form of the lap): a horizon is thermal with
  `k_BT = ℏ/τ`, `τ` the Gibbons–Hawking period `2πc/a` for its surface gravity `a` (`I1`,
  thermodynamics), taken at the horizon of the solution without a mass, `a = −g(r_h)`; the first
  link makes that surface gravity `a_Λ` (`Reg.surface_gravity_eq`) and the period the lap time
  `Lt_c` (`Reg.horizon_period`).

Then `G = c³ℓ_c²/(πℏ ln 2)`, `Λ = 3/R_Λ²`, `GΛ = 12πc³/(ℏL² ln 2)`, `k_BT = E_c/L`, and the
horizon's heat, its temperature times the entropy of its thermal state, is the vacuum's energy `E_Λ`
to relative order `2/L` (`Cosmo.vacuum_energy`, with the free strings `hfree` and the senses'
probabilities read off the strings' thermal states, `hq`). -/
theorem chain_from_sources {Slot V Gm Sp : Type*} (R : Register.Reg) {Λ : ℝ}
    (P : H.Positions) (f : H.Cell → H.Loop → V)
    (hsym : ∀ x y : H.Cell, ∃ s : H.Symmetry, s.cellMap x = y ∧
      ∀ l, ∀ z ∈ H.cells l, f (s.cellMap z) (s.loopMap l) = f z l)
    (hdir : ∀ x l l', x ∈ H.cells l → x ∈ H.cells l' → f x l = f x l')
    [NeZero L] (T : H.Loop → Register.Qubit.Tick L) (β : ℝ) (En : ℂ → ℝ) (ρ : H.Loop → Register.Qubit.Op)
    (hthermal : ∀ l, ρ l = (T l).state β En)
    (Pst : (H.Loop → Bool) → ℝ) (q : H.Loop → ℝ) (hfree : Pst = Register.Entropy.jointProb q)
    (read : ∀ l : H.Loop, {X // X ∈ H.cells l} → ℝ) (halike : ∀ l x, read l x = 1 / (L : ℝ))
    (geom : Slot → Gm)
    (hgeom : IsQubits (fun σ : described (Set.univ : Set (H.Cell → H.Loop → Slot)) =>
      (lawAt Set.univ f σ, lawAt Set.univ (crossingState ρ read Pst) σ)) fun σ => geom σ)
    (Closes : Slot → Prop) (hclose : ringsAlong H Set.univ Closes)
    (sp : Sp) (embedSp : (K : ℝ) → Space.SpaceForm K → Sp)
    (hKH : (∀ σ τ : Slot, geom σ = geom τ) → (∀ σ, Closes σ) →
      ∃ K, ∃ c : Space.SpaceForm K, sp = embedSp K c)
    (η : H.Cell → H.Loop → ℝ)
    (hsymη : ∀ x y : H.Cell, ∃ s : H.Symmetry, s.cellMap x = y ∧
      ∀ l, ∀ z ∈ H.cells l, η (s.cellMap z) (s.loopMap l) = η z l)
    (hdirη : ∀ x l l', x ∈ H.cells l → x ∈ H.cells l' → η x l = η x l')
    {l₀ : H.Loop} {x₀ : H.Cell} (h₀ : x₀ ∈ H.cells l₀) (rh : ℝ)
    (hcount : η x₀ l₀ = R.kB * (R.Rhor * R.ln2) / (4 * R.pi * rh ^ 2))
    (M : Register.Einstein.Spacetime)
    (hcl : ∀ η₀ : ℝ, η₀ ≠ 0 → (∀ l x, x ∈ H.cells l → η x l = η₀) → ∀ p k,
      Register.Einstein.IsNull k → Register.Einstein.quad (M.ric p) k =
        (2 * R.pi * R.kB / (R.ℏ * R.c * η₀)) * Register.Einstein.quad (M.stress p) k)
    (hfirst : ∀ p u, Register.Einstein.IsTimelike u → dotProduct (M.divStress p) u = 0)
    (hbianchi : ∀ (κ : ℝ) (φ : M.Pt → ℝ),
      (∀ p, M.ric p - κ • Register.Einstein.symmPart (M.stress p) = φ p • Register.Einstein.eta) →
      (∀ p, M.divStress p = 0) →
      ∀ p q, φ p + κ / 2 * Register.Einstein.trace (Register.Einstein.symmPart (M.stress p)) =
        φ q + κ / 2 * Register.Einstein.trace (Register.Einstein.symmPart (M.stress q)))
    (hnm : ∀ p, M.stress p = 0) (hΛ : ∃ p, M.ric p = Λ • Register.Einstein.eta)
    (hcon : Register.Einstein.VacuumEinstein M Set.univ Λ →
      ∀ K (c : Space.SpaceForm K), sp = embedSp K c → 3 * K = Λ)
    (hslice : ∀ K (c : Space.SpaceForm K), sp = embedSp K c →
      Space.SliceIsQubits H (R.L * R.ℓc) c)
    (hdrawn : ∀ K Γ (hK : 0 < K) (hΓ : Space.SphereQuotient (1 / K) Γ),
      sp = embedSp K (Space.SpaceForm.sphere Γ hK hΓ) → Space.RingsDrawn H P (1 / K) Γ R.ℓc x₀)
    (G : ℝ) (Mw : Register.Einstein.Spacetime)
    (hclw : ∀ η₀ : ℝ, η₀ ≠ 0 → (∀ l x, x ∈ H.cells l → η x l = η₀) → ∀ p k,
      Register.Einstein.IsNull k → Register.Einstein.quad (Mw.ric p) k =
        (2 * R.pi * R.kB / (R.ℏ * R.c * η₀)) * Register.Einstein.quad (Mw.stress p) k)
    (pw : Mw.Pt) (A ρw : ℝ)
    (hweak : ∀ κ : ℝ, Register.Einstein.TraceFree Mw κ →
      Mw.ric pw = A • (1 : Matrix (Fin 4) (Fin 4) ℝ))
    (hρw : ρw ≠ 0) (hdust : Mw.stress pw = Matrix.diagonal ![ρw * R.c ^ 2, 0, 0, 0])
    (hN : A = 4 * R.pi * G * ρw / R.c ^ 2) (hrh : 0 < rh ∧ R.fSdS G 0 Λ rh = 0)
    (Temp : ℝ) (I1 : R.kB * Temp = R.ℏ / (R.La (-R.gSdS G 0 Λ rh) * R.tc))
    (hL : 4 ≤ L) (hRL : R.L = L)
    (hq : ∀ l, q l = Register.Qubit.prob ((T l).state β En) 0) :
    Λ = 3 / R.RL ^ 2 ∧ G = R.c ^ 3 * R.ℓc ^ 2 / (R.pi * R.ℏ * R.ln2) ∧
    G * Λ = 12 * R.pi * R.c ^ 3 / (R.ℏ * R.L ^ 2 * R.ln2) ∧
    R.kB * Temp = R.Ec / R.L ∧
    R.kB * Temp * Register.Bridge.horizonEntropy H Pst = R.EΛ * (1 - 2 / R.L + 4 / R.L ^ 2) := by
  -- the count's density on the horizon is not zero
  have hη0 : η x₀ l₀ ≠ 0 := by
    rw [hcount]
    have := hrh.1; have := R.kB_pos; have := R.ln2_pos; have := R.pi_pos; have := R.L_pos
    unfold Register.Reg.Rhor
    positivity
  have hΛ' := cosmological_constant_from_sources R P f hsym hdir T β En ρ hthermal Pst q hfree
    read halike geom hgeom Closes hclose sp embedSp hKH η hsymη hdirη h₀ hη0 M hcl hfirst hbianchi
    hnm hΛ hcon hslice hdrawn
  have hdS := (R.deSitter G Λ).2 hΛ'
  -- the horizon of the solution without a mass is at `R_Λ`, so the count's density there is `η`
  have hr := R.horizon_radius_eq G Λ rh hdS hrh.1 hrh.2
  have hη : η x₀ l₀ = R.η := by rw [hcount, hr]; rfl
  have hJ := jacobson_G_from_sources R G η hsymη hdirη h₀ R.η (eta_pos R).ne' hη Mw hclw pw
    A ρw hweak hρw hdust hN
  -- the horizon's surface gravity, `−g(r_h)`, is `a_Λ`
  rw [R.surface_gravity_eq G Λ rh hdS hrh.1 hrh.2] at I1
  have hT := (R.horizon_temperature G Λ Temp hdS I1).2.1
  have hlap : R.kB * Temp = R.ℏ / (R.L * R.tc) := by
    rw [hT]
    unfold Register.Reg.tc Register.Reg.Ec
    have := R.c_pos; have := R.ℓc_pos; have := R.L_pos
    field_simp
  exact ⟨hΛ', (R.G_eq G hJ).1, (R.G_Lambda G Λ hJ hdS).1, hT,
    R.vacuum_energy H hL hRL Temp hlap T β En Pst q hfree hq⟩

        
/-! ### The hypotheses of the route can be met together -/

section Model

open Geodesic RealInnerProductSpace

        /-- the Fano register's rings, with their decidable equality and finiteness in view for `decide` -/
instance : DecidableEq Horizon.fano.Loop := inferInstanceAs (DecidableEq (Fin 7))

        LemmaSolution.sphereQuotient_botline 494
        /-- the trivial group is a quotient of the three-sphere -/
lemma sphereQuotient_bot (k : ℝ) :
    Space.SphereQuotient k
      (⊥ : Subgroup ((ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)))) where
  iso g hg x y := by rw [Subgroup.mem_bot] at hg; subst hg; rfl
  time g hg x := by rw [Subgroup.mem_bot] at hg; subst hg; rfl
  free g hg _ _ _ := Subgroup.mem_bot.1 hg
  finite := by
    rw [Subgroup.coe_bot]
    exact Set.finite_singleton 1
        DefinitionSolution.vacuumSpacetimeline 505
        /-- **A spacetime without matter in which the vacuum equations hold with `Λ`**, of one point. -/
noncomputable def vacuumSpacetime (Λ : ℝ) : Register.Einstein.Spacetime where
  Pt := Unit
  ric _ := Λ • Register.Einstein.eta
  stress _ := 0
  divStress _ := 0
  ric_symm _ := by
    unfold Matrix.IsSymm Register.Einstein.eta
    rw [Matrix.transpose_smul, Matrix.diagonal_transpose]
        LemmaSolution.vacuumSpacetime_clausiusline 515
        /-- in the vacuum spacetime both sides of Jacobson's relation vanish on every null vector -/
lemma vacuumSpacetime_clausius (Λ κ : ℝ) (p : (vacuumSpacetime Λ).Pt) (k : Fin 4 → ℝ)
    (hk : Register.Einstein.IsNull k) :
    Register.Einstein.quad ((vacuumSpacetime Λ).ric p) k =
      κ * Register.Einstein.quad ((vacuumSpacetime Λ).stress p) k := by
  show Register.Einstein.quad (Λ • Register.Einstein.eta) k = κ * Register.Einstein.quad 0 k
  rw [Register.Einstein.quad_smul, show Register.Einstein.quad Register.Einstein.eta k = 0 from hk]
  simp [Register.Einstein.quad]
        LemmaSolution.closes_deSitterline 524
        /-- every spacelike geodesic of de Sitter space of radius `R_Λ` closes in the trivial quotient
with the length `Lℓ_c` (`Geodesic.IsGeodesic.hasLength`, `Quotients.closesIn_bot`) -/
lemma closes_deSitter (R : Register.Reg) {γ : Curve ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4))}
    (hg : IsGeodesic (R.RL ^ 2) γ) (hsp : IsSpacelike γ) :
    ClosesIn ((⊥ : Subgroup ((ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) ≃ₗ[ℝ]
      (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)))) : Set ((ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) ≃ₗ[ℝ]
        (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)))) γ.pos (speed γ) (R.L * R.ℓc) := by
  have hRL := R.RL_pos
  have h := hg.hasLength (by positivity) hsp
  rw [Real.sqrt_sq hRL.le] at h
  have e : 2 * Real.pi * R.RL = R.L * R.ℓc := by
    have := R.pi_pos
    unfold Register.Reg.RL
    rw [R.pi_def]
    field_simp
  rw [e] at h
  exact closesIn_bot.2 h

lemma fano_shared (l l' : Fin 7) (hne : l ≠ l')

    (hl' : ((0 : Fin 7), false) ∈ Horizon.fanoLines l' ×ˢ (univ : Finset Bool)) (X : Fin 7 × Bool)
    (hX : X ∈ Horizon.fanoLines l ×ˢ (univ : Finset Bool))
    (hX' : X ∈ Horizon.fanoLines l' ×ˢ (univ : Finset Bool)) :
    X = ((0 : Fin 7), false) ∨ X = ((0 : Fin 7), true) := by
  revert l l' X; decide

  if Fin.val l = 0 then 1 else if Fin.val l = 4 then 2 else 3

        /-- the place of the cell `X` of the model's ring `l`: the point of its great circle at the angle

        LemmaSolution.modelPlace_innerline 609
        /-- the component along `e_m` of a point of the model's ring `l` at the angle `θ` -/
lemma modelPlace_inner (l : Horizon.fano.Loop) (θ : ℝ) (m : Fin 4) :
    ⟪Register.Bridge.regSix.RL • (Real.cos θ • e4 0 + Real.sin θ • e4 (fanoDir l)), e4 m⟫ =
      Register.Bridge.regSix.RL * (Real.cos θ * (if (0 : Fin 4) = m then 1 else 0) +
        Real.sin θ * (if fanoDir l = m then 1 else 0)) := by
  rw [real_inner_smul_left, inner_add_left, real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_left, e4_inner,
    e4_inner]
        LemmaSolution.eq_of_cos_sin_eqline 617
        /-- two angles in `[0, 2π)` with the same cosine and sine are one angle -/
lemma eq_of_cos_sin_eq {x y : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Ico 0 (2 * Real.pi))
    (hy : y ∈ Set.Ico 0 (2 * Real.pi)) (hc : Real.cos x = Real.cos y)
    (hs : Real.sin x = Real.sin y) : x = y := by
  have h1 : Real.cos (x - y) = 1 := by
    rw [Real.cos_sub, hc, hs, ← sq, ← sq, Real.cos_sq_add_sin_sq]
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := (Real.cos_eq_one_iff _).1 h1
  have hpi := Real.pi_pos
  have h2 : (n : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi) < 1 * (2 * Real.pi) := by
    rw [hn]; linarith [hx.1, hx.2, hy.1, hy.2]
  have h3 : (-1 : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi) < (n : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi) := by
    rw [hn]; linarith [hx.1, hx.2, hy.1, hy.2]
  have hn1 : (n : ℝ) < 1 := lt_of_mul_lt_mul_right h2 (by positivity)
  have hn2 : (-1 : ℝ) < n := lt_of_mul_lt_mul_right h3 (by positivity)
  have hn0 : n = 0 := by
    have : n < 1 := by exact_mod_cast hn1
    have : -1 < n := by exact_mod_cast hn2
    omega
  rw [hn0] at hn
  simp only [Int.cast_zero, zero_mul] at hn
  linarith
        LemmaSolution.sin_mul_pi_div_three_eq_zeroline 639
        /-- `sin(jπ/3) = 0` with `j < 6` only for `j = 0` or `j = 3` -/
lemma sin_mul_pi_div_three_eq_zero {j : ℕ} (hj : j < 6)
    (h : Real.sin ((j : ℝ) * (Real.pi / 3)) = 0) : j = 0 ∨ j = 3 := by
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := Real.sin_eq_zero_iff.1 h
  have h3 : ((3 * n : ℤ) : ℝ) * Real.pi = (j : ℝ) * Real.pi := by
    push_cast
    linear_combination 3 * hn
  have h3' : ((3 * n : ℤ) : ℝ) = (j : ℝ) := mul_right_cancel₀ Real.pi_ne_zero h3
  have h3'' : 3 * n = (j : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast h3'
  omega

lemma angle_mem_Ico {j : ℕ} (hj : j < 6) : (j : ℝ) * (Real.pi / 3) ∈ Set.Ico 0 (2 * Real.pi) := by
  have hpi := Real.pi_pos
